name: Bankability Standard
description: A standard for investment due diligence built on claims that can be disproved. It says what a deal folder holds and what must be known.

stages.title: Lead
stages.purpose: Capture and log new investment opportunities from all sourcing channels.

stages.title: Screening
stages.purpose: Assess whether the opportunity fits the investor's mandate, sector focus, and risk appetite.

stages.title: Concept note
stages.purpose: Produce a structured summary of the opportunity for internal review and go/no-go decision.

stages.title: Due diligence
stages.purpose: Conduct comprehensive investigation across all activated workstreams to verify claims and assess risks.

stages.title: Approval
stages.purpose: Compile findings into a formal investment recommendation for the approval committee.

stages.title: Legal documentation
stages.purpose: Complete legal due diligence and draft transaction documents including conditions precedent.

stages.title: Disbursement
stages.purpose: Verify all conditions precedent are met and execute the initial disbursement.

stages.title: Monitoring
stages.purpose: Track ongoing compliance, financial performance, and covenant adherence post-investment.

stages.title: Exit
stages.purpose: Manage loan repayment, equity exit, or portfolio wind-down and capture lessons learned.

subject_kinds.title: Party
subject_kinds.description: A company or a public body.

subject_kinds.title: Person
subject_kinds.description: A natural person. A person is asked only what fits a person.

subject_kinds.title: Facility
subject_kinds.description: A loan under review, a guarantee facility or another financing that the lender considers. Debt that already exists is not a facility. It is a `lends_to` link.

subject_kinds.title: Contract
subject_kinds.description: A contract that matters for repayment.

subject_kinds.title: Asset
subject_kinds.description: A plant, a site, a property or another asset.

subject_kinds.title: Project
subject_kinds.description: A project that is financed or built.

subject_kinds.title: Group
subject_kinds.description: Parties that report or are treated together, such as a consolidated group. A group is the perimeter whose business and money are examined. It is not asked what is asked of a legal entity.

link_types.title: Borrows under
link_types.description: The party borrows under the facility.

link_types.title: Relies on
link_types.description: Repayment of the facility relies on the cash flow of this party or group, whether or not it is the borrower.

link_types.title: Guarantees
link_types.description: The party guarantees the facility. A guarantee of debt that already exists is a fact about that debt's `lends_to` link.

link_types.title: Sponsors
link_types.description: The party stands behind the borrower, or behind the project the loan pays for, as its main shareholder or promoter. Who is behind another project of the business is recorded with `owns`.

link_types.title: Owns
link_types.description: The party owns shares in another party, or owns an asset or a project. It makes its holder a shareholder, and is asked the checks on an owner, only where it points at a party or a group.

link_types.title: Controls
link_types.description: The party controls another party without owning it, for example through voting rights or management.

link_types.title: Is a member of
link_types.description: The party belongs to a group.

link_types.title: Supplies to
link_types.description: The party supplies goods or services to another party.

link_types.title: Sells to
link_types.description: The party sells to another party.

link_types.title: Lends to
link_types.description: The party lends to another party, including loans within a group. Debt that already exists is recorded this way, with its terms, its security and its guarantors as facts about the link.

link_types.title: Operates
link_types.description: The party operates an asset or a project that belongs to someone else, under a contract. A company that runs its own plant needs no such link.

link_types.title: Builds
link_types.description: The party builds an asset or a project for someone else, under a contract.

link_types.title: Is a party to
link_types.description: The party is a party to a contract.

link_types.title: Is security for
link_types.description: The asset is security for the facility.

link_types.title: Ranks behind
link_types.description: The facility ranks behind another facility.

link_types.title: Is part of
link_types.description: One thing is part of another, such as a tranche of a facility or an asset of a project.

link_types.title: Gives support to
link_types.description: The party has given a support undertaking that is not a guarantee. Like a guarantor, it is examined for whether it can and must stand behind the loan.

link_types.title: Supports completion of
link_types.description: The party supports the completion of a project or the facility that finances it. Like a guarantor, it is examined for whether it can and must stand behind that promise.

link_types.title: Pays for
link_types.description: The facility pays for a project or an asset. The link runs from the facility to what it pays for.

link_types.title: Supports within a portfolio
link_types.description: One project or party supports another, for example through a cash sweep or shared reserves.

link_types.title: Other link
link_types.description: Any other link. Say what it is in the reason.

indicators.title: Who is in the deal
indicators.claim: Every party, asset and contract that repayment depends on is in the structure, and the borrower is the kind of party it is said to be.

matters_more_when.reason: In a group, the cash, the assets and the obligations can sit in a company other than the borrower
A project stands on its contracts and on the parties behind them

look_again_when.reason: A new structure chart can show parties that were not in the deal before
A new term sheet can change who borrows, who supports and what is given as security
The parties can still change, so the structure has to be read again when they are fixed

checks.question: What kind of party is the borrower: a company that runs a business itself, a holding company that owns other companies, a vehicle set up for one project or asset, or a fund?
checks.why: The kind of party says where the cash is earned and what stands between that cash and the lender.
checks.ask: Is the borrower a company that runs the business itself, a holding company, a company set up only for this project or asset, or a fund?
checks.if_unknown: Until the kind of borrower is known, nobody can say where the cash that repays the loan is earned.
checks.note: Where there are several borrowers and they are of different kinds, record the answer for each of them.

leads_to.reason: A holding company depends on what the companies below it are able and allowed to pay up

checks.question: Is the borrower part of a larger group, with a parent, subsidiaries or sister companies under the same owners?
checks.why: In a group, money and obligations move between companies. The companies that matter for repayment have to be in the structure.
checks.ask: Does the borrower have a parent company, subsidiaries or sister companies? A group chart would answer this.
checks.if_unknown: Without the group, the lender does not know which other companies can take cash out of the borrower or bring obligations to it.

leads_to.reason: Whether the group would support the borrower, and whether it can take cash out, is examined there
Companies of one group deal with each other, and not always at market terms

checks.question: Which parties, projects, assets, facilities and contracts are part of the proposed deal?
checks.why: The answer is entered as the structure, with each party, asset and contract as a subject and each relation between them as a link. The checks follow from the structure.
checks.ask: Could you describe the deal in outline? Who borrows, which projects or assets are financed, which facilities are planned and which contracts matter. A structure chart or a term sheet is enough at this stage.
checks.if_unknown: Without the structure, the checks cannot be put to the right parties.

checks.question: Does any party support another party or the loan, through a guarantee, a support undertaking, completion support or cash shared between projects (a cash sweep, shared reserves)?
checks.why: Each support is a link with its own checks. It has to be in the structure before it can be relied on.
checks.ask: Does any party stand behind another in this deal, for example with a guarantee, an undertaking to complete the project, a cash sweep or shared reserves? If so, who supports whom?
checks.if_unknown: A support that is not in the structure is not examined, and may be counted on without reason.

leads_to.reason: Support for completion ends at a defined event, and that event has to be examined
Cash shared between projects ties the fate of one to the others

checks.question: Does repayment depend on one contract or a few contracts (for example a sales or offtake contract, a concession, a lease or a supply contract), so that the loss of one of them would put debt service in doubt?
checks.why: Such a contract, and the party on the other side of it, belong in the structure and are examined on their own.
checks.ask: Is there a contract that the business could not service its debt without? For example with a main customer, a public authority, a landlord or a main supplier.

leads_to.reason: The terms of each such contract decide whether the cash flow can be counted on
A sales contract is worth what the customer is able to pay

checks.question: Could the borrower, or another party that repayment relies on, still change before signing (a company that is yet to be set up, a guarantor or a buyer that is not yet chosen, a group that is being reorganised)?
checks.why: A party that is not yet decided is entered in the structure without a name. The checks follow the role, so they wait for whoever takes it, and nothing is lost when the party changes.
checks.ask: Is it settled which company will borrow and who else will stand behind the loan, or could that still change before signing?

checks.question: Do the borrower's own accounts show that it carries on the business itself, with its own employees and with operating assets that it owns or leases?
checks.assumption: The borrower carries on the business itself, with its own staff and assets
checks.ask: Does the borrower itself employ the people and hold the plant, premises and equipment of the business, or are they in another company of the group?
checks.note: Read the borrower's own accounts, not the consolidated accounts of its group. Staff costs and fixed assets are in the notes. Where the staff or the assets sit in another company, that company is what the business runs on.

checks.question: Is there a party that the cash passes through on its way to the borrower or to the lender, or that could stop it, and that the client has not mentioned (for example a holding company, a collection agent, a marketing or trading company, or the owner of the site or of a licence)?
checks.assumption: Every party that the cash passes through, or that could stop it, has been named and is in the structure
checks.note: Follow the money. Who invoices the customer, into whose account does the customer pay, and who owns the site, the licences and the brand? This check does not hang on what the client has said. If the search finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when.

indicators.title: The request
indicators.claim: The lender can provide what is asked for, the money goes to a use that can be checked and not to someone who is already in the business, and with the other sources it pays for the whole plan.

matters_more_when.reason: In a business in distress, new money is often wanted to pay out those who are already in it
A new business that runs out of money before it is finished earns nothing to repay with

look_again_when.reason: A new term sheet can change the amount, the rank or the purpose
A new plan of sources and uses can change where the money goes and whether the plan is funded

checks.question: What is the lender asked for: how much, in which currency, for how long and for what purpose?
checks.why: Everything else is read against the request. The answer also puts the facility into the structure.
checks.ask: What are you asking us for? How much, in which currency, for how long, and what will the money pay for?

checks.question: Does the money pay for a project or an asset that can be named: something that is built, bought or expanded, such as a plant, a production line or a site?
checks.why: The checks on a project are asked of the project that the loan pays for, and of no other. A yes puts that project or asset into the structure, linked to the facility. A no means that the money goes into the business as a whole.
checks.ask: Will the money pay for one thing that you can name, such as a new plant or line, or the purchase of an asset? Or will it go into the business as a whole?
checks.note: Record the project or the asset as a subject, and link the facility to it with a link of the kind finances. Where the money pays for several, link each of them. Working capital, a refinancing and general purposes are a no. Other projects of the business are described in facts and on pages. They get no such link and are not checked.

leads_to.reason: What the loan pays for is described there, and examined for whether it can be built or bought and run as planned

checks.question: Where would the lender rank against the others who have put money into the business?
checks.why: The rank says who is paid before the lender when there is not enough for everyone, and so what has to be known about those who stand ahead.
checks.ask: What kind of financing are you looking for? A senior loan with or without security, a loan that ranks behind other lenders, equity, or a guarantee?
checks.if_unknown: Until the rank is known, nobody can say who would be paid before the lender.
checks.note: Choose guarantee where the lender gives a guarantee and lends no money. Choose co_invest where the lender takes a share in another investor's deal, on that investor's terms.

checks.question: Does the business already have other financing in place (loans from banks or other lenders, bonds, leases, shareholder loans)?
checks.why: Opens the topic. The new loan has to fit beside what is already there. A "no" is checked against the accounts and the registry under existing debt.
checks.ask: Does the business already have loans, bonds, leases or shareholder loans? A yes or no is enough to start with.

leads_to.reason: Each lender that is already there can rank ahead, hold security or call its loan first
What is already owed, and how it has been paid, is examined there

checks.question: What does the financing of the business consist of: for each loan or other financing the provider, the amount, the rank, the security and the final maturity, and the equity the owners have paid in?
checks.why: Shows what stands ahead of the lender, beside it and behind it, and when the others must be repaid.
checks.ask: Please list all the financing of the business. For each loan or lease we need the lender, the amount, the security and the final repayment date, and we need the equity that has been paid in. A table is ideal.
checks.if_unknown: Without the full list, nobody can say what ranks ahead of the lender or what falls due before its loan.

checks.question: Are the amount, the currency, the tenor and the rank that are asked for all within what the lender's own policies and limits allow for this country, this sector and this client?
checks.assumption: The lender can provide what is asked for under its own policies and limits
checks.note: This is about the lender's own products and limits. For the country limit, ask whoever keeps the limits and record the date. Whether the lender is the right source of the money is asked under impact and additionality.

checks.question: Is the use of the money set out item by item, each with an amount, so that every item can later be checked against an invoice, a contract or a payment?
checks.assumption: The use of the money is specific enough to be checked after it is paid out
checks.ask: Could you give us a list of what the money will pay for, with an amount for each item?
checks.note: A purpose such as "general corporate purposes", "expansion" or "working capital", without a list of what is to be paid for, is a no.

checks.question: Does any part of the money go to shareholders, related parties or existing lenders (to repay a loan, buy shares, pay a dividend or settle an amount owed to them)?
checks.assumption: All of the money goes into the business, and none of it pays out someone who is already in it
checks.ask: Will any of the money be used to repay an existing loan or a shareholder loan, to settle an amount owed to a related company, to pay a dividend or to buy shares?
checks.note: Record with the answer who is paid, how much, and why that party wants its money now. A refinancing is not a fault in itself. The point is to know who leaves, and whether they leave because they know something.

leads_to.reason: A lender that is repaid may know the business better than the lender that replaces it
Money that goes to owners or related parties leaves the business the loan is repaid from

checks.question: Do the committed sources of money (this loan, other loans and the owners' own money) cover the whole cost of what is planned, including an allowance for cost overruns and the working capital needed until the plan pays for itself?
checks.assumption: The whole plan is funded from committed sources, with room for overruns and for working capital
checks.ask: Could you show us the full cost of the plan and where each part of the money comes from? Which of these sources are signed or already paid in, and which are still being discussed?
checks.if_unknown: A plan that is only partly funded can stop half way, with the lender's money already spent.
checks.note: Committed means signed or paid in. A source that is still being negotiated is not committed. Equity the sponsor intends to put in, or a loan still in another lender's approval process, is not committed. Say how much is still open and who is expected to provide it.

leads_to.reason: A gap in the funding has to be closed by someone who is bound to close it
Funding that is not yet committed is usually made a condition of the first drawdown

checks.question: Is at least about a third of the cost of the plan paid in cash by the owners or from the business's own retained cash, before the lender's money or in step with it, and not in kind, by revaluing assets or with borrowed money?
checks.assumption: The owners carry a share of the plan in cash and stand to lose it first
checks.ask: How much of the cost of the plan do the owners pay themselves, in cash? When is that money paid in, before our loan is drawn or alongside it, and where does it come from?
checks.note: A third is a guide. An institution can set its own share.

leads_to.reason: Where the owners' money comes from, and whether it is theirs, is examined there

checks.question: Is everything that is paid out owed to a lender that is neither a shareholder nor a related party, on a loan that was being paid as agreed (no missed payment, waiver or rescheduling in the last twelve months)?
checks.assumption: Only outside lenders are repaid, on loans that were being paid as agreed, so the lender replaces a creditor and neither rescues one nor pays out an owner
checks.note: A letter counts as best evidence only if it comes from the lender that is repaid. Twelve months is a guide.

indicators.title: Stage of the business
indicators.claim: Repayment is shown on what the business earns today, or the step from today to the projected business is in the structure as a project.

matters_more_when.reason: Repayment then rests wholly on the step from today's business to the projected one
A project has no other business to fall back on if it is late or over budget

look_again_when.reason: A new model can move repayment from today's business to the business that is planned
New management accounts can show that the business has slipped into losses or late payment
A new capital spending programme changes the stage of the business

checks.question: What stage is the business in?
checks.why: The stage says how much of the repayment story has already happened and how much is still a plan.
checks.ask: Is the business already operating? If it is, is it running steadily, in the middle of a large expansion or change, or in difficulty?
checks.note: Choose greenfield where the business is not yet operating. Choose expanding where it operates and a capital spending programme of the size asked about in the next check is planned or under way. Choose established where it operates and no such programme is planned. Choose distressed where the business is in default, is being restructured, or does not pay suppliers, lenders, staff or taxes on time. Where distressed applies together with another stage, choose distressed.

leads_to.reason: A business that does not operate yet rests on its feasibility
A business in distress fails first for lack of cash

checks.question: Is a capital spending programme planned or under way that the business cannot pay for from one year of its own operating cash flow, or that the projected revenue depends on?
checks.why: Such a programme has to be finished on time and on budget before the projected business exists, so it is examined as a project.
checks.ask: Do you plan to build, expand or replace on a scale that needs outside money, or that the growth in your plan depends on?
checks.note: This covers a new plant, a large expansion and a major overhaul. The routine replacement of worn equipment is not meant. A site visit answers best whether building is under way. Record what was seen, and when.

checks.question: Do the projections show the loan repaid by the business as it is today (current_state), by today's business with the plan on top while today's business alone would still cover debt service (blended), or only by the business as it will be once the plan is carried out (future_state)?
checks.assumption: Repayment is shown on the business as it is today
checks.why: Projections for the business as it is can be checked against its accounts. Projections for the business as it will be hold only if the plan is finished on time, on budget and at the planned output, so the plan has to be examined as a project.
checks.ask: Could the business repay the loan from what it earns today, or only once the new capacity is in use?
checks.note: Compare the first projected year with the last audited year. Revenue, capacity or margin that the model shows and the accounts do not belongs to the future state. Choose current_state where the projections hold no planned change. Choose blended where they include the planned business, and today's business alone would still cover debt service in every year. Choose future_state where debt service in any year is covered only with the planned business.

leads_to.reason: The projections describe a business that does not exist yet
Whether the planned business can be built and run as projected is examined there

checks.question: Did the business make a loss in its latest financial year or in the current year to date, or is it paying suppliers, lenders, staff or taxes late today?
checks.assumption: The business makes a profit and pays what it owes on time today
checks.ask: Is the business making a profit this year? Are all suppliers, lenders, salaries and taxes being paid on time at the moment?
checks.note: Read the latest management accounts and the ageing list of amounts owed to suppliers, not only the last audited year. A party that says yes is believed. If the answer is yes, look at the stage again.

leads_to.reason: Late payment is the first sign that cash is short
A business that pays late has often already missed a payment to a lender

checks.question: Is the step from today's business to the projected business set out as a project, with a budget, a timetable and a named party that answers for its completion?
checks.assumption: The step from today's business to the projected one is a defined project, with a budget, a timetable and a party that answers for completion

indicators.title: Kind of business
indicators.claim: The business earns its revenue and its profit from the activity it is described as, and not mainly from something else.

look_again_when.reason: New accounts can show a different mix of revenue and profit

checks.question: What kind of credit is this: a company repaid from its business as a whole, a project or single asset repaid from its own cash flow, a financial institution, or a fund?
checks.why: The answer decides which view applies. A company and a project are examined with the corporate view, and a bank or another lender with the bank module.
checks.if_unknown: Until the kind of credit is known, the tool cannot say which indicators apply.
checks.note: The answer is for the deal. It can be recorded for one party alone when that party is a different kind of credit from the rest of the deal, for example a bank that guarantees a factory's loan. The standard has no checks yet for a fund's own repayment (net asset value against debt, uncalled commitments of its investors, concentration of its portfolio). Where the answer is fund, record these as open by hand.

checks.question: Which sector is the business in?
checks.why: The sector switches on the checks that belong to it, such as those for power and for agribusiness.
checks.ask: What does the business do, and which activity earns the largest part of its profit?
checks.note: Choose the sector that earns the largest part of the profit, also where another activity brings in more revenue. A business that trades more than it makes, and earns most of its profit from what it makes, is in manufacturing. OBS_VALUE_CHAIN_001 goes by the same rule. Agribusiness covers growing, processing and trading farm produce. Power covers generating, transmitting and selling electricity.

checks.question: Is the business supervised as a financial institution, by a central bank or another financial regulator (as a bank, an insurer, a leasing or microfinance company, or a fund manager)?
checks.why: A supervised business answers to a regulator that can limit what it lends, pays out and repays.
checks.ask: Does the business hold a licence from a central bank or another financial regulator, and does that regulator supervise it?
checks.note: If the answer is yes and the kind of credit is not recorded as a financial institution, look at the kind of credit again.

leads_to.reason: What the supervisor requires, and what it has found, is examined there

checks.question: Where does the business sit in its value chain?
checks.why: The place in the chain says whom the business depends on. A trader depends on its suppliers and its bank lines, a concessionaire on the authority that granted the concession.
checks.ask: What is the main role of the business? Does it grow or extract, make, trade, distribute, sell to consumers, provide a service, develop assets, own and operate them, hold a concession, lend, or manage funds?
checks.note: Choose the role that earns the largest part of the profit, also where another role brings in more revenue. A business that trades more than it makes, and earns most of its profit from what it makes, is a manufacturer. The sector in OBS_SECTOR_002 goes by the same rule. Choose developer where the business builds assets to sell them, and owner_operator where it keeps and runs them.

checks.question: How does the business earn its money: what does it buy, what does it do with it, whom does it sell to, and where does its margin come from?
checks.why: A sector and a place in the value chain are labels. The description says what the business does in fact, and every figure is read against it. The pages on the business start from this answer.
checks.ask: Please walk us through the business. What do you buy and from whom, what do you do with it, whom do you sell to, and on which step do you earn your margin?
checks.note: Describe, do not judge. A few sentences in the terms of the business itself: the goods, the steps, the customers. Where the accounts show it, say what share of revenue and of profit each activity brings. Where the business has several activities, describe each.

checks.question: What is particular about this business compared with others of its kind, and how does that show in its figures?
checks.why: Two businesses in one sector can earn their money in different ways. What sets this one apart explains figures that would look wrong beside its peers, such as a thin margin in a business that trades more than it makes.
checks.ask: What do you do differently from other businesses in your line? What would surprise someone who knows the sector but not your company?
checks.note: Name a few things, each with the figure it shows in. Examples are an unusual mix of activities, an owner who is also a customer or a supplier, a location, a season, the way stock is financed, or a rule that applies to this business alone. Leave out what is true of every business of its kind. If nothing sets it apart, say so.

checks.question: Is the largest revenue line in the latest audited accounts the activity that the business is described as?
checks.assumption: The largest source of revenue is the activity the business is described as
checks.note: Read the revenue note or the segment note, not the description at the front of the report. The check is not asked of a business that does not operate yet, because it has no revenue to read.

checks.question: Does more than half of the profit before tax come from something other than the stated business (for example trading gains, the sale or revaluation of property, financial income or dealings with related parties)?
checks.assumption: Most of the profit comes from the stated business
checks.note: Take the profit before tax over the last three years where the accounts allow it, and count gains from revaluation as something else. Half is a guide. What counts is whether the business that was described is the one that earns the money.

leads_to.reason: Income from related parties may not be earned at market terms, and may not last
Profit that does not come from the stated business has to be understood before it is counted on

indicators.title: How the loan is repaid
indicators.claim: The loan has a first way out in cash flow that can be named and checked, a second way out if that fails, and the two would not fail for the same reason.

matters_more_when.reason: A holding company is repaid from what its subsidiaries pay up to it, not from a business of its own
There is no cash flow yet, so the first way out is a plan
A lender that ranks behind others reaches the second way out only after they have been paid

look_again_when.reason: A new term sheet can change the security, the guarantee or who borrows
A new model can change what repayment rests on and which assumptions carry it
In a business in distress, the cash flow that was relied on is already failing

checks.question: What is the first way out: whose cash flow repays the loan, and what does that cash flow come from?
checks.why: The party named here is the one the analysis has to follow, whether or not it is the borrower.
checks.ask: Where will the money to repay the loan come from? Which company earns it, and from which activity or contract?
checks.if_unknown: If nobody can say whose cash flow repays the loan, there is no deal to analyse yet.

checks.question: How do businesses of this kind, in this country, usually fail to repay their loans?
checks.why: The answer says where to look first. It comes from the lender's own experience and from what is known about the sector, not from the client.
checks.note: Name the two or three usual causes, for example a fall in the price of the product, a late start of operations, a customer that pays late or a currency that loses value. Each cause points at an indicator to look at first.

checks.question: Is the cash that repays the loan earned by the borrower itself, and not by a subsidiary, a parent, a sister company or another party that would first have to pass it on?
checks.assumption: The cash that repays the loan is earned by the borrower itself
checks.ask: Which company receives the revenue that will repay the loan? Is it the borrower itself, or another company in the group?
checks.note: Read the borrower's own accounts, not the consolidated accounts of its group. A holding company's cash is whatever its subsidiaries pay up to it.

leads_to.reason: Cash earned elsewhere in a group has to be passed up or across before it can repay the loan

checks.question: What does the first way out rest on: cash flow the business has already earned, cash flow due under signed contracts, both together, or cash flow that is only projected?
checks.assumption: Repayment rests on cash flow that already exists, either earned in past years or due under signed contracts
checks.why: Cash flow that has been earned, or is owed under a signed contract, can be checked against accounts and documents. Projected cash flow exists only in a plan, so the loan then depends on the plan being carried out.
checks.ask: Will the loan be repaid from what the business already earns, from payments under contracts that are already signed, or from revenue that is still to be built up?
checks.note: Choose by what covers debt service, not by what the business plan calls it. Choose historical where the cash flow of the last years, as the accounts show it, covers debt service on its own. Choose contracted where payments due under signed contracts cover it on their own. Choose mixed where the two cover it together and neither does alone. Choose projected where debt service cannot be covered without cash flow that neither the accounts nor signed contracts show yet.

leads_to.reason: The projections then carry the whole first way out
A contract is worth what the party that must pay under it is worth

checks.question: Which few assumptions must hold for the first way out to work (for example a price, a volume, the renewal of a contract, a completion date, an exchange rate)?
checks.why: These are the assumptions the rest of the analysis sets out to disprove. If one of them fails, the first way out fails.
checks.note: Keep the list short. A list of ten has not yet been thought through.

checks.question: What is the second way out: where would the money come from if the first way out failed (the sale of assets held as security, a guarantor, the owners, a refinancing, the sale of the business)?
checks.why: A lender that cannot name its second way out has only one. A refinancing or a sale of the business counts only if someone would still lend to the business, or buy it, after the first way out has failed.

checks.question: What is the loan secured on: one asset, several assets, the whole business, or nothing?
checks.assumption: The loan is secured on assets, so that the lender is paid from them ahead of other creditors
checks.why: Security gives the lender assets to be paid from, ahead of others, if the cash flow fails. Without it the lender stands with every unsecured creditor, and the second way out has to come from a guarantee or from the owners.
checks.ask: What security is offered for the loan? One asset, several assets, everything the business owns, or none?
checks.note: Choose enterprise where the security covers all, or nearly all, of the assets of the business and its shares. Record what is offered now. Whether the security holds, and what it is worth, is asked about the facility and about each asset.

checks.question: If the first way out failed for its most likely reason, would the second way out still bring in enough to repay what is owed?
checks.assumption: The second way out would still repay the loan if the first failed for its most likely reason
checks.note: First name the most likely reason. Then ask what the security would fetch, or what the guarantor could pay, in that case. A plant built for one customer is worth little once that customer is gone. A guarantor that lives on the borrower's dividends has nothing when the borrower stops paying them. Where there is no second way out, the answer is no.

checks.question: Has a party whose own income does not depend on the borrower's business promised in writing to pay the lender if the borrower cannot (a guarantee, a completion undertaking or a standby letter of credit from a bank)?
checks.assumption: A party whose income does not depend on the borrower's business has promised to pay if the borrower cannot
checks.note: A letter of comfort or a statement of intent is not a promise to pay. The promise itself is examined on its own link.

checks.question: Is every party that earns the cash bound to the loan as co-borrower or guarantor, or is its cash paid into an account that the lender controls?
checks.assumption: The parties that earn the cash are bound to the loan, or their cash reaches an account the lender controls

indicators.title: Country
indicators.claim: Nothing in the country would stop a sound business from paying a foreign lender on time, or stop that lender from enforcing its claim there.

matters_more_when.reason: A concession is granted by the state and can be taken back by it
Security on one asset is worth only what the courts of its country will enforce

look_again_when.reason: A change in the rating of the state, or in its outlook, says the state's own position has moved
Local counsel's opinion can change the view on exchange controls and on enforcement

checks.question: In which country is the borrower incorporated, in which are its main assets, and from which does it earn the revenue that services the loan?
checks.why: Every other check of this topic is asked about one of these countries. Where they differ, each is looked at for what happens there.
checks.ask: Where is the company registered, where are its main sites, and in which countries does it sell?
checks.if_unknown: Until the countries are named, none of the country checks can be answered.

checks.question: Is the government of the country from which the loan is serviced in default on its foreign debt, restructuring it, or drawing emergency financing to meet its payments abroad?
checks.assumption: The state is paying its own foreign creditors and is not short of foreign currency
checks.why: A state that cannot pay its own foreign creditors usually rations foreign currency for everyone else.
checks.note: A regular programme with the International Monetary Fund is not by itself an emergency. Arrears, a moratorium, a restructuring or rapid financing to close a gap in payments abroad are. If the search finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when.

leads_to.reason: A state short of foreign currency usually has a currency that is falling

checks.question: In the last five years, has armed conflict or civil unrest stopped businesses from operating in the region where the main assets are, or has the state seized privately owned assets in the sector or forced their sale?
checks.assumption: The business can keep operating where its main assets are, and keep owning them
checks.note: Say which of the two it was, and how close to the assets. If the search finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when.

checks.question: In the last ten years, has the country delayed or blocked private payments abroad, frozen bank deposits, or forced debts or deposits in foreign currency to be converted into local currency?
checks.assumption: For the last ten years the country has let private borrowers pay foreign lenders without interruption
checks.why: A base rate. A country that has done this within memory has the rules and the habit to do it again.
checks.note: If the search finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when.

checks.question: Under the rules and the practice of today, do exchange controls or a shortage of foreign currency delay or limit the conversion of local currency and its transfer abroad for debt service?
checks.assumption: Local currency can be converted and sent abroad for debt service without delay or limit
checks.ask: Do you need an approval, a registration or an allocation of foreign currency to pay a lender abroad? How long did your last transfer abroad take, from the request to the payment?
checks.note: Where the loan must be registered or approved before it can be serviced abroad, answer for the position once that is done, and record the registration as a condition.

checks.question: Could a foreign lender obtain a judgment or an arbitral award against the borrower on the loan, have it recognised in the borrower's country and collect on it there within about three years?
checks.assumption: A foreign lender can enforce its loan claim through the country's courts within about three years
checks.note: Three years is a guide. Ask local counsel how long contested enforcement by a foreign creditor has taken in recent cases, not how long the law says it takes.

leads_to.reason: Where enforcement is slow or uncertain, the security has to be looked at asset by asset

checks.question: Is debt service paid from an account outside the country, into which buyers pay export proceeds or other foreign-currency receipts before the money enters the country?
checks.assumption: Debt service is paid from foreign currency that is collected and held outside the country
checks.note: Ask counsel whether the rules of the country allow export proceeds to be kept abroad. An account that breaks them protects nobody.

checks.question: Is the lender protected against the event that the test found, by political risk insurance or a guarantee that names that risk, or (for a block on transfers only) by treatment as a preferred creditor that the country honoured the last time it restricted payments?
checks.assumption: Political risk cover, or treatment as a preferred creditor, protects the lender against the event
checks.note: Cover must name the risk: a block on conversion and transfer, expropriation, or political violence. Treatment as a preferred creditor rests on practice, and it does not help against conflict or expropriation.

indicators.title: Power: tariff and regulation
indicators.claim: The project keeps the tariff it was granted until the loan is repaid, or is made whole if the tariff or the rules change.

matters_more_when.reason: Repayment rests on a tariff or a contract that the state granted and can change

look_again_when.reason: A tariff order, a licence or a notice from the regulator bears directly on the claim
A new draft or the signed purchase agreement can change the price and the protection against a change in law
Counsel's review can find a missing licence or a rule that is about to change

checks.question: How is the price for the project's electricity set?
checks.assumption: The price is fixed, or set by a stated rule, and does not follow the market from day to day
checks.why: A merchant plant sells at the market price of the day, so no rule and no contract holds its revenue up. A hybrid leaves part of the output exposed in the same way. The other mechanisms fix the price or the way it is set.
checks.ask: How is your selling price set? By a regulator, by a tariff scheme, by an auction award, by a contract you negotiated with the buyer, or by the market?
checks.note: bilateral_contract is a price negotiated with the buyer. hybrid means part of the output is sold at market prices. Say what share.

leads_to.reason: The project is exposed to the market price of power
Part of the output is exposed to the market price of power

checks.question: Is the tariff, or the formula that sets it, fixed until the final maturity of the loan, with no review before then that could lower it?
checks.assumption: The tariff or its formula is fixed until the loan is repaid
checks.note: A regulated tariff that is reset every few years is a no, even where past resets were mild. Indexation by a stated formula is not a review. For a plant that sells at market prices the answer is no.

checks.question: Has a change to the tariff, to grid access or dispatch rules, or to the taxes and incentives for power producers been proposed, or passed but not yet brought into force, that would lower the project's revenue or raise its costs?
checks.assumption: No change now proposed or passed would lower the project's revenue or raise its costs
checks.ask: Do you know of any change to tariffs, grid rules, taxes or incentives for power producers that is being prepared? What would it mean for the project?
checks.note: Name the measure and the date it is due. If the search finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when.

checks.question: In the last ten years, has the government, the regulator or the state power buyer in this country cut a tariff that had been granted, reopened signed power contracts, or stopped paying under them?
checks.assumption: The country has kept to the tariffs and the power contracts it granted
checks.note: This asks about the country's record, not about this project. Name each case and its year. If the search finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when.

leads_to.reason: A state that has reopened power contracts before may do so again

checks.question: Does the project need a subsidy, a tax incentive or a tariff higher than the buyer pays for power from other sources to cover its debt service?
checks.assumption: The project can service its debt without a subsidy, a tax incentive or a tariff above what other power costs the buyer
checks.ask: Which subsidies, tax incentives or special tariffs does the project receive? Would it still cover its debt service without them, at the price the buyer pays for other power?
checks.note: Run the projections without the support. Name each support, who grants it and until when it is granted.

leads_to.reason: The downside case should show the project without the support

checks.question: Has the grid operator or an independent engineer confirmed that the plant meets, or as designed will meet, the technical rules for connection and operation (the grid code)?
checks.assumption: The plant meets the grid code
checks.if_unknown: A plant that does not meet the grid code can be refused connection or be disconnected.

checks.question: Does a signed agreement or a law protect the project if the tariff or the rules change, through a clause that makes good the loss from a change in law, a stabilisation clause, or a government undertaking?
checks.assumption: A signed agreement or a law makes good the project's loss if the tariff or the rules change
checks.note: Read the clause itself and say who must pay, and whether that party has paid under such a clause before. A protection owed by the same state that changes the rule is only as good as that state's record (OBS_EREG_006).

leads_to.reason: A government undertaking is worth what it binds the government to do

indicators.title: Licences and regulation
indicators.claim: The party holds every licence, permit and concession it needs, and none will lapse, be withdrawn or be overtaken by a new rule before the loan is repaid.

matters_more_when.reason: A supervised financial institution cannot trade for a day without its licence
The concession is the business, and its terms say when the grantor can end it
Infrastructure is usually run under a licence or a concession from the state

look_again_when.reason: A new or renewed licence can carry a new expiry date and new conditions
A letter, a notice or an order from an authority bears directly on the claim
Counsel's review can find a licence that is missing or a condition that is not met

checks.question: Does the party need a licence, a permit or a concession from an authority to carry on its main business?
checks.why: Opens the topic. A "no" is not the end of it. OBS_REG_002 and OBS_REG_004 are asked whatever the answer.
checks.ask: Do you need a licence, a permit or a concession to run your main business? Examples are a banking or telecom licence, a mining or water permit, a generation licence or a concession to run a port or a road.

checks.question: Does the party hold, in force today and in its own name, every licence, permit and concession that the law requires for its main business?
checks.assumption: The party holds, in force and in its own name, every licence its business needs
checks.ask: Please share your key licences and permits, or a confirmation from the authority that they are in force. Is any of them held by another company of the group, or by a person?
checks.note: This check does not hang on OBS_REG_001, so that the topic cannot close on one answer. Where the party says it needs no licence, a legal opinion or the authority's own register should bear that out. A licence held by a sister company or by the owner in person is not held by the party. For a power project this is first of all the licence to generate and sell electricity. A provisional licence or an application is a no.

checks.question: In the last three years, has a regulator or a licensing authority sent the party a warning, a notice of breach, a fine or an order to show cause?
checks.assumption: No authority has found the party in breach of its licences or of the rules of its sector in the last three years
checks.ask: In the last three years, has any regulator or authority sent you a warning, a notice of breach, a fine or a request to explain yourself? What was it about, and how did it end?
checks.note: A party that says yes is believed. A party that says no is believed once the authority's record or counsel's review bears it out. If the search finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when.

leads_to.reason: A notice from a regulator can turn into proceedings

checks.question: Does any licence, permit or concession that the business depends on expire, or come up for renewal, before the final maturity of the loan?
checks.assumption: Every licence the business depends on runs beyond the final maturity of the loan
checks.ask: When does each of your key licences and permits expire? What do you have to do to renew it?
checks.note: Record the expiry date of each licence, not only the answer.

checks.question: Can any licence or concession be withdrawn, or does it need a fresh approval, when the ownership of the party changes or when a lender enforces its security?
checks.assumption: The licences stay with the business through a change of ownership and through enforcement of security
checks.if_unknown: Security over the shares or the business may be worth little if the licence does not pass to a buyer.

leads_to.reason: A lender that cannot pass the licence to a buyer needs a direct agreement with the authority, or other security

checks.question: Has a law, a regulation or a change to licence terms been proposed, or passed but not yet brought into force, that would raise the party's costs, cap its prices or restrict its main business?
checks.assumption: No rule now proposed or passed would restrict the party's business or cut its margin
checks.ask: Do you know of any new law, regulation or change to your licence that is being prepared? Think of licensing rules, price controls, taxes on your product, or environmental standards. What would it cost you?
checks.if_unknown: Nobody has looked at what is in preparation.
checks.note: Name the measure and the date it is due. If the search finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when.

checks.question: Does the licence or the law give the party a right to renewal if it has met its conditions, or has the same licence been renewed at every expiry so far without a break?
checks.assumption: Renewal is a right, or has been granted at every expiry so far
checks.note: Say which of the two it is. A record of renewals is weaker than a right, and weaker still where the authority or the policy has changed since the last renewal.

checks.question: Has the authority concerned confirmed in writing that the breach is put right, or that the missing licence is now granted?
checks.assumption: The authority concerned has confirmed that the breach is put right
checks.note: The confirmation must come from the authority. The party's own account of it is not a confirmation.

indicators.title: Sector and market
indicators.claim: For the life of the loan, the market the party sells into will take its output at a price that covers its costs and its debt service.

matters_more_when.reason: Repayment rests on sales that have not been made yet
A new business has no record of selling through a downturn
A primary producer sells what buyers can get elsewhere, at the price the market gives

look_again_when.reason: A new market study can change the view on demand, prices and competitors
A signed sales contract changes how much of the revenue is exposed to the market

checks.question: In the party's main market, has the volume sold grown, stayed level or fallen over the last five years?
checks.why: The trend so far is where any forecast starts. A forecast that breaks with it needs a reason.
checks.ask: Over the last five years, has your market as a whole sold more, about the same or less, in volume? What figures do you rely on?
checks.note: The main market is the product and the place that bring in the largest share of the party's revenue. Say which it is.

leads_to.reason: A forecast of growth in a market that is falling needs a reason

checks.question: In the worst downturn of the last ten years, by how much did the market price of the party's main product fall from its peak to its lowest point?
checks.why: The size of the last downturn is the first measure of what the next one could do. It is the fall to set against the party's margin and its projections.
checks.note: Where the price is fixed and the market adjusts through volume (a regulated price, a service), give the fall in volume and say so. Give the years of the peak and of the low.

leads_to.reason: The downside case should be at least as hard as the last downturn

checks.question: Is the party's selling price set by a market or by its buyers, so that the party cannot raise it when its own costs rise?
checks.assumption: The party has a say in its selling price and can pass on a rise in its costs
checks.ask: Who sets the price you sell at? When your costs last went up, could you raise your price, and how long did it take?

leads_to.reason: A party that takes the market's price carries price risk on its stock and its forward sales

checks.question: At the lowest price of the last ten years (for a processor or a trader: in the year in which the gap between its selling price and the price of its main input was narrowest), would the party's revenue still cover its cash operating costs and its debt service, the proposed loan included?
checks.assumption: The party covers its cash costs and its debt service at the lowest price, or the narrowest spread, of the last ten years
checks.note: Use the party's accounts for that year where it was already trading. Otherwise set today's cash cost per unit against that price (for a processor or a trader, today's cash costs other than the main input against that gap). Where the price is fixed and the market adjusts through volume, use the lowest volume. A producer whose costs are among the highest in its market is the first to lose money when the price falls. The test does not wait for the terms of the loan. If the answer already goes against the assumption on the debt the party owes today, record it now and say that it is before the new loan. Answer again when the terms are known.

checks.question: In the last five years, has a direct competitor of the party, of similar size or larger, become insolvent, defaulted on its debt or had its debt restructured?
checks.assumption: Businesses of this kind and size in this market have serviced their debt through the last five years
checks.why: A base rate. What brought down a business of the same kind in the same market is the first thing to rule out for this one.
checks.ask: Has any of your competitors failed or had to restructure its debt in the last five years? What went wrong?
checks.note: Record who failed and why. If the search finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when.

checks.question: Does the party's margin depend on an import tariff, a quota, an export ban or levy, a subsidy or a regulated price that the government can change or end during the life of the loan?
checks.assumption: The party's margin does not rest on a measure that the government can withdraw
checks.ask: Would you still make money if the import duty, the quota, the export ban or levy, the subsidy or the regulated price that applies to your business were changed or taken away?
checks.note: A regulated price, an export ban, a quota or a levy can protect the party in one year and squeeze it in the next. The test is whether a decision the party does not control can change its margin. Name the measure. A tax holiday or reduced rate is asked under OBS_TAX_008.

leads_to.reason: A measure the margin rests on should be checked for any change that is pending

checks.question: Is there a substitute product, a source of cheaper imports, or new capacity already announced or being built, that would take sales from the party or force its price down during the life of the loan?
checks.assumption: No substitute, import or new capacity now in sight would take the party's sales or force its price down
checks.ask: Who could take your customers in the next few years? Is anyone building new capacity, or importing at a lower price than yours?
checks.note: Count only what can be named today, such as a plant under construction, an import that is already landing or a product that buyers are already switching to. If the search finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when.

checks.question: Over the last three years, has the party lost share in its main market (its sales grew more slowly than the market's, or fell faster)?
checks.assumption: The party has held its place against its competitors over the last three years
checks.ask: How have your sales moved over the last three years compared with your market as a whole? Who has gained share, and who has lost it?
checks.note: Set the party's sales, from its accounts, against the figures for the market used in OBS_MARKET_001, in volume where both are known. Name the source of the market figures. Where the party has traded for less than three years, answer for the time it has traded and say so.

checks.question: Does the party hold signed sales contracts, at a fixed or floor price and for volumes the buyer must take or pay for, that cover its debt service in each year of the loan?
checks.assumption: Sales under contract cover the debt service in each year of the loan
checks.note: A contract that follows the market price, or that the buyer can end at short notice, does not count.

leads_to.reason: A sales contract is worth what the buyer behind it can pay

indicators.title: Agribusiness: crop, supply and season
indicators.claim: A bad season, a broken supply chain or a rejected shipment would not stop the party from servicing its debt.

matters_more_when.reason: A grower carries the weather, the pests and the disease itself
A processor has fixed costs to cover and needs its full intake every season

look_again_when.reason: A season has been lost, so what it cost and whether the protections worked need a new look
The accounts of a new season show intake and stock written off

checks.question: What share of the crop or other farm produce that the party processes or trades, by volume, does it buy from farmers or outgrowers that it does not control?
checks.why: Produce from the party's own farms is in its hands. Produce bought from independent farmers can go to another buyer in any season. The larger this share, the more the check on side-selling, and the check on advances under Working capital, count.
checks.ask: How much of the crop you process or trade comes from your own farms, and how much do you buy from farmers or outgrowers?
checks.note: Give the figure for the last full season, and say whether it changes much from year to year.

checks.question: In any of the last five seasons, did farmers that the party had contracted or financed deliver less than about four fifths of the agreed volume because they sold to other buyers?
checks.assumption: The farmers that the party contracts or finances deliver their crop to it, also in seasons when other buyers pay more
checks.ask: In each of the last five seasons, how much did your contracted farmers agree to deliver and how much did they deliver? Was there a season in which they sold to others?
checks.note: Four fifths is a guide. Look at the seasons in which the market price rose above the contract price: that is when side-selling shows. Answer no, and say so, where the party buys nothing from contracted or financed farmers.

checks.question: Is the highest yearly volume of crop, milk or other farm produce that the projections count on no more than the party took in during its best season of the last five, or is the extra volume contracted with named farmers, cooperatives or suppliers who have it to sell?
checks.assumption: The farm produce that the projections count on has been delivered before, or is contracted with those who have it
checks.why: A processing line built ahead of its supply runs below capacity, whatever the plant can do. The produce has to exist and has to be the party's to buy.
checks.ask: What is the highest yearly intake in your projections, and what was your intake in each of the last five seasons? Where will the extra volume come from, and is it under contract?
checks.note: Use volume, not value. A letter of intent, or a list of farmers the party hopes to sign, is not a contract. Where the extra volume is to come from the party's own new plantings or herd, say when they will first yield.

leads_to.reason: The volumes in the projections then have to be cut to what the supply can deliver

checks.question: What was the party's lowest yearly harvest or intake in the last ten years, as a percentage of the average of those years?
checks.why: The gap between the worst year and the average is the size of a bad season for this party. The downside case in the projections should be at least as bad.
checks.ask: What was your harvest or intake in each of the last ten years? Which was the worst year, and what caused it?
checks.note: Use volume, not value. With fewer than ten years of record, use the record of the district or of the crop and say so.

checks.question: In the last five years, has drought, flood, frost, a pest or a disease cut the party's harvest or intake in a season to less than about four fifths of its average?
checks.assumption: The party's harvest or intake has held up through the weather, pests and disease of the last five years
checks.ask: In the last five years, was there a season in which drought, flood, frost, a pest or a disease cut your harvest or intake? By how much?
checks.note: Four fifths is a guide. Record the event, the season and the fall in volume. If a search of weather and disease records finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when.

leads_to.reason: The downside case should repeat a season of that kind

checks.question: In the last five years, was a shipment of the party stopped at a border for food safety, residues or pests, or was a certificate that it needs in order to sell (food safety, organic, plant health or export approval) suspended or withdrawn?
checks.assumption: The party's product meets the food safety and plant health rules of its markets, and the party has kept the certificates it needs in order to sell
checks.ask: In the last five years, was any shipment of yours stopped at a border? Was any of your certificates suspended or withdrawn?
checks.note: If the search finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when. Some importing markets publish their border rejections. A batch or shipment that a customer rejected is asked in OBS_OPS_006.

checks.question: Does the party own, or hold under a contract that runs through the season, what it needs to keep the produce from spoiling on the way in and on the way out: collection, cooling and testing at intake between the farm and the plant, and storage and (for a product that spoils) the cold chain until the product is sold?
checks.assumption: The party controls the collection, the storage and the cold chain that its raw produce and its product need
checks.ask: How does the produce get from the farm to your plant, and who owns the collection points, the cooling and the testing at intake? Where is your product stored until it is sold, and who owns the stores, the cold rooms and the refrigerated transport?
checks.note: Both the way in and the way out must hold for a yes. Say which part is missing. Products that spoil include fresh fruit and vegetables, flowers, milk, meat and fish. For grain and other dry crops, ask about drying and about storage free of pests and damp.

checks.question: In which months of the year is the party's cash lowest and its borrowing highest, and what causes it?
checks.why: An agribusiness buys its crop in a few weeks and sells it over many months. Its debt and its liquidity are read at that peak, and repayment dates are set after the crop is sold.
checks.ask: In which months do you buy your crop, and in which months is your overdraft or seasonal borrowing at its highest?

leads_to.reason: Cash has to be read in the months this answer names, not at the year-end
Stock and seasonal borrowing peak in the months this answer names

checks.question: What protects the party against a bad season?
checks.assumption: Irrigation, supply from regions with different weather, or crop or weather insurance limits what a bad season costs the party
checks.why: With none of the three, the whole loss of a bad season falls on the party's cash flow in the year it happens.
checks.ask: What protects you in a bad season: irrigation, buying from several regions, or crop or weather insurance?
checks.note: Say which event each protection answers: irrigation does not help against a flood or a disease, and insurance pays only for the perils and the area it names.

indicators.title: Operating assets
indicators.claim: The asset can do its work until the loan is repaid without spending that the projections do not show.

matters_more_when.reason: One asset secures the loan, so its condition decides both the cash flow and the value of the security
In real estate the building is the business, and its condition sets the rent and the value
An infrastructure asset has to stay available to earn its payments and to keep its concession

look_again_when.reason: An engineer's report can change the view of the condition, the remaining life and the spending needed
A valuer who has inspected the asset reports on its condition and its remaining life

checks.question: Who owns the asset?
checks.why: An asset that the party uses but does not own can be taken back, and the party cannot give it as security. The owner belongs in the structure, with an "owns" link to the asset.
checks.ask: Who holds the title to this asset? If it is leased or held under a concession, from whom, and until when?
checks.note: Title documents are filed with the security documents. Under a lease or a concession the owner is someone else, however long it runs.

checks.question: Does repayment depend on this asset: does it carry about a tenth or more of the output or the earnings that repay the loan, or is it offered as security?
checks.why: An asset that carries little of the business and secures nothing is described and not examined. The checks on its condition, its upkeep and its remaining life are asked of the assets that repayment or the security rests on.
checks.note: A tenth is a guide. Say in the reason what share of output or earnings the asset carries, and whether it is to be security. Answer again when the security for the loan is settled.

checks.question: What condition is the asset in?
checks.assumption: The asset is in working condition and needs no major repair or replacement now
checks.why: An asset in poor condition or at the end of its life needs repair or replacement that takes cash from debt service, and it can stop without warning.
checks.ask: How old is this asset and what condition is it in? An asset register, a recent valuation or an inspection report would answer this.
checks.note: New: in its first years of use. Good: runs at the output it was built for, with routine maintenance. Fair: runs at that output, with wear that planned maintenance can deal with. Poor: runs below that output, breaks down often or needs a major overhaul now. End of life: at or past the life it was built for. Record the age of the asset with the answer. What the officer saw on a site visit counts as stated.

checks.question: Has someone independent of the party (an engineer, a surveyor or a valuer) inspected the asset and reported on its condition in the last three years?
checks.assumption: Someone independent of the party has inspected the asset and reported on its condition
checks.ask: Has an independent engineer, surveyor or valuer inspected this asset in the last three years? May we see the report?
checks.note: Three years is a guide. A valuation made without an inspection does not count.

checks.question: Is there a written maintenance plan for the asset, with a budget that is carried into the projections?
checks.assumption: Maintenance of the asset is planned, and its cost is in the projections
checks.ask: Do you have a maintenance plan and a yearly maintenance budget for this asset? Where does that budget appear in your projections?
checks.if_unknown: Without a plan and a budget, the cost of keeping the asset working is not in the projections.

checks.question: Has maintenance that was due on the asset been put off, so that a backlog has built up?
checks.assumption: The maintenance that was due on the asset has been done
checks.ask: Has any maintenance that was due on this asset been postponed? What would it cost to catch up?
checks.if_unknown: A backlog that nobody has counted is a cost that the projections do not show.
checks.note: Where there is a backlog, record what it would cost to clear. Maintenance spending that falls while the asset ages is a sign of one.

checks.question: Is the remaining useful life of the asset shorter than the time until the final repayment of the proposed loan?
checks.assumption: The asset will last until the loan is repaid
checks.ask: How many more years can this asset work before it has to be replaced or rebuilt?
checks.note: Use the technical life that an engineer or a valuer gives, not the life used for depreciation in the accounts. Where the asset is held under a lease or a concession, its life for the party ends when that does.

checks.question: Is the cost of the repair, overhaul or replacement that the asset needs included in the projections, with its funding named?
checks.assumption: The spending that the asset needs is in the projections and is funded
checks.ask: What will the repair, overhaul or replacement of this asset cost, when is it planned, and how will it be paid for?
checks.note: Compare the amount in the projections with the estimate of the engineer or the valuer, not with the party's own.

indicators.title: Insurance
indicators.claim: A loss the party could not absorb is insured, and the insurer would pay.

matters_more_when.reason: One uninsured loss would take both the cash flow and the security
A single project has no other business to carry it through a loss

look_again_when.reason: Policies are renewed each year, and the cover can change at each renewal
A broker's report can show gaps, unpaid premiums or a change of insurer

checks.question: Does the party hold insurance?
checks.why: Opens the topic. A yes says nothing about what is covered: OBS_INS_005 checks it against the policies whatever the answer here.
checks.ask: Does the company hold any insurance? A policy schedule, a certificate or a letter from your broker would be ideal, but a list of the policies is enough to start with.

checks.question: Which kinds of insurance does the party hold?
checks.why: The kinds held are set against the losses the party could not absorb: damage to its assets, the profit lost while they are repaired, and claims by others.
checks.ask: Which kinds of insurance do you hold? For example property, machinery breakdown, business interruption, liability, goods in transit, key person.

checks.question: Do the policy schedules, or a confirmation from the insurer or the broker, show that the party's policies are in force today and that all premiums due are paid?
checks.assumption: The party's insurance is in force and paid for
checks.ask: Are all your policies in force and all premiums paid to date? A confirmation from your broker or insurer would show this.
checks.note: This check does not hang on OBS_INS_001, so that the topic cannot close on one answer. Answer no where the party holds no insurance or cannot show a policy. Policies usually run for a year: record the renewal dates.

checks.question: Do the sums insured cover the cost of replacing the party's operating assets as new, and at least twelve months of lost gross profit?
checks.assumption: The sums insured would pay for replacing the assets and for the profit lost while they are replaced
checks.ask: What are the sums insured for your assets and for lost profit, and how were they set? We will compare them with the replacement cost of the assets and with a year's gross profit.
checks.if_unknown: Until the sums insured are set against replacement cost, the party may be insured for less than a loss would cost.
checks.note: Twelve months is a guide: use the time it would take to rebuild and restart where that is longer. Compare the sums insured with a valuation at replacement cost, not with book value. Under many policies the insurer may cut every claim in proportion where the sum insured is below the value.

checks.question: Do the policies exclude, or leave uninsured, a peril that could stop the party's operations at its sites (for example fire, flood, earthquake, machinery breakdown, riot or political violence)?
checks.assumption: The perils that could stop the party's operations at its sites are insured
checks.ask: Which risks do your policies exclude? For example flood, earthquake, machinery breakdown, riot or political violence.
checks.note: Start from the hazards of the sites and of the sector, then read the exclusions and the deductibles. A deductible larger than the cash the party holds works like an exclusion.

checks.question: Is the insurer that carries the property and business interruption cover rated investment grade for financial strength, or is the risk passed on to reinsurers that are?
checks.assumption: The insurer, or the reinsurers behind it, can pay a claim of the size insured
checks.ask: Which insurer carries your property and business interruption cover? Is it rated, and is the risk reinsured?
checks.note: Investment grade (BBB- or its equal on the scale of an international rating agency) is a guide, and many lenders ask for more. A local insurer that keeps the whole risk on its own books may be unable to pay a large claim. Where the cover is reinsured, ask whether the insured can claim from the reinsurers directly.

checks.question: In the last five years, has an insurer refused a claim by the party, paid less than was claimed after a dispute, or cancelled or declined to renew a policy?
checks.assumption: Insurers have paid the party's claims and kept its cover
checks.ask: In the last five years, has an insurer refused or reduced a claim of yours, or cancelled or declined to renew a policy? May we see the claims record from your broker or insurer?
checks.note: Ask for the claims record from the insurer or the broker, not only from the party.

indicators.title: Construction
indicators.claim: The project will be complete and performing as designed before the first repayment falls due, for no more money than is committed.

matters_more_when.reason: There is no cash flow at all until the project is complete
A single-purpose company has no other business to carry a delay or an overrun

look_again_when.reason: A signed or amended construction contract changes the price, the date and the remedies
A progress report from the independent engineer shows cost and schedule at a new date

checks.question: Has the project signed a construction contract, or a set of contracts, that covers all the works needed to complete it?
checks.assumption: A builder is bound by contract to carry out all the works
checks.ask: Is the construction contract signed? Please share it. If the works are split between several contracts, please list them and say who answers for the whole.
checks.if_unknown: Until a contract is signed, the scope, the price and the completion date are estimates.
checks.note: A letter of intent, a preferred bidder or a contract still under negotiation is a no. The terms of the contract and the builder itself are examined on the link to the builder (CAS_BUILDER_OPERATOR_001).

checks.question: Does the construction contract make handover depend on performance tests against stated figures (such as capacity, output or efficiency), with damages or a right to reject the works if the figures are not met?
checks.assumption: The builder must hand over works that pass stated performance tests, or pay
checks.if_unknown: The project may have to accept and pay for a plant that does not perform as designed.

checks.question: Would the damages the builder must pay for delay, up to their cap, cover the interest and repayments that fall due during a delay of six months and that the existing business could not pay from its own cash flow?
checks.assumption: Damages for delay cover the debt service that falls due while the project is late and that the existing business cannot pay
checks.note: Six months is a guide. Use the delay the independent engineer thinks plausible where there is one. For a new project with no existing business, the damages have to cover all the debt service of those months. For a line added to a running business, take off what the existing business can pay, and say how much that is. Record the daily rate, the cap as a share of the contract price, and for how long after handover the builder must repair defects.

checks.question: How does the construction budget compare with the cost incurred so far and an independent estimate of the cost to complete?
checks.assumption: The budget, with its contingency, covers the cost to complete as someone independent estimates it
checks.why: An overrun larger than the contingency that is left means the committed money will not finish the project. Where nobody independent has compared, the budget is the sponsor's own word.
checks.ask: Has an independent engineer or cost consultant reviewed the budget? If construction has started, please share the latest report on cost to date and cost to complete.
checks.note: minor_overrun means the overrun fits within the contingency that is left. material_overrun means it does not. For a project that has not started, compare the budget with the independent engineer's or cost consultant's own estimate.
