checks.question: Is the first repayment of principal due at least six months after the date on which the project is expected to be complete?
checks.assumption: The first repayment falls due only after the project is complete and earning, with room for a delay
checks.note: Take the completion date the independent engineer expects where there is one, and the date in the contract otherwise. Say which. Six months is a guide. What counts is that a plausible delay does not leave a repayment due before the project earns.

checks.question: Has a sponsor or another party signed an undertaking to pay for cost overruns or to see the project completed?
checks.assumption: A party other than the project is bound to pay for overruns or to complete the project
checks.note: A letter of comfort or a statement of intent is a no.

leads_to.reason: The undertaking is worth what its triggers, its cap and its giver are worth

indicators.title: Power: generation and sale
indicators.claim: The plant can deliver to the grid the energy the projections count on, and a buyer is bound to take it or pay for it.

matters_more_when.reason: Repayment rests on the purchase agreement, so its terms on output and curtailment decide the cash flow
There is no operating record to set the forecast against

look_again_when.reason: A new draft or the signed purchase agreement can change the volume, the price and who bears curtailment
A new yield study, grid study or engineer's report can change the output the plant is expected to deliver

checks.question: What is the plant's installed or planned generating capacity?
checks.why: Capacity sets the scale of the project. With the capacity factor it gives the energy the projections sell.
checks.ask: What is the capacity of the plant in megawatts, installed or planned?
checks.note: Say whether the figure is the capacity of the generating units or the capacity that may be fed into the grid, where the two differ.

checks.question: What capacity factor do the projections assume (the energy sold in a year as a share of what the plant would produce if it ran at full capacity all year)?
checks.why: The capacity factor turns capacity into energy sold. A figure above what the independent yield study or the plant's own record supports overstates revenue in every year.
checks.note: Take the figure net of the plant's own use, of losses up to the meter and of planned outages. Say whether it is the central estimate (P50) or a more cautious one.

checks.question: Has the project signed a power purchase agreement, or another contract of sale, for its output?
checks.assumption: A buyer is bound by contract to buy the plant's output
checks.ask: Is a power purchase agreement signed? Please share it. If not, who will buy the power, and at what stage are the talks?
checks.if_unknown: Without a signed agreement the plant sells at whatever price and volume the market gives it.
checks.note: An award letter, a term sheet or an agreement that is initialled but not signed is a no. Record the share of the projected output that the agreement covers. What it does not cover is sold at market prices (OBS_EREG_002).

leads_to.reason: The agreement is worth what the buyer can pay
The term, the price and the rights to terminate decide what the agreement gives the lender
Without a contract the project is exposed to the market price of power

checks.question: Under the purchase agreement, who bears the loss when the grid cannot take the plant's output (curtailment or a grid outage)?
checks.assumption: The buyer pays for energy the plant could have delivered but the grid could not take
checks.why: Where the buyer pays for energy that was available, curtailment is the buyer's cost. Where the project bears it or shares it, or the agreement is silent, curtailed hours are lost revenue.
checks.note: buyer_pays means the buyer pays for energy deemed delivered. For shared, say what allowance of unpaid hours or what cap applies, and set it against the curtailment found in OBS_EGEN_005.

checks.question: Is the plant connected to the grid, or does it hold a signed connection agreement for its full capacity with a connection date no later than its planned start of operation?
checks.assumption: The plant can deliver its full output to the grid from the day it starts
checks.ask: Is the plant connected, or is the connection agreement signed? Who builds and pays for the line and the substation, and by when?
checks.if_unknown: A plant that cannot deliver its power earns nothing, whatever it can generate.
checks.note: An application, a connection offer not yet accepted or a study by the grid operator is a no. Say who builds the line and the substation, and whether that work is inside the construction budget and schedule.

checks.question: Does a grid study, or the grid operator's record for this area, show that more of the plant's output is likely to be curtailed (held back because the grid cannot take it) than the projections allow for?
checks.assumption: The grid can take the plant's output, apart from the curtailment the projections already allow for
checks.ask: Has output from this plant, or from plants nearby, been held back by the grid operator? Is there a grid study that estimates how much will be?
checks.note: A no needs a grid study or the operator's record behind it. If the search finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when. Where nobody has studied it, the answer is not known.

checks.question: Has the energy the plant delivered in each of the last three full years reached the yearly figure the projections count on?
checks.assumption: The plant's own record bears out the output the projections count on
checks.ask: Please share the metered energy delivered in each of the last three years, with the buyer's statements or invoices.
checks.note: Take metered energy at the delivery point. Where the plant has run for less than three years, use the years there are and say so. Where capacity is being added, compare per megawatt installed. A shortfall with a one-off cause is still a no, with the cause named.

indicators.title: Power: resource
indicators.claim: The wind, sun, water or fuel will be there, year after year, in the quantity the projections count on.

matters_more_when.reason: There is no operating record, so the yield estimate is the only measure of the resource
A fixed price leaves the quantity generated as the main thing that can move revenue

look_again_when.reason: A new yield study or a longer measurement record can move the estimate and its uncertainty
A new or amended fuel contract changes the quantity and the term that are secured

checks.question: Does the plant draw its energy from a natural resource at its site (sun, wind, water or heat from the ground)?
checks.why: Opens the topic. A yes leads to the checks on measurement and yield. A no means the plant burns fuel that has to be bought, and leads to the check on fuel supply (OBS_ERES_009).
checks.ask: What does the plant run on? Sun, wind, water, heat from the ground, or a fuel that is bought in?
checks.note: For a plant with two sources, answer for the one that most of the projected energy comes from, and say so.

checks.question: Is the yield estimate based on resource data for the site itself (measurements on site, or long-term records calibrated to the site) that cover at least one full year?
checks.assumption: The yield estimate rests on data for this site, not on regional averages
checks.ask: What resource data do you have for the site, measured how, and over what period? Please share the measurement report or the dataset.
checks.if_unknown: Without data for the site, the yield cannot be estimated and the revenue projections have no base.
checks.note: For wind, this means measurement at or near hub height. For water, river flow records over many years. For sun, satellite records checked against measurement on the ground. One year is the least. Record how long the data runs.

checks.question: Has a specialist who is independent of the sponsor and the equipment supplier made or reviewed the energy yield assessment?
checks.assumption: The yield estimate was made or checked by an independent specialist
checks.ask: Who prepared the energy yield report? Please share it.
checks.note: The report must be in hand, with the name of the firm and its date. A yield figure from the developer or from the equipment supplier's own software is not independent.

checks.question: What is the P90 annual energy yield (the yield the plant should exceed in nine years out of ten) as a share of the P50 yield (the yield it is as likely to exceed as to miss)?
checks.why: The gap between the two shows how uncertain the estimate is. The further the P90 lies below the P50, the weaker the central estimate is as a base for debt.
checks.if_unknown: Without a P90 the debt cannot be set against a poor year.
checks.note: Say whether the P90 is for a single year or for an average over ten years. The single-year figure is the lower of the two and the one that matters for a year's debt service. Record both yields in gigawatt hours as well. For water, also record the driest year on record as a share of the average.

checks.question: Does the project still pay its debt service in full in every year of the loan if the yield is the single-year P90 instead of the P50?
checks.assumption: The debt can be serviced in a year as poor as one in ten
checks.note: Paying in full means cash flow available for debt service of at least one times the debt service of that year, before any reserve is drawn. The model is the party's own. The case counts as tested once the lender or an independent adviser has run it.

leads_to.reason: The downside case has to show what a poor resource year does to debt service

checks.question: Do the projections lower the plant's output each year for the wear of the equipment, at a rate that the maker's warranty or an independent study supports?
checks.assumption: The projections allow for the loss of output as the equipment ages
checks.ask: What yearly loss of output do your projections assume, and what is that rate based on?
checks.note: Record the rate. A flat output over the whole life of the loan is a no. For a plant that burns fuel, the loss shows as lower output and as more fuel used for each unit of energy.

checks.question: Is the fuel the plant needs secured under a signed supply contract, for the quantity the projections count on and until the final maturity of the loan?
checks.assumption: A supplier is bound to deliver the fuel the projections count on, for the life of the loan
checks.ask: Who supplies the fuel, under what contract, for what quantity and until when? Please share the contract.
checks.note: A contract that is shorter than the loan, or that covers less than the quantity the projections count on, is a no. Say what is missing. This covers fuel that is grown or collected, such as biomass, as well as gas, coal and oil.

leads_to.reason: The contract is worth what the supplier can deliver
Fuel bought without a contract is exposed to price and to availability

indicators.title: Feasibility
indicators.claim: The project can be built on its site for the estimated cost and run as planned, with technology that already works at this scale.

matters_more_when.reason: Nothing has been built yet, so the studies are all there is to rely on
Repayment rests on cash flows that exist only if the project works as planned

look_again_when.reason: A new study or engineer's report can change the design, the cost or the risks that are known
A signed construction contract replaces estimates with prices

checks.question: What is the project: what is built or bought, where, for how much, by when, who pays for it, and what does it add to the business?
checks.why: Opens the topic. The tests that follow ask whether the project can be built and run as planned. This answer says what the plan is, and the page on the project starts from it.
checks.ask: Please describe the project. What will be built or bought, where, at what cost and by when? Who pays for which part, and what will it add to the business (capacity, products, revenue)?
checks.note: Give the figures with their dates: the cost, the capacity, the planned start and end, and what has been spent so far. Say how far the project has come (planned, approved, under construction, in operation). Where the loan pays for an asset that is bought and not built, describe the asset and the purchase.

checks.question: Is there a written feasibility study for the project that covers its design, its site, its cost and its schedule?
checks.assumption: The plan for the project rests on a written feasibility study
checks.ask: Has a feasibility study been made for the project? Please share it, with its date and the name of whoever wrote it.
checks.if_unknown: Without a study, the design, the cost and the schedule are the sponsor's own word.
checks.note: A study written by or for the sponsor counts here. Whether anyone independent agrees with it is asked in OBS_FEAS_003.

checks.question: Is the project's core technology in commercial operation elsewhere, at about the scale of this project and under conditions like those it will meet?
checks.assumption: The core technology already works in commercial operation at this scale
checks.ask: Where is this technology already running commercially at a similar size? Since when, and who can confirm how it performs?
checks.note: A pilot plant, a demonstration unit or the first plant of its kind is a no. So is a known technology used at several times its largest size so far, or with a feedstock or in a climate it has not run in. The supplier's own list of references is the supplier's word. For a power plant, answer for the chosen model of the main generating equipment, not for its maker or its technology family: a new model from an established maker is a no. Two years of operation at several plants is a guide.

checks.question: Does the project hold the rights of way and the connections it needs (the way in to the site, and the connections to water and transport) under signed agreements that run beyond the final maturity of the loan?
checks.assumption: The project holds its access and its connections for the life of the loan
checks.ask: Are the rights of way to the site and the connections to water and transport signed? Please share the agreements, with the date on which each ends.
checks.note: An option, a letter of intent or an application that is still pending is a no until it is signed or granted. Say which right is missing. The land itself is asked under OBS_LAND_001, and the grid connection of a power project under OBS_EGEN_003.

leads_to.reason: A right of way that is not yet secured may still have to be acquired from people who live on the land or use it

checks.question: Does the cost estimate rest on signed contracts or binding bids for the larger part of the cost, and carry a contingency for the part that is not fixed?
checks.assumption: Most of the cost is fixed by contracts or binding bids, and a contingency covers the rest
checks.note: Both parts must hold for a yes. Indicative quotes, price lists and the sponsor's own figures do not fix a cost. "The larger part" is a guide. Record the contingency as a share of the cost that is not fixed.

leads_to.reason: A cost that is not fixed has to be met from committed funding or from support for overruns

checks.question: Has a technical expert who is independent of the sponsor, the builder and the equipment suppliers reviewed the project's design, cost and schedule, and confirmed that it can be built and run as planned?
checks.assumption: An independent technical expert has confirmed that the project can be built and run as planned
checks.if_unknown: The feasibility of the project rests on the sponsor's word alone.
checks.note: The expert's report must be in hand. Whoever wrote the study for the sponsor has not reviewed it. The usual form is a technical adviser who reports to the lenders. A review that confirms only with open reservations is a no, and the reservations belong in OBS_FEAS_004.

checks.question: Does the feasibility study or the independent expert's review name a technical risk that is still open, with no agreed fix, no party that bears it and no allowance in the cost or the schedule?
checks.assumption: Every technical risk the studies found has a fix, a party that bears it or an allowance in the budget
checks.note: Examples are ground that has not been surveyed, equipment with no reference at this size, a resource or a feedstock that has not been measured, or a single route for delivery. Name each open risk. A study that names no risk at all has not looked.

checks.question: Does the supplier of the technology warrant the plant's output and availability for at least two years after handover, in a signed contract, with damages if they are not reached?
checks.assumption: The supplier must pay if the technology does not perform in its first years of operation
checks.note: A warranty is worth what its giver can pay. A young technology company with little capital does not carry this risk, whatever it signs. Two years is a guide. Performance at handover is asked under OBS_ECON_003.

leads_to.reason: The warranty is worth what the supplier behind it can pay

indicators.title: Inputs and suppliers
indicators.claim: The party can get the inputs it cannot work without, at a price it can bear, until the loan is repaid.

matters_more_when.reason: A manufacturer often turns one feedstock or one source of energy into its product
A distributor lives on the right to sell the goods of one or a few principals
A trader that buys from one source has nothing to sell when that source stops

look_again_when.reason: An interruption has happened, so its length, its cause and the protections need a new look
A new or changed supply contract changes the end date and the price terms

checks.question: Is there one input (a feedstock, a fuel, a utility, a component or goods for resale) that the party cannot produce or trade without, or one supplier that provides about a fifth or more of what it buys?
checks.why: Opens the topic. A no is not the end of it: OBS_INPUT_002 and OBS_INPUT_010 are read from the accounts whatever the answer here.
checks.ask: Is there one input that your production cannot run without, such as a feedstock, a fuel or a utility? Or one supplier from which you buy a large part of what you need? If so, please name the input and the supplier.
checks.note: A fifth is a guide. The checks below call this input "the critical input".

leads_to.reason: The supplier's own standing and the supply contract then need their own look
Whether a rise in the price of the input can be passed on to customers is asked there

checks.question: What share of the party's cost of sales does its largest single bought-in input take?
checks.why: The share says how much of the margin a rise in the price of that one input can take. A processor, a miller, a dairy or a trader spends most of its cost of sales on one input, and that is sound as long as it can pass a rise on. OBS_INPUT_010 tests whether it has.
checks.ask: Which single input costs you the most, and roughly what share of your cost of sales is it?
checks.note: Take the figure from the breakdown of the cost of sales, not from what the party says. Where one input takes about a third of the cost of sales or more and OBS_INPUT_001 was answered no, look at that answer again: this input is then the critical input. A third is a guide.

checks.question: In any of the last five financial years in which the price of the party's largest input rose by about a tenth or more, did its gross margin fall by about a fifth of its level or more (for example from 20 percent to 16)?
checks.assumption: The party has passed on rises in the price of its largest input, so that its margin held
checks.why: What matters is not how large the input is in the costs but whether the gap between the selling price and the price of the input holds when the input costs more.
checks.ask: In which of the last five years did the price of your main input rise the most? What was your gross margin in that year and in the year before?
checks.note: A tenth and a fifth are guides. This check does not hang on OBS_INPUT_001, so that the topic cannot close on one answer. Take the price of the input from the party's purchase records or from a published price, and the margin from the accounts. Where the price did not rise by about a tenth in any of the five years, the record shows nothing either way. Leave the check open and say so.

checks.question: How many suppliers could deliver the critical input in the volume the party needs?
checks.assumption: The party could replace the supplier of its critical input
checks.why: With one source, the supplier's failure, a dispute or a broken pipeline stops production, and the supplier sets the price. With two or more, the party has somewhere to go.
checks.ask: Could another supplier deliver this input in the volume you need, or is there in practice only one source, such as one pipeline, one allocation or one licensed producer?
checks.if_unknown: Until it is known whether the supplier can be replaced, the loss of that supplier has to be treated as the loss of production.
checks.note: Count a supplier only if it could deliver the full volume to the party's site with the transport and the approvals that exist today. Choose commodity_market where the input is bought freely from many sellers at a quoted price.

checks.question: Does a government body set the price of the critical input, or decide how much of it the party receives?
checks.assumption: The price and the volume of the critical input do not depend on a decision of government
checks.ask: Is the price of this input, or the amount you are allotted, set by a government body? For example a regulated tariff, a quota or a levy.
checks.note: A price set by the state can be low today. The test is whether a decree, a budget or a change of policy can raise it or cut the allocation while the loan is outstanding.

leads_to.reason: The rule that sets the price or the allocation, and how it can change, is examined there

checks.question: Has the supply of the critical input been cut, reduced or suspended in the last 24 months, even for a short time?
checks.assumption: The critical input has reached the party without interruption over the last 24 months
checks.ask: Has this input been cut, reduced or suspended at any time in the last two years, even briefly? Please include partial cuts.
checks.note: The party has a reason to understate this. Compare its answer with production volumes against capacity, and with what the supplier or the press reported. If the search finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when.

checks.question: Is there a court case, a dispute with an authority or a regulatory proceeding, pending or threatened, that could change the price the party pays for the critical input or stop its supply?
checks.assumption: No dispute or proceeding threatens the price or the supply of the critical input
checks.ask: Is there any court case, disputed levy or regulatory proceeding that affects what you pay for this input, or whether you receive it?
checks.note: If the search finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when.

leads_to.reason: The amount at stake and the likely outcome are examined with the party's other disputes

checks.question: What limits the effect on the party of a rise in the price of the critical input?
checks.assumption: A contract or a hedge limits what a rise in the price of the critical input costs the party
checks.why: With none of these, a rise in the price of the input reaches the party's margin at once and in full.
checks.ask: What limits the effect of a price rise on you: a price fixed in your supply contract, sales contracts that pass the rise on to your customers, or a hedge?
checks.note: Name only what is in a signed contract or a hedge confirmation, and say until when it runs and what share of the party's need it covers. A price fixed in a signed contract counts, also where the supplier is a state body. A tariff that an authority can change by its own decision does not. What protects the supply itself is asked in OBS_INPUT_MIT_002 and on the link to the supplier.

checks.question: Could the party keep producing within three months of losing the critical input, by switching to another input or to another plant?
checks.assumption: The party can keep producing without the critical input by switching within three months
checks.ask: If this input stopped tomorrow, could you keep producing within about three months, by switching fuel, feedstock or plant? Have you ever done so?
checks.note: Three months is a guide. A switch that has never been made is a plan: ask whether it has been done or tested, and what it costs.

checks.question: What share of the party's operating earnings comes from operations that do not need the critical input or its supplier?
checks.assumption: Most of the party's earnings come from operations that do not need the critical input
checks.why: Where less than half of the earnings comes from elsewhere, what is left when the input stops is unlikely to carry the party's fixed costs and its debt service. Half is a guide: the real measure is whether the rest covers debt service.
checks.ask: Of your operating earnings, roughly what share comes from plants or business lines that do not rely on this input?

indicators.title: Operations
indicators.claim: The party can keep producing and delivering at the volume and quality its projections assume.

matters_more_when.reason: A manufacturer earns only while its plant runs
The asset that secures the loan is also the one that earns the money to repay it
Repayment rests on a volume that the party has not yet reached

look_again_when.reason: An engineer's report can change the view of capacity and of the weak points
New projections can assume a different volume

checks.question: What share of its production or delivery capacity did the party use over the last full financial year?
checks.why: Capacity in use cuts both ways. High use leaves no room for the growth in the projections without new investment. Low use means that fixed costs are spread over little output.
checks.ask: How much could your plant or fleet produce or deliver in a year, and how much did it produce or deliver last year?
checks.note: Say what capacity is measured in (tonnes, units, hours, beds, vehicles), and whether it is the capacity the plant was designed for or the best output it has reached in a full year.

checks.question: Can the party's existing plant, equipment and staff produce the highest yearly volume in the projections, counting new capacity only where its cost and funding are in the same projections?
checks.assumption: The capacity that the projections need is in place, or is paid for in the plan
checks.ask: What is the highest yearly volume in your projections, and what would have to be added to the plant, the fleet or the staff to reach it?
checks.note: Compare with the best output reached in a full year, not with the capacity the plant was designed for.

leads_to.reason: The volumes in the projections then have to be cut, or the missing investment added

checks.question: Would the loss of one site, one production line or one machine stop more than half of the party's output for longer than a month?
checks.assumption: No single site, line or machine carries most of the party's output
checks.ask: If you lost your main site, line or machine tomorrow, how much of your output would stop, and for how long?
checks.note: Half and a month are guides. Think of fire, flood and breakdown, and of the time it takes to have a replacement delivered and running.

leads_to.reason: The condition of that one asset then decides the party's output
Cover for the asset and for lost profit counts most where everything hangs on one asset

checks.question: In the last 24 months, did a failure of power, water or transport (grid outages, a water shortage, a closed road, port or rail line) stop or cut the party's production or deliveries for more than a week in total?
checks.assumption: Failures of power, water or transport have not cut the party's production or deliveries
checks.ask: In the last two years, on how many days did you stop or slow production or deliveries because power, water or transport failed?
checks.note: A week in total is a guide. The party has a reason to understate this: compare its answer with production records and with what stand-by power and fuel have cost. Where the utility is itself the party's critical input, OBS_INPUT_005 asks about the same events.

checks.question: In any of the last three financial years, did the party's output or deliveries fall short of its own budget for that year by more than about a tenth?
checks.assumption: The party has produced and delivered what it planned in each of the last three years
checks.ask: For each of the last three years, what volume did you budget and what volume did you produce or deliver?
checks.if_unknown: A party that cannot set its output against its own budget gives the lender no record to hold the projections against.
checks.note: A tenth is a guide. Record the cause of each shortfall: it points at the topic to look at next.

checks.question: In the last three years, because of quality or safety, was a product of the party recalled, a whole batch or shipment rejected by a customer, the product taken off a customer's list, or its sale stopped by an authority?
checks.assumption: The party's products have met the quality and safety that its customers and the authorities require
checks.ask: In the last three years, has a product of yours been recalled, sent back in bulk, taken off a customer's list or stopped by an authority?
checks.note: If the search finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when. For an agribusiness, border rejections and lost certificates are asked in OBS_AGRI_007.

checks.question: Does the party's production depend on a plant that someone else owns or runs, or on a brand, a technology or a franchise that it uses under licence from someone else?
checks.assumption: The party owns or controls the plant, the technology and the brands it produces with
checks.ask: Do you produce in a plant that someone else owns or runs for you? Do you make or sell your products under someone else's brand, technology or franchise?
checks.note: A permit from an authority is not meant here: those are asked under Licences and regulation. Record who the other party is and when its contract or licence ends.

leads_to.reason: The lease, the operating contract or the licence is then a contract the party cannot afford to lose

checks.question: Does the party have a second site or line, or a back-up (stand-by power, a second water source, another route or a contract manufacturer), that could carry at least half of its normal output within a month of a failure?
checks.assumption: A second site or a back-up can carry at least half of the party's output when the main one fails
checks.ask: If your main site or your power, water or transport failed, where would you produce, and how much could you produce there within a month?
checks.note: Half and a month are guides. A back-up that has never carried production is a plan: ask when it last did. Insurance for a site or line that is lost is asked in OBS_OPS_MIT_002.

checks.question: Do property and business interruption policies in force cover the cost of rebuilding the site or line as new and the gross profit lost for as long as the rebuilding would take?
checks.assumption: Insurance pays for rebuilding the site or line and for the profit lost meanwhile
checks.ask: What are the sums insured for your main site or line and for lost profit, and for how many months does the cover for lost profit run? How long would it take to rebuild and restart?
checks.note: Both parts must hold for a yes. Set the sum insured against the cost of rebuilding as new, not against book value. Set the months of cover for lost profit against the time it would take to rebuild, with the delivery of the machines. Insurance pays money. It does not keep the customers who went elsewhere while the plant stood still.

leads_to.reason: The cover counts only if the policies are in force, the peril is not excluded and the insurer can pay

indicators.title: Revenue and customers
indicators.claim: No single customer, contract or product, if lost or left unpaid, would stop the party from servicing its debt.

matters_more_when.reason: Repayment rests on contracts, so the customers behind those contracts carry the loan
A single project usually sells one product to one buyer or one market

look_again_when.reason: New accounts show another year of revenue, the customers behind it and what they still owe
A new or changed sales contract changes how much revenue is fixed and who owes it

checks.question: Does the party earn revenue from sales today?
checks.why: Opens the topic. A business with no revenue yet is a different deal: its customers are judged from signed contracts and a market study, not from a sales record. OBS_BUYER_CONC_001 and OBS_REV_008 are asked either way.
checks.ask: Does the company earn revenue from selling goods or services today? A yes or no is enough to start with.

leads_to.reason: With no sales record, the case for future revenue rests on the feasibility work

checks.question: Does any single customer bring in about a tenth or more of the party's revenue, or would it under contracts already signed?
checks.why: A customer of this size has to be in the structure, where its own ability and obligation to pay are examined. A yes does not go against the claim. Whether the party could lose its largest customer is tested in OBS_REV_008.
checks.ask: Is there a customer that brings in a tenth or more of your sales, or that will once a signed contract starts? If so, who is it and what share does it bring?
checks.note: A tenth is a guide, not a gate. Listed companies that report under IFRS disclose reliance on a customer of that size (IFRS 8), so look for that note in their accounts. Count customers under common control as one. This check does not hang on OBS_REV_001: a business with no revenue yet can already depend on one buyer.

leads_to.reason: The customer's own ability and obligation to pay then decide part of the party's revenue

checks.question: If the largest customer stopped buying and its volume were not replaced for twelve months, would the party's cash flow still cover its debt service?
checks.assumption: The party can lose its largest customer for a year and still service its debt
checks.why: The claim is about what the loss of one customer would do to debt service, not about how large the customer is.
checks.ask: If your largest customer stopped buying tomorrow, how much of its volume could you sell elsewhere within a year, and which costs could you cut?
checks.if_unknown: Until this is worked out, nobody knows whether the loan hangs on one customer.
checks.note: Twelve months is a guide. Take out the revenue from that customer and only the costs that would fall with it within the year. Use the debt service of the first full year of repayment, this loan included. Count customers under common control as one. Where the party sells its whole output to one buyer, the answer is no. The test does not wait for the terms of the loan. If the answer already goes against the assumption on the debt the party owes today, record it now and say that it is before the new loan. Answer again when the terms are known.

checks.question: Do the three largest customers together bring in more than half of the party's revenue?
checks.assumption: The party would keep most of its revenue if it lost its three largest customers
checks.ask: What share of last year's sales came from your three largest customers? A list of sales by customer would answer this.
checks.if_unknown: Without sales by customer, nobody can say how much revenue one lost account would take with it.
checks.note: Half is a guide. Count customers under common control as one.

checks.question: Does one product, or one market (a country or a kind of customer), bring in more than half of the party's gross profit?
checks.assumption: The party's gross profit does not hang on one product or one market
checks.ask: Which product, and which market, earns you the most gross profit, and what share of the total is it?
checks.note: Half is a guide. Measure gross profit, not revenue: a product can be a small part of sales and most of the profit.

leads_to.reason: The outlook for that one product or market then decides the party's revenue

checks.question: By what percentage a year did the party's revenue change, on average, over the last three full financial years?
checks.assumption: The party's revenue has not fallen over the last three years
checks.why: Zero is where revenue turns from growing to shrinking. Revenue that has fallen over three years means that customers, volume or price are already being lost.
checks.ask: What were your sales in each of the last three financial years?
checks.note: Record each year as well as the average, since one bad year can hide in it. Where inflation is high, measure in volume or in a stable currency: growth below inflation is a fall. With fewer than three full years, use the years there are and say so.

checks.question: Is revenue in the party's strongest quarter of the year regularly at least one and a half times revenue in its weakest quarter?
checks.why: Seasonal revenue means that cash and borrowing swing through the year. Debt, liquidity and repayment dates are then read against the low season, not against the year-end.
checks.ask: Do your sales peak in certain months? Monthly or quarterly sales for the last two years would show it.
checks.note: One and a half times is a guide.

leads_to.reason: Stock, receivables and borrowing peak with the season
Cash is thinnest just before the season pays

checks.question: What share of the party's receivables is owed by government bodies (unpaid sales to the state, subsidies, tax and duty refunds)?
checks.assumption: The party does not wait on government bodies for a large part of what it is owed
checks.why: In many countries government bodies pay late when their budgets are tight, and enforcing a claim against them can be slow. At about a fifth of receivables, a delay of some months takes a large part of the party's working capital. A fifth is a guide.
checks.ask: How much of what you are owed is owed by government bodies: unpaid sales to state bodies, subsidies, tax or duty refunds? How old are those balances?
checks.note: Count all receivables, not only trade receivables: tax and subsidy claims often sit under other receivables. Record how long the balances have been outstanding.

checks.question: What share of a year's revenue has the party collected from customers before delivery (advances received, contract liabilities)?
checks.why: A prepayment is a debt owed in goods. It funds the business for as long as orders keep coming. When they stop, the party has to deliver or repay with no new advances to fund it, and customers that have prepaid stand beside the lender as creditors.
checks.ask: Do customers pay you before delivery? How much do you hold in customer advances, at the year-end and at the highest point in the year?
checks.note: Take the balance at its highest point in the year where it swings, and say which date it is for.

checks.question: What share of the party's trade receivables is backed by a letter of credit, a bank guarantee, credit insurance or collateral?
checks.assumption: Most of what customers owe the party is backed by a bank, an insurer or collateral
checks.why: Where less than half is backed, most of the loss from a customer that does not pay stays with the party. Half is a guide.
checks.ask: Of the money customers owe you, what share is covered by a letter of credit, a bank guarantee, credit insurance or collateral?
checks.note: This protects what customers already owe. It does not replace the sales that a lost customer would have brought.

indicators.title: Owners and control
indicators.claim: The people who ultimately own and control the party are known, up to natural persons, and no one stands behind them unseen.

matters_more_when.reason: A special-purpose company has no record of its own: it is only as well known as those behind it
In a group the chain has more steps, and each step is a place where an owner can stay out of sight

look_again_when.reason: A new register can show a transfer of shares
A new extract can show a holder or a director who was not there before
A person who controls without owning changes who is behind the party

checks.question: Who holds the party's shares directly?
checks.why: Opens the chain. Each holder that is entered as a party is asked the same question in turn, until the chain ends at natural persons, at a state or at a listed company with no large holder.
checks.ask: Who holds your shares directly: people in their own name, companies, a trust, or someone who holds them for another person? A copy of the shareholder register would answer this.
checks.note: Give every kind that applies. Enter each holder above the lender's threshold as a party with an 'owns' link, so that it gets these checks itself. For a party that is a natural person, answer party_is_a_person: the chain ends there.

checks.question: Has the party given the lender its whole chain of ownership in writing, step by step and with the share held at each step, up to natural persons?
checks.assumption: The party has disclosed its whole chain of ownership, up to natural persons
checks.ask: Please give us your ownership chain in writing: who owns you, who owns them, and so on up to the people at the top, with the percentage held at each step.
checks.if_unknown: Until the chain is disclosed, the checks on the owners cannot start.
checks.note: A chain may end at a state, or at a company listed on a regulated exchange with no large holder. Say where it ends. Whether the disclosure is true is tested by OBS_BO_002.

checks.question: Has every natural person who ultimately owns or controls the party above the lender's threshold been identified, with the identity checked against an identity document and each step of the chain against a register or a registry extract?
checks.assumption: Every natural person who ultimately owns or controls the party above the lender's threshold is identified and verified
checks.note: Common practice sets the threshold at a quarter of the shares or votes. Many lenders set it lower, and lower still where the risk is higher: use the lender's own. Where no one is above it, identify the person who in fact controls the party, or failing that its most senior manager. For a party that is a natural person, the question is whether that person's own identity has been checked. Use extracts no more than about twelve months old. A holder or a holding that differs from what the party declared, or a transfer agreed but not registered, is a no.

checks.question: Is any step in the chain between the party and its ultimate owners held through a nominee, a trustee, a foundation or bearer shares?
checks.assumption: Every holder in the chain holds its shares for itself and in its own name
checks.ask: Does anyone in your ownership chain hold shares for someone else, as a nominee or as a trustee? If so, for whom?
checks.if_unknown: A nominee or a trust that is not disclosed hides the owner the other checks are meant to reach.

checks.question: Can the party give a business, legal or tax reason for every company and every country in the chain between it and its ultimate owners?
checks.assumption: Every step in the chain is there for a reason the party can state
checks.ask: Why is each holding company in your chain there, and why in that country?
checks.note: A company in a country with no tie to the business, to the owners or to the financing needs a reason of its own. "For tax" is a reason only if the party can say which tax and how.

leads_to.reason: A step with no stated reason is often there for tax: see what it saves and whether that holds

checks.question: Does anyone who is not on the shareholder register direct the party's decisions in practice: a relative of the owners, a former owner, a financier, or another person whose instructions the directors follow?
checks.assumption: The party is run by its registered owners and the people they have appointed, and by no one behind them
checks.ask: Is there anyone outside the shareholder register whose agreement is needed for the big decisions, or who gives instructions to the directors?
checks.note: Signs are a director who cannot answer for the business, a power of attorney over the shares or the bank accounts, a lender whose consent is needed for everything, or a name that people in the market give as the owner. If the search finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when.

checks.question: Is the person behind each nominee, trust or foundation named, and is the arrangement shown by its own document (a nominee agreement, a trust deed, the foundation's statutes)?
checks.assumption: The lender can see through each nominee, trust or foundation to the people behind it
checks.note: For a trust, name the settlor, the trustees, the protector if there is one, and the beneficiaries. Each person so named is entered as a party.

indicators.title: Board
indicators.claim: The party's large decisions (borrowing, large investments, dealings with its owners) need the approval of a body that has at least one member independent of management and of the main shareholder, and that body sees the party's figures at least every quarter.

matters_more_when.reason: In an operating business the board is the main check on the people who run it
A shareholder has no covenants: the board is where it is heard

matters_less_when.reason: A special-purpose company often has no working board: the sponsor and the project agreements do the overseeing

look_again_when.reason: New minutes show what the board was asked and what it decided
A change of directors can remove the one who was independent

checks.question: Does the party have a board of directors, or a supervisory board, that meets as a body of its own and is not simply its management?
checks.why: Opens the topic. Without a board, OBS_BOARD_006 asks who oversees management in its place.
checks.ask: Does your company have a board of directors that meets separately from the management team?

checks.question: Does the board have at least one member who is not an employee of the party, is not a shareholder nor a shareholder's relative or nominee, and does no other business with the party?
checks.assumption: At least one member of the board is independent of management and of the shareholders
checks.ask: Is any member of your board independent: not an employee, not a shareholder or related to one, and with no other business with the company?
checks.note: A director named by another lender or by a financial investor counts, if there is no other tie. Record how many members the board has and how many of them are executives.

checks.question: Did the board meet at least four times in each of the last two financial years?
checks.assumption: The board meets at least once a quarter, so that it knows the business between year-ends
checks.note: Four a year is a guide. A meeting counts if a quorum was present and minutes were kept.

checks.question: Are minutes kept of every board meeting, signed by the chair, and do they record what was decided and who voted against?
checks.assumption: What the board decides, and who disagreed, is on record
checks.ask: Could we see the minutes of the board meetings of the last two years? Sensitive passages can be blacked out.

checks.question: In the last three years, has the board, or the body that oversees management in its place, turned down, sent back or changed a proposal from management or from the main shareholder?
checks.why: Shows whether the approval of the board is more than a formality.
checks.ask: Can you give an example from the last three years where the board did not approve what management or the main shareholder proposed, or approved it only after changes?
checks.note: Read the minutes themselves. A board that approved every proposal as tabled for three years has not been tested, or does not test. This check does not hang on OBS_BOARD_001.

checks.question: Does another body oversee management in the board's place: a supervisory or advisory committee, a partners' meeting, or the board of the parent?
checks.assumption: Where the party has no board, another body oversees its management
checks.ask: As there is no board, who reviews what management does, and how often?
checks.note: A body counts if it can refuse a proposal and has someone on it who does not report to the manager it oversees.

indicators.title: Bank: supervision and governance
indicators.claim: The supervisor has no open concern about the institution, and its own risk control is independent of the people who make the loans and of those who own it.

matters_more_when.reason: A bank that belongs to a group is under pressure to lend to its sister companies
A supervisor usually acts before the accounts show the trouble

look_again_when.reason: A new letter, inspection report or order from the supervisor changes where the institution stands with it
The related-party note and the auditor's remarks show insider lending at a new date

checks.question: What is the institution's standing with its prudential supervisor today?
checks.assumption: The supervisor has placed no special measure on the institution
checks.flag_when: is enhanced_monitoring or corrective_action or conservatorship
checks.why: Each of the three means that the supervisor has seen something it does not accept. It has ordered closer reporting, imposed a plan with deadlines, or put its own people in charge. A supervisor sees figures that a lender does not, and it usually acts before the accounts show the trouble. An institution without a supervisor is not flagged, but nobody inspects it on the lender's behalf.
checks.ask: Where do you stand with your supervisor today? Are you under ordinary supervision, or has the supervisor asked for closer reporting, agreed a corrective plan with you, or taken any other special measure?
checks.note: The options: normal is ordinary supervision with no special measure. enhanced_monitoring is more frequent reporting or inspection ordered for this institution. corrective_action is a plan with deadlines, agreed with the supervisor or imposed by it. conservatorship means the supervisor or its appointee runs the institution. not_supervised means there is no prudential supervisor, as for some microfinance and leasing companies. An institution under a measure may not be free to say so. Search the supervisor's published decisions as well. If the search finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when.

leads_to.reason: An institution outside prudential supervision still needs a licence to lend, and that indicator asks whether it holds one

checks.question: In the last three years, has the supervisor (or, where there is none, the licensing authority) fined the institution, restricted its business, or ordered it in writing to correct a breach of the rules on capital, liquidity, lending limits, provisioning or money-laundering controls?
checks.assumption: In the last three years the supervisor has found no breach that it met with a fine, a restriction or a written order
checks.ask: In the last three years, has your supervisor fined you, limited what you may do, or written to you with an order to correct something? If so, what was it about, and is it closed?
checks.note: Remarks in a routine inspection that carry no deadline and no penalty are not meant. Ask for the last inspection report and the institution's reply to it. If a search of the supervisor's published decisions finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when.

checks.question: Do the institution's loans and guarantees to its shareholders, directors and managers, and to parties connected with them, exceed the limit its regulator sets for such lending?
checks.assumption: Lending to insiders stays within the limit the regulator sets
checks.ask: How much have you lent to your shareholders, directors and managers, and to companies connected with them? What limit does your regulator set, and how do you decide who is connected?
checks.note: Where no regulatory limit applies, take a tenth of the institution's capital as a guide and say so. The related-party note in the audited accounts gives the total. Ask how the institution decides who is connected, because a narrow definition keeps the figure low. Whether insiders borrow on easier terms than others is asked in Related parties.

leads_to.reason: Lending to insiders above the limit takes value out of the institution, and that indicator asks on what terms and whether it can be called back

checks.question: Does a risk committee of the board meet at least once a quarter and keep minutes, and does the head of risk report to it directly, not through the people who make the loans?
checks.assumption: Risk is overseen at board level, apart from the people who make the loans
checks.ask: Do you have a risk committee of the board? How often did it meet last year, and to whom does your head of risk report?
checks.note: A charter alone is not enough. Read the minutes of the last four meetings for who attended, what was reported and what was decided. In a small institution the whole board may do this work. Then answer for the board, and say so.

checks.question: Can a shareholder, a director or the chief executive approve a loan alone, or overturn a refusal by the credit committee or the risk function?
checks.assumption: No single person can push a loan through against the credit process
checks.ask: Who can approve a loan, and up to what amount? In the last two years, was any loan approved although the risk function had advised against it?
checks.note: Read the approval limits in the credit policy, then test them against practice. Ask for the loans of the last two years that were approved against the opinion of the risk function, and who signed them. Approval of large loans by the board as a body is normal. What is meant is one person deciding.

checks.question: Has the supervisor confirmed in writing that the measure is lifted or the finding closed, or that the institution is meeting each deadline of the agreed plan?
checks.assumption: The supervisor has confirmed that its concern is resolved, or is being resolved on schedule
checks.note: The confirmation must come from the supervisor. The institution's own account of it is not a confirmation.

indicators.title: Internal controls
indicators.claim: No one person can move the party's money or change its books unseen.

matters_more_when.reason: A trader moves large sums on thin margins: one unseen payment can cost a year's profit
A business that grows fast outgrows controls that rested on the owner seeing everything

look_again_when.reason: A new letter from the auditor shows which weaknesses are open now
A failure shows that a control did not work as described

checks.question: Does the party have written rules that say who may commit it, who may approve a payment and who may post to the books, with limits by amount?
checks.assumption: The party's rules for commitments, payments and entries in the books are written down
checks.ask: Do you have written rules on who may sign contracts, approve payments and make entries in the accounts, and up to what amount? Could we have a copy?

checks.question: Are ordering, approving, paying and recording done by different people, so that nobody can both make a payment and enter it in the books?
checks.assumption: Whoever makes a payment cannot also approve it or record it
checks.ask: Who orders, who approves, who pays and who books a purchase? Are these different people?
checks.note: Include who can change supplier bank details and who reconciles the bank accounts. In a small finance team, look at what the owner or an outside accountant checks each month.

checks.question: Does every payment above a set amount need two people to release it at the bank, with no exception for the owner or the chief executive?
checks.assumption: No single person, the owner included, can release a large payment alone
checks.ask: Above what amount does a payment need two signatures? Is there anyone who can sign alone without limit?
checks.note: Record the amount. Ask for the bank's list of signatories: it shows what the bank will accept, which may differ from what the rules say.

checks.question: Does someone who does not report to the head of finance check at least once a year that the controls work: an internal auditor, an outside firm or an audit committee?
checks.assumption: Someone independent of the finance function checks that the controls work
checks.ask: Do you have an internal audit, in-house or by an outside firm? To whom does it report, and could we see its last report?

checks.question: In the last three years, has the party had a fraud, an unauthorised payment, or an unexplained loss of cash or stock?
checks.assumption: The controls have held: no fraud, unauthorised payment or unexplained loss in the last three years
checks.ask: In the last three years, has there been a fraud, a payment nobody had approved, or a loss of cash or stock you could not explain? Please include cases that are settled.
checks.if_unknown: If neither the auditor's letters nor the board minutes have been seen, the party's no is its own word.
checks.note: A party that says yes is believed.

checks.question: Does the auditor's latest management letter, or the latest internal audit report, list weaknesses in the controls over cash, payments or the books that are still open?
checks.assumption: The weaknesses the auditors found in the controls over money and the books are closed
checks.ask: Could we have the auditor's last two management letters, with your replies?
checks.if_unknown: If no management letter has been seen, ask the auditor whether one was issued. That none was issued is an answer. That none was shown is not.
checks.note: A point that comes back in two letters running is open, whatever the reply says.

checks.question: Has the cause of the failure been found and the control changed, and has the auditor or a later internal audit confirmed that the change works?
checks.assumption: The gap behind the failure is closed, and someone independent has confirmed it
checks.note: That the person involved has left does not close the gap. The control has to be different.

indicators.title: Integrity record
indicators.claim: Nothing in the record of the party or of the people who own and run it points to fraud, corruption or money laundering, and the party has its own rules against bribery.

matters_more_when.reason: A financial institution handles other people's money: its controls against money laundering are part of its licence
A shareholder is tied to the party's name for longer and more closely than a lender

look_again_when.reason: A new search can find a report or a case that was not there before
A letter or an order from an authority can open or close a matter

checks.question: In the last ten years, has a court or an authority fined or penalised the party, or debarred it from public contracts or from a development bank's financing, for fraud, bribery, money laundering, tax evasion or a breach of sanctions?
checks.assumption: No court or authority has penalised or debarred the party for a financial crime in the last ten years
checks.ask: In the last ten years, has a court, a regulator, a tax authority or a development bank fined, penalised or debarred you for fraud, bribery, money laundering, tax evasion or a breach of sanctions? Please include matters that were settled.
checks.if_unknown: A record that has not been disclosed and cannot be checked is not a clean record.
checks.note: Ten years is a guide: an older matter that is still talked about counts. A settlement without admission counts. A criminal case against a person goes under OBS_KYC_008. If the search finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when.

checks.question: Has any director or senior manager of the party, or the party itself where it is a person, been convicted of fraud, bribery, money laundering or another crime of dishonesty, or is any of them charged with one or under criminal investigation for one?
checks.assumption: None of the people who direct or manage the party has been convicted of a crime of dishonesty, is charged with one or is under investigation for one
checks.ask: Has any director or senior manager ever been convicted of fraud, bribery, money laundering or a similar offence? Is any of them charged or under investigation now?
checks.note: A party that says yes is believed. Owners and controllers are parties of their own and get this check themselves. If the search finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when.

checks.question: Has the lender searched the press, the court records and the development banks' lists of debarred firms and persons for the party, its directors and its senior managers, in the countries and the languages in which they are active?
checks.assumption: The public record of the party and of the people who direct it has been searched
checks.if_unknown: Without a search, the record is only what the party says it is.
checks.note: A search in one language of a party that works in another has not been done. Owners and controllers are parties of their own and get this check themselves. If the search finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when.

checks.question: Did the search find an allegation of fraud, corruption, money laundering or another financial crime against the party, its directors or its senior managers that no court or authority has yet ruled on: a press report, a civil claim, a whistleblower's account?
checks.assumption: No public allegation of financial crime hangs over the party or the people who direct it
checks.note: Record who made the allegation, when, and what became of it. One report in a source with a known grudge weighs less than several that do not depend on each other, but it is still recorded. A penalty or a conviction goes under OBS_KYC_003 or OBS_KYC_008. If the search finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when.

checks.question: Does the party have a written code of conduct or policy against bribery, approved by its board or its owners, with a named person who answers for it and a way for staff to report a breach without going through their own manager?
checks.assumption: The party has written rules against bribery, someone who answers for them and a way to report a breach
checks.ask: Do you have a written code of conduct or a policy against bribery? Who answers for it, and how can a member of staff report a breach?
checks.note: All three parts are needed for a yes. In a small business the person can be an owner or a senior manager beside other duties, and the way to report can be a named director or an outside address. What counts is that a report can reach someone other than the manager it concerns.

checks.question: Does the party have a written policy against money laundering, approved by its board or its owners, that says how it identifies whom it deals with, what it does about a suspicious payment and who is told?
checks.assumption: The party has written rules against money laundering that its board or owners have approved
checks.ask: Do you have a written policy against money laundering? Could we have a copy, with the date on which the board approved it?

checks.question: Does the party check who its customers, agents and other main counterparties are before it deals with them, and keep the record?
checks.assumption: The party knows whom it deals with and can show it
checks.ask: Before you take on a new customer, agent or large supplier, what do you check about them, and where is that kept?
checks.note: For a financial institution this is the identification of customers that its regulator requires. Ask to see the file of one recent counterparty.

checks.question: How far has the matter been dealt with: closed by the authority or by an independent inquiry, those responsible removed, and the weakness behind it put right?
checks.assumption: The matter is closed, those responsible have gone and the weakness behind it is put right
checks.why: A matter is behind the party only when all three are done. Anything less leaves the lender exposed to the same people or to the same gap.
checks.note: full_remediation: all three are done and shown. partial_remediation: some are done, or the work is still under way. none: nothing is done, or nothing is shown. For an allegation, an independent inquiry that found no basis for it is full_remediation.

indicators.title: Litigation and disputes
indicators.claim: No lawsuit or investigation could take away the cash or the assets the lender counts on.

matters_more_when.reason: The creditors of a business in distress go to court before they come to the table
Without security the lender stands in line beside whoever wins a claim

look_again_when.reason: New accounts can show a new provision or a new contingent liability
A new letter from the lawyers can change the amounts and the odds
A new case has to be measured against what the party can pay

checks.question: Is a court case, an arbitration or a written claim pending against the party?
checks.why: Opens the topic. A no is checked by OBS_LIT_007 against the registers and the accounts, and OBS_LIT_004 asks about investigations whatever the answer.
checks.ask: Is anyone suing you, or has anyone sent you a written claim? Please include arbitrations and cases you expect to win.

leads_to.reason: See whether a claim touches an asset that is to be given as security

checks.question: What is the total amount claimed against the party in all pending cases, with interest and costs?
checks.why: The starting figure. OBS_LIT_006 asks what it would mean if it had to be paid.
checks.ask: What is claimed in each pending case, and what do your lawyers say about each?
checks.note: Take the amount claimed, not the party's own view of what it will lose, and say at which date. List the cases one by one where there are more than one.

checks.question: If the party lost every pending case at the amount claimed, could it pay and still meet what it owes its lenders (and, for a guarantor, what it has guaranteed)?
checks.assumption: The party could lose every pending case and still pay its lenders
checks.note: This is the worst case, and it is meant to be. If the answer is no, OBS_LIT_003 and OBS_LIT_008 show how likely the loss is and who else would bear it.

checks.question: Do the latest audited accounts carry a provision for every case the party's lawyers expect it to lose, at the amount they expect?
checks.assumption: The accounts already carry the losses that the party's own lawyers expect
checks.ask: Which of the pending cases have you provided for in your accounts, and for how much?
checks.note: Set the lawyers' letter to the auditor beside the note on provisions and contingent liabilities. A case the lawyers call likely to be lost, with no provision, means that profit and equity are overstated by that amount.

checks.question: Is a regulator, a competition authority or a prosecutor investigating the party, or has one given notice that it will?
checks.assumption: No authority has an inquiry open that could end in a penalty or the loss of a licence
checks.ask: Is any authority looking into your company at the moment: a regulator, the competition authority, a prosecutor? A routine inspection with no findings does not count.
checks.note: This check does not hang on OBS_LIT_001. Tax audits and tax disputes are asked under OBS_TAX_005.

leads_to.reason: An inquiry into fraud, bribery or money laundering is also a matter of integrity
An inquiry by a regulator can put a licence at risk

checks.question: Does a search of the court and insolvency registers, a credit report or the lawyers' letter to the auditor show a case, a judgment or an attachment against the party that it had not mentioned?
checks.assumption: The party has told the lender of every case, judgment and attachment against it
checks.note: This check does not hang on OBS_LIT_001, so that the topic cannot close on one answer. Search where the party is registered and where its main assets are. If the search finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when.

checks.question: Is the amount at stake covered by insurance, or by an indemnity from someone able to pay it, and has the insurer or the giver of the indemnity confirmed cover for these cases in writing?
checks.assumption: Someone other than the party will pay if the cases are lost, and has said so in writing
checks.note: The letter has to come from the insurer or from whoever gave the indemnity. A policy that exists is not cover that has been confirmed: insurers reserve their rights. An indemnity is worth what its giver can pay.

indicators.title: Shareholders
indicators.claim: The party's shareholders are settled and agree on how it is run, and they take out no more than it earns.

matters_more_when.reason: As a shareholder the lender sits among the others and lives by what they have agreed
Shareholders of a business in distress fall out, and some take out what they still can

look_again_when.reason: A new or amended agreement changes who decides what
New accounts show what was paid out to shareholders in the year
A change of ownership brings shareholders who are not yet examined

checks.question: Does more than one shareholder have a say in how the party is run: a holding of about a tenth or more, a seat on the board or a right of veto?
checks.why: With one shareholder there is nobody to fall out with. With several, the lender needs to know how they decide and what happens when they disagree.
checks.note: A tenth is a guide. A family that votes together counts as one shareholder only if nothing shows that its members disagree.

checks.question: Are there circular or cross holdings: does the party, or a company it controls, hold shares in any of its own owners?
checks.assumption: No part of the party's shareholding is circular
checks.if_unknown: If the holdings cannot be drawn on one page with every line ending in a name, treat the answer as not known.

leads_to.reason: A chain of owners that runs in a circle does not end at a person

checks.question: Have the shareholders agreed in writing how they decide together, how shares may change hands and how a deadlock is broken (in a shareholders' agreement or in the articles)?
checks.assumption: The shareholders have written rules for deciding, for transfers of shares and for deadlock
checks.ask: Is there a shareholders' agreement? If so, could we have a copy?

checks.question: Do the shareholders' agreement or the articles give minority shareholders rights of their own: a veto on named decisions, a seat on the board, pre-emption, tag-along or protection against dilution?
checks.why: These rights cut both ways for a lender. They keep the majority from taking value out, and they can block a decision the loan needs, such as new security or new capital. Where the lender itself takes shares, they are its own protection.
checks.note: If yes, list the decisions that need the minority's consent, and see whether this financing is one of them.

leads_to.reason: The borrowing or the security may need the consent of a minority shareholder

checks.question: Is there now, or has there been in the last five years, a dispute among the party's shareholders, or between a shareholder and the party, that went to a lawyer, a court or an arbitrator, or that left a decision blocked?
checks.assumption: The shareholders have not been in dispute with each other or with the party in the last five years
checks.ask: Have the shareholders had a serious disagreement in the last five years, among themselves or with the company? What was it about, and how did it end?
checks.note: A party that says yes is believed. If the search finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when.

leads_to.reason: A dispute that reached a court or an arbitrator is a case with an amount at stake

checks.question: Are any of the party's shares pledged, charged or under an option in favour of someone other than the lender?
checks.assumption: No one else can take over the party's shares by enforcing a pledge or an option
checks.ask: Has any shareholder pledged its shares in the company, or given someone an option over them?
checks.note: Whoever enforces a pledge over the shares can end up as the owner, and the lender has no say in it. A pledge counts when its enforcement, alone or with a change that is already planned, could move control or a blocking stake. A smaller one is a no, and the reason gives its size. Where one company owns the party and is not itself asked this check, look up the chain as well. Record a pledge over the owner's own shares in the reason, and answer OBS_OWN_009 on whether its enforcement would change who controls the party. If the search finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when.

leads_to.reason: A pledge over the shares often means that the owner borrowed to pay for them

checks.question: Is a sale of shares, the entry of a new investor, a listing, a merger or a handover between generations planned or under way that would change who controls the party?
checks.assumption: Those who control the party today will control it for the life of the loan
checks.ask: Do the owners plan to sell, to bring in a new investor, to list the company or to hand over to the next generation during the life of the loan?
checks.note: Where one company owns the party and is not itself asked this check, look up the chain to the people or the listed company at the top. A share issue, or the enforcement of a pledge, that would take control from those who control the owner counts, and the reason says at which level the change sits.

leads_to.reason: The terms have to give the lender the right to leave when control changes

checks.question: Over the last three financial years taken together, did dividends, share buy-backs and loans or advances to shareholders exceed the party's profit after tax?
checks.assumption: Over the last three years the shareholders took out no more than the party earned
checks.note: Take profit in cash terms: leave out gains on revaluation. Count fees and other payments to shareholders that are not the price of a service at market rates.

leads_to.reason: Money also leaves through contracts with the shareholders and their other companies

indicators.title: Political exposure
indicators.claim: Where a politically exposed person owns, controls or directs the party, the wealth behind that person's stake is explained and the business does not depend on that person's office.

matters_more_when.reason: The business lives on a licence and a tariff that the state grants
The business lives on a concession or a contract that the state grants

look_again_when.reason: A new screening can show a person who has taken or left office
A political tie that is newly found has not been examined

checks.question: Is the party, or any of its directors or senior managers, a politically exposed person: someone who holds or has held a prominent public office, or a close relative or a close associate of such a person?
checks.why: To be politically exposed is not a fault. It decides how closely the lender has to look. A no is checked by OBS_PEP_006 against a screening.
checks.ask: Does any owner, director or senior manager hold a prominent public office, or has one held such an office? Is any of them a close relative or a close business associate of someone who does?
checks.note: Prominent public office means, for example, a minister, a member of parliament, a senior judge, a general, a senior official of a ruling party or the head of a state-owned company. How long a person counts after leaving office is set by the lender's own rule. Owners and controllers are parties of their own and get this check themselves.

leads_to.reason: Where the person's money comes from is part of the closer look

checks.question: What is the tie: does the person hold the office, or is the person a close relative or a close associate of the one who does?
checks.why: The closer the tie and the higher the office, the closer the look. Name the person, the office and the years in it.

checks.question: Did a screening against a database of politically exposed persons, or a search of public sources, find a political tie that the party had not declared?
checks.assumption: The party has declared every political tie of its own, of its directors and of its senior managers
checks.if_unknown: Without a screening, the answer to OBS_PEP_001 rests on the party's word alone.
checks.note: This check does not hang on OBS_PEP_001, so that the topic cannot close on what the party says. If the search finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when.

checks.question: Does the business that the lender finances hold a licence, a concession, a public contract, a subsidy or a loan from a state bank that the person's office grants, renews or can influence?
checks.assumption: The business does not depend on anything that the politically exposed person's office can give or take away
checks.note: Look at who signed the licence or the contract, and who decides on its renewal. An office that the person left counts while the people the person appointed still decide.

leads_to.reason: A licence that came through a political tie can go when the tie goes

checks.question: Has the lender examined the person more closely and put the result on file: where the person's wealth comes from, what the person receives from the party, and the approval of the lender's senior management?
checks.assumption: The lender has examined the person's wealth and role, and its senior management has approved the relationship
checks.note: This closer look is often called enhanced due diligence. The file has to show all three parts.

checks.question: While the loan is outstanding, does the lender look again at least once a year at the person's office and at the party's dealings with it?
checks.assumption: The lender looks again at the political tie at least once a year
checks.note: Once a year is a guide. An election, a change of government or a new public contract is a reason to look at once.

checks.question: Was that licence, contract, subsidy or loan won in an open procedure (a public tender, or a published rule that applies to everyone), and has the lender seen the record of the award?
checks.assumption: What the business holds from the state was awarded in an open procedure, and the record shows it
checks.note: The record is the tender notice, the list of bidders and the decision. A direct award, or a tender with one bidder, is not an open procedure.

indicators.title: Sanctions
indicators.claim: Neither the party nor anyone who owns, controls or directs it is under sanctions, and its business does not deal with anyone who is.

look_again_when.reason: A new screening is run against the lists as they stand now, and lists change
A new holder has not been screened
