checks.question: Is the institution's net open position in foreign currency, all currencies taken together and with items off the balance sheet, above the limit its regulator sets or, where there is none, above about a fifth of its capital?
checks.assumption: A move in the exchange rate would cost the institution only a small part of its capital
checks.why: An open position turns a move in the exchange rate straight into a gain or a loss. A position that is closed in the accounts can still be open in fact, where loans in foreign currency went to borrowers who earn local currency. They stop paying when the local currency falls.
checks.ask: What is your net open position in foreign currency as a share of your capital, and what limit applies to it? What share of your foreign-currency loans went to borrowers who earn local currency?
checks.note: A fifth is a guide. Take the highest month-end of the last twelve months. Record what share of the loans in foreign currency went to borrowers without income in that currency. Where the loan under review is in foreign currency, work the position out again with it included.

checks.question: In the last three years, has the institution missed a payment to a lender, breached a financial covenant in a loan agreement, or asked a lender for a waiver or an extension?
checks.assumption: The institution has paid and performed as agreed under its own borrowings
checks.ask: In the last three years, was there any moment when a payment to one of your lenders was late, a financial covenant was not met, or you asked a lender for a waiver or for more time?
checks.note: An institution that says yes is believed. An institution that says no is believed once the accounts, a lender or a credit report bear it out. Deposits are not meant here.

checks.question: Is the institution admitted to a standing lending facility of its central bank, and does it hold unpledged assets today that the central bank accepts as collateral?
checks.assumption: The central bank would lend to the institution against assets it holds today
checks.ask: Can you borrow from the central bank when you need to? Against which assets, and have you done so in the last twelve months?
checks.note: Access in name is not enough. The collateral must be in hand and free. A central bank lends its own currency, so the facility does not answer a shortage of foreign currency. Record whether the institution has drawn on it in the last twelve months, and why. Frequent use is itself a sign of strain.

checks.question: Have the lenders concerned confirmed in writing that the breach is cured or waived?
checks.assumption: The lenders concerned have confirmed that the breach is cured or waived
checks.note: The letter must come from the lender concerned. The institution's own account of it is not a confirmation.

indicators.title: Currency risk
indicators.claim: A fall in the currency the party earns, against the currencies it owes and buys in, would not stop it from servicing its debt.

matters_more_when.reason: Primary producers often sell at prices set in a foreign currency and pay their costs in local currency
Manufacturers often buy imported inputs and sell at home
Imported equipment is usually priced in a foreign currency

look_again_when.reason: A new hedge, or one that has run off, changes how much of the exposure is covered
The currency of the proposed loan may have changed
The currency note and the exchange gains and losses show the exposure at a new date

checks.question: Does the party earn any of its revenue in a foreign currency, or at prices that are set in one?
checks.why: Opens the revenue side. A "no" is not the end of it. OBS_FX_008 and OBS_FX_CAPEX_001 are asked whatever the answer, and the currency note in the audited accounts shows whether the answer is right.
checks.ask: Do you earn revenue in a foreign currency, or sell at prices that follow one? A revenue breakdown by currency or a rough share is enough to start with.
checks.note: Foreign means any currency other than the one in which the party pays most of its costs.

checks.question: In which foreign currencies does the party earn revenue?
checks.why: Revenue covers a payment only in the same currency, or in one that moves with it.
checks.note: Where the answer is other, name the currency.

checks.question: What share of the party's revenue is earned in a foreign currency, or at prices set in one?
checks.why: The share says how much of the revenue can cover costs and debt in that currency.
checks.ask: What share of your revenue is in foreign currency, or at prices that follow one? A rough percentage is fine at this stage.

checks.question: Does the party pay any of its costs in a foreign currency, or at prices that follow one (imported inputs, fuel, freight, licence fees)?
checks.why: Opens the cost side. A party that sells only at home can still be hit through what it buys.
checks.ask: Do you pay for anything in a foreign currency, or at a price that goes up when the local currency falls? Think of imported raw materials, fuel, spare parts, freight and licence fees.
checks.if_unknown: A breakdown of costs by currency is not in the documents so far.

checks.question: What share of the party's input costs is imported, or priced at import parity so that it rises when the local currency falls?
checks.assumption: A fall in the local currency would raise only a small part of the party's input costs
checks.why: Inputs that follow the exchange rate cost more on the day the currency falls, while selling prices follow later or not at all. Above about a quarter of input costs, a fall of a fifth in the currency raises total input cost by 5 per cent or more, which many margins cannot carry. The figure is a guide carried over from earlier practice, and an institution can set its own.
checks.ask: Roughly what share of your input costs is imported, or priced off international markets even when billed in local currency (imported gas, fuel or raw materials, for example)?
checks.note: Inputs billed in local currency at a price that follows the import price count as imported.

checks.question: Is more than about a tenth of the party's debt, the proposed loan included, owed in a currency other than the one in which the party earns the cash flow that services it?
checks.assumption: No more than a small part of the party's debt is owed in a currency other than that of the cash flow that services it
checks.ask: Is any of your borrowing in a different currency from the income you repay it with? For example a loan in dollars or euros repaid from sales in local currency. How much is it, out of all your borrowing?
checks.note: A tenth is a guide to what matters. What counts is whether a fall of the earning currency would raise the party's debt service by an amount that matters against its cash flow. Where there is such debt but it stays below the guide, the answer is no: record the amount and its share of all debt in the reason. Go by the currency the cash is paid in. A price set in or linked to another currency but paid in local currency is a protection, not a match. OBS_FX_PASSTHROUGH_001 asks about it. The test does not wait for the terms of the loan. If the answer already goes against the assumption on the debt the party owes today, record it now and say that it is before the new loan. Answer again when the terms are known.

leads_to.reason: Debt owed in a foreign currency also has to be converted and transferred abroad
The currency of the loan is a term that can still be changed

checks.question: If the currency in which the party earns its cash flow fell against the currency of its debt by as much as in its worst twelve months of the last ten years, and the party raised its prices no faster than it did then, would its cash flow still cover the service of all its debt, the proposed loan included?
checks.assumption: The party can service its debt after a fall of its earning currency as deep as the worst of the last ten years
checks.why: A mismatch says only that a fall in the currency raises the debt service in the party's own money. The test is whether the cash flow carries a fall that has already happened once.
checks.if_unknown: Nobody knows how far the currency can fall before a payment is missed.
checks.note: Take the fall from published exchange rates and name the twelve months. Take the party's prices and volumes in those months from its own accounts where it was already trading. If no such case has been run, the check stays open. The test does not wait for the terms of the loan. If the answer already goes against the assumption on the debt the party owes today, record it now and say that it is before the new loan. Answer again when the terms are known.

leads_to.reason: The cash flow does not carry the debt once the currency has fallen

checks.question: Is any committed capital expenditure, or other large purchase commitment, priced in a currency other than that of the money set aside to pay for it?
checks.assumption: Capital expenditure and large purchase commitments are funded in the currency in which they are priced
checks.ask: Are any of your equipment orders, building contracts or other large purchases priced in a foreign currency? In which currency is the money that will pay for them?
checks.if_unknown: A fall in the currency between the order and the payment would leave the investment plan short of funds.

checks.question: When the local currency falls, can the party raise its selling prices within one quarter to recover the rise in its input costs and in its debt service (for example because its prices are set in or linked to the foreign currency)?
checks.assumption: The party recovers a currency-driven rise in its input costs and its debt service through its selling prices within one quarter
checks.why: Only a full recovery within a quarter keeps the margin and the cover of debt service whole. With a partial one, or with prices set by the state, the party carries the rest itself.
checks.ask: When a weaker currency raises your input costs and the cost of your foreign-currency debt, can you raise your selling prices to match within a quarter, fully or in part? Are your prices set in or linked to a foreign currency, or are they set or capped by the state?
checks.note: Look at what happened to the gross margin in the last year in which the currency fell sharply. That is better evidence than a price clause that has never been used.

checks.question: In each foreign currency, is the gap between what the party receives and what it pays in a year (costs, capital expenditure and debt service) smaller than about a fifth of its yearly operating cash flow?
checks.assumption: Receipts and payments in the same currency offset each other, so that only a small net amount is exposed
checks.ask: Do you have costs or debt in the same foreign currencies as your revenue? For each currency, how much do you receive and how much do you pay in a year?
checks.note: About a fifth is a guide. Take the year of the loan in which the gap is widest. The risk note in the audited accounts usually gives the net position in each currency.

checks.question: What share of the party's net foreign-currency exposure of the next twelve months is covered by hedging contracts (forwards, swaps or options)?
checks.assumption: Hedging contracts cover most of the party's net foreign-currency exposure of the next twelve months
checks.why: When half or less is hedged, at least half of any currency move still reaches the cash flow. Treasury policies commonly hedge between half and all of the committed exposure of the coming year. An institution can set its own point.
checks.ask: What part of your foreign-currency exposure for the next twelve months is hedged today, and with which contracts? Please share the confirmations or the bank's hedge report.
checks.note: Count only contracts that are signed. Where there are none, the answer is 0. The party's own figure needs the bank's confirmations behind it. A board-approved hedging policy shows that the cover will be kept up.

checks.question: Do the hedging contracts run for as long as the exposure they cover: for a loan in a foreign currency, to its final maturity?
checks.assumption: The hedges run for as long as the exposure they cover
checks.note: Where hedges are rolled over each year, the answer is no. The party then depends on being able to roll them, at a price nobody knows yet. Where there are no hedging contracts, the answer is no.

checks.question: Are the hedging contracts made under a signed master agreement with a supervised bank that is not part of the party's own group?
checks.assumption: The hedges are with a supervised bank outside the group, under a signed agreement
checks.note: Record the bank's rating where it has one. A hedge with a weak bank fails when the currency moves most. Where there are no hedging contracts, the answer is no.

indicators.title: Liquidity
indicators.claim: The party can pay everything that falls due in the next twelve months from its free cash, its committed credit lines and the cash its business brings in, without new borrowing, even in its weakest month.

matters_more_when.reason: A business in distress fails on the day it cannot pay, whatever its balance sheet says
A business that is not yet selling has no cash coming in, so cash and committed lines are all there is
A holding company's cash sits in its subsidiaries and reaches it only as dividends

look_again_when.reason: New monthly figures show the cash position at a new date
New or rescheduled debt changes what falls due in the next twelve months
A credit line that is signed, renewed or cancelled changes what the party can draw

checks.question: How much cash and bank deposits does the party hold today that it is free to use to pay its own debts?
checks.why: The starting figure. Cash that is pledged, blocked, held where it cannot be brought back, or held for others is left out. OBS_LIQ_008 tests whether it has been.
checks.ask: How much cash do you have in the bank today that you could use to pay a bill tomorrow? Please leave out anything that is pledged to a lender or held for someone else.
checks.note: Say which date and which currency. For a group, say which companies hold the cash.

checks.question: Does a month-by-month cash forecast for the next twelve months show the party paying everything that falls due (debt repayments and interest, taxes, wages, suppliers, committed capital spending and declared dividends) in every month, from its free cash, its undrawn committed credit lines and the cash its business brings in, without new borrowing?
checks.assumption: The party's free cash, committed lines and cash from its business cover what falls due in each of the next twelve months
checks.ask: Please send your cash forecast for the next twelve months, month by month, with every loan repayment, tax payment and capital spending shown.
checks.if_unknown: Without a monthly forecast nobody has shown that the party can pay through its weakest month. A year-end balance does not show it.
checks.note: Find the month in which cash is lowest, and record that month and the balance. Count a loan that falls due as a payment unless its renewal is signed. Count the proceeds of the loan under review only against the spending it is meant to pay for. Leave out credit lines that fail OBS_LIQ_003 and cash that fails OBS_LIQ_008. Take the cash from the business at what the lender's own base case expects, not at the party's budget.

checks.question: Is about a fifth or more of the cash in the party's balance sheet out of its reach: pledged or blocked in favour of a lender, held in a country or in a subsidiary from which it cannot be brought back, or held on behalf of customers or others?
checks.assumption: The cash in the party's balance sheet is the party's own to use
checks.note: A fifth is a guide. What counts is whether the party could still pay what falls due without that cash. Look in the notes to the accounts for restricted cash, in the loan agreements for reserve accounts and pledged accounts, and at which company and which country holds each balance.

checks.question: Is every undrawn credit line that the party counts on for the next twelve months committed: the bank is bound by a signed agreement to pay out on request, cannot cancel at will, and the line does not end within those twelve months?
checks.assumption: The credit lines the party counts on are committed, not merely available
checks.ask: Which credit lines could you draw on tomorrow, and up to what amount? Please send the agreement for each, so that we can see until when it runs and whether the bank can cancel it.
checks.note: Read the cancellation and review clauses of each line. An overdraft that is repayable on demand, or a line the bank renews each year at its own discretion, is not committed. Nor is a line the party cannot draw today, for example because a covenant is breached. A party that counts on no credit line is a yes. Say so, because it then pays from cash alone.

checks.question: In the last two years, has the party paid wages, taxes or suppliers late for lack of cash, or needed money from its owners or its bank at short notice to pay them?
checks.assumption: The party has had the cash to pay what fell due over the last two years
checks.ask: In the last two years, was there a month when wages, a tax payment or a supplier had to wait because the cash was not there, or when a shareholder or the bank had to step in at short notice?
checks.note: Late payments to lenders are asked in Existing debt (OBS_DEBT_008). A party that says yes is believed. A no is borne out by a tax clearance, the ageing list of payables and the bank statements.

leads_to.reason: A party that ran short of cash has often asked its lenders for more time as well

checks.question: Is the shortfall covered by money that is promised in writing and has not been counted: a signed undertaking by an owner to pay in cash, or a standby line signed with a bank?
checks.assumption: Money that is promised in writing covers the shortfall
checks.note: The promise must name an amount and say when it can be drawn. A statement that the owner stands behind the party is a no.

leads_to.reason: An owner's undertaking counts only as far as the lender can enforce it and the owner can pay

indicators.title: Interest rate and price risk
indicators.claim: A rise in interest rates, or a move in commodity prices against the party's stock and forward contracts, would not stop the party from servicing its debt.

matters_more_when.reason: A trader lives on the difference between two prices and finances its stock with short-term debt
A crop is bought in one season and sold over the year, at prices that move in between
A primary producer sells at the price the market gives on the day

look_again_when.reason: New debt, or debt that has been refinanced, changes the share that follows the market rate
A new hedge, or one that has run off, changes what is covered
The notes on derivatives and on stock show the positions at a new date

checks.question: What share of the party's debt, the proposed loan included, carries a floating rate or falls due for refinancing within twelve months?
checks.why: This is the debt whose cost follows the market. Short-term debt at a fixed rate counts, because it takes the new rate when it is rolled over.
checks.ask: How much of your borrowing is at a floating rate, and how much falls due within the next twelve months?

checks.question: If interest rates rose by three percentage points, would the party's operating cash flow of the last full year still cover the interest and the scheduled repayments on its debt as contracted, the proposed loan included and before any hedge?
checks.assumption: The party can service its debt after a rise in interest rates of three percentage points
checks.note: Three points is a guide. Where the reference rate has stood more than three points above today's level within the last ten years, test against that level. For a business without a full year of trading, use the first full year of the base case. The test does not wait for the terms of the loan. If the answer already goes against the assumption on the debt the party owes today, record it now and say that it is before the new loan. Answer again when the terms are known.

leads_to.reason: The cover for debt service is too thin to take a rise in rates

checks.question: Does the party buy or sell a commodity whose price is set on a market and changes from day to day?
checks.why: Opens price risk. A "no" is not the end of it. OBS_PRICE_003 is asked whatever the answer, against the accounts.
checks.ask: Is the price of what you sell, or of your main input, set on a commodity market? Which one?

checks.question: Taken at its seasonal peak, is the party's open price position (stock that is neither sold nor hedged, and forward sales at a fixed price for which the goods are neither bought nor hedged) so large that a price move of a fifth against it would cost more than the operating profit of the last full year?
checks.assumption: A price move of a fifth against the party's open position would cost less than a year's operating profit
checks.ask: At the busiest point of your season, how much stock do you hold that is not yet sold or hedged? And how much have you sold forward at a fixed price without having bought the goods?
checks.note: A fifth is a guide. Use a larger move where the price of this commodity has moved by more within a season. The year-end accounts seldom show the peak, so ask for the position report of the peak month.

leads_to.reason: Stock that is not sold is also financed, usually with short-term debt

checks.question: Do the accounts or the party's position reports show futures, options or forward contracts that are larger than its physical purchases and sales, or in goods it does not deal in?
checks.assumption: The party uses futures, options and forward contracts only to cover its physical business
checks.note: This check does not hang on OBS_PRICE_001, so that the topic cannot close on one answer. Large gains or losses on derivatives in the accounts of a party that says it does not deal in commodities are a sign. If the search finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when.

checks.question: In the last five years, has a buyer or a supplier walked away from a forward contract at a fixed price with the party, or forced the party to renegotiate it, after the market price moved?
checks.assumption: The party's buyers and suppliers have honoured their forward contracts when the price moved against them
checks.ask: When prices last moved sharply, did any buyer refuse to take delivery, or any supplier fail to deliver at the agreed price? What did it cost you?
checks.note: A forward contract fixes the price only as long as the other side performs. A party that says yes is believed.

checks.question: Has the party fixed or capped the interest rate on enough of its floating-rate debt, by a swap, a cap or a switch to a fixed rate, that it could service its debt after a rise of three percentage points?
checks.assumption: An interest hedge or a fixed rate keeps the debt service within the party's cash flow after a rise in rates
checks.note: A hedge that ends before the debt does covers only the years it runs.

checks.question: Does the party have a written price-risk policy with position limits, and does someone who does not trade (finance, risk or the board) check the positions against those limits at least once a month?
checks.assumption: Position limits are written down and are checked by someone outside trading
checks.ask: Who sets the limits on how much unsold stock and how many open contracts the traders may hold? Who checks them, and how often? Please share the policy and a recent limit report.
checks.note: Ask for a limit report from a month in which the price moved. A limit that was raised each time it was reached is not a limit.

leads_to.reason: Trading without limits that someone else checks is a gap in control

indicators.title: Working capital
indicators.claim: The party's stock and receivables exist, are worth what its accounts say and turn into cash on time, and its working capital is financed through the peak of the season.

matters_more_when.reason: A trader's assets are almost all stock and receivables, financed with short-term debt
Stock and advances build up over a season and are repaid from a single harvest
Growth ties up cash in stock and receivables before the sales are collected

look_again_when.reason: New accounts show stock, receivables and the provisions against them at a new date
Monthly figures show the seasonal peak, which a year-end balance sheet hides

checks.question: How many days pass, on average, between the party paying for its inputs and collecting the cash from its customers (days of stock plus days of receivables, less days of payables)?
checks.why: The length of the cycle says how much cash each sale ties up, and for how long. It is read against earlier years and against businesses of the same kind.
checks.ask: How long does it take from the day you pay for your inputs to the day your customers pay you? If the figure is not to hand, we can work it out from your stock, receivables and payables.
checks.note: Where the monthly figures allow it, work the cycle out at the seasonal peak as well as at the year-end, and say which date each figure is for. Give days of stock, receivables and payables separately, and set payable days against the suppliers' terms.

checks.question: Do the party's customers pay, on average, within the credit terms the party gives them (days of receivables no longer than those terms)?
checks.assumption: Customers pay within the agreed terms
checks.ask: What credit terms do you give your customers, and how long do they take to pay in practice? An ageing list of your receivables would answer this.
checks.if_unknown: A party that cannot produce an ageing list of its receivables does not know who owes it what.
checks.note: Record the terms and the days of receivables. Where terms differ between kinds of customer, answer for the kind that owes the most and say so.

checks.question: What share of the party's trade receivables, by value, is more than ninety days past its due date?
checks.assumption: Only a small part of the receivables is long overdue
checks.why: Ninety days overdue is where the accounting standards presume a receivable to be in default unless the contrary is shown, and where lenders stop counting it towards a borrowing base. A few such invoices are disputes. Once they pass about a tenth of the total, late payment is a pattern, and the write-down still to come is large enough to change the year's profit. A tenth is a convention, not a rule. An institution can set its own figure.
checks.note: Take the figure from the ageing list at the latest month-end and, where possible, at the seasonal peak. Count the days from the due date, not from the invoice date. Record how much of the overdue amount is provided for.

checks.question: Was the stock in the latest annual accounts counted with the auditor or another independent party present, and valued at the lower of its cost and the price it can be sold for?
checks.assumption: The stock exists and is worth what the accounts say, and someone independent has checked both
checks.ask: Who was present at your last year-end stock count besides your own staff? Is any of your stock held by someone else, such as a warehouse keeper or a processor?
checks.note: A count by the party's own staff alone is a no. Stock held by others (in a public warehouse, at a processor, in transit) counts only where the holder has confirmed it in writing or an inspector has seen it.

checks.question: Is more than about a tenth of the stock, by value, older than one normal selling season or production cycle, or carried at a value that no sale contract and no current market price supports?
checks.assumption: The stock is current and can be sold for at least its value in the accounts
checks.note: A tenth is a guide. Ask for the stock list by age. For a commodity, set the value per tonne in the accounts against the market price on the balance sheet date and today.

checks.question: Does the party's balance sheet carry advances paid to suppliers, farmers or contractors that are still outstanding more than one season, or one normal delivery cycle, after they were paid, with neither the goods delivered nor the money returned?
checks.assumption: Advances to suppliers and farmers come back as goods or as cash within the season
checks.ask: Do you pay suppliers or farmers in advance? How much is outstanding today, and how much of it was paid more than a season ago?
checks.note: Ask for the advances by recipient and by date paid. Record the amount that is overdue and set it against the party's equity. An advance that is rolled into the next season has not come back. For an agribusiness, look at each of the last three seasons. Unrecovered advances above about a tenth of those given are a pattern.

leads_to.reason: A supplier that holds the party's money and has not delivered is a credit risk of its own

checks.question: Do the credit lines that finance the party's seasonal stock and receivables fall due, or come up for the bank's review, before that stock and those receivables have turned into cash?
checks.assumption: The lines that finance the season stay in place until its stock and receivables have turned into cash
checks.ask: In which month do you need the most money for stock and receivables, and how much? Which credit lines pay for it, and when does each of them fall due?
checks.note: Take the peak from the monthly figures of the last two years, not from the year-end balance sheet. A line that falls due, or comes up for the bank's review, in the middle of the season is a yes. A party that finances its season from its own cash alone is a no. Liquidity asks whether a line is committed (OBS_LIQ_003).

indicators.title: Environment
indicators.claim: No environmental harm done by the party's operations, now or in the past, could close a site, cost more than the party has set aside, or come back on the lender.

matters_more_when.reason: A new site needs its assessment and its permits before work starts, and has no record to be judged by
Process industry brings emissions, effluent, waste and, on old sites, contamination
A site that is the only security loses its value, and may bring a clean-up cost, if it is contaminated

look_again_when.reason: A new assessment can show harm, or a missing permit, that was not known
A notice, a fine or an order from an environmental authority bears directly on the claim
An expansion can need a new assessment and new permits

checks.question: Has every environmental impact assessment that the law or the lender's risk category requires, for the party's sites and for anything the loan finances, been carried out, and approved by the environmental authority where the law asks for its approval?
checks.assumption: Every impact assessment that the law or the lender's risk category requires has been done and, where the law asks for it, approved
checks.ask: Has an environmental impact assessment been done for your sites, or for the investment this loan would pay for? Please share the report and the authority's approval of it. If none was needed, who confirmed that?
checks.if_unknown: Without the assessment, nobody has set out what harm the operations can do.
checks.note: Where neither the law nor the category requires an assessment, answer yes and record who confirmed that and on what basis. An assessment done for an earlier, smaller plant does not cover an expansion.

checks.question: Does the party hold, in force, every environmental permit that its sites need (for example for emissions to air, discharge to water, waste, and the taking of water), and do its latest monitoring results meet the limits those permits set?
checks.assumption: The party holds its environmental permits and operates within their limits
checks.ask: Please share your environmental permits and your latest monitoring results for emissions, effluent and waste. Is any permit expired, under renewal or held in another name?
checks.note: Compare the monitoring results with the limits written in the permit itself. Record the expiry date of each permit.

leads_to.reason: A missing environmental permit can also mean the party may not operate at all

checks.question: In the last three years, has the party had a spill, a release or another environmental incident that had to be reported to an authority, or received a fine, a notice of breach or an order to stop work on environmental grounds?
checks.assumption: The party's operations have run for three years without a reportable incident and without a sanction on environmental grounds
checks.ask: In the last three years, has there been a spill, a leak or any other environmental incident at your sites? Has an environmental authority fined you, sent you a notice or told you to stop work? What happened, and how did it end?
checks.note: A party that says yes is believed. A party that says no is believed once its incident log, the authority's record or a press search bears it out. If the search finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when. A site that is not yet built has no record. Say so instead of answering no.

checks.question: Is soil or groundwater known or suspected to be contaminated at any site that the party owns, leases or used to operate, or does the party owe a cost to clean up, decommission or restore a site?
checks.assumption: No site of the party is contaminated, and the party owes no cost to clean up or restore one
checks.ask: Do you know of any contamination of soil or water at your sites, or at sites you used before? Do you have to clean up, dismantle or restore any site, now or when operations end? Is there a provision for it in your accounts?
checks.if_unknown: Old contamination tends to come to light at a sale, an expansion or an enforcement.
checks.note: A site with a long industrial past that nobody has tested is not known to be clean. Ask what the land was used for before the party came.

leads_to.reason: A contaminated site is worth less as security, and whoever takes it over may be asked to pay for the clean-up

checks.question: Has the party named a person who answers to senior management for environmental and social matters, and does it keep a written management system that sets out the risks, the procedures, the monitoring and who does what?
checks.assumption: A named person and a written system manage the party's environmental and social risks
checks.ask: Who in your company is responsible for environmental and social matters, and to whom does that person report? Please share your environmental and social policy and procedures, and the latest monitoring report made under them.
checks.note: A policy on paper is not a system. Look for monitoring records made under it in the last twelve months. A current certificate under a standard such as ISO 14001, with its audit report, counts as best evidence. For a financial institution, the system is the one by which it screens and follows the loans it makes, including against the exclusion lists.

checks.question: Has the exposure of the party's main sites to flood, drought, heat, storm and rising sea level over the life of the loan been assessed, site by site, from hazard data and not from experience alone?
checks.assumption: The physical climate hazards at the party's main sites over the life of the loan have been assessed
checks.ask: Have your main sites been assessed for flood, drought, heat, storm or rising sea level? Who did the assessment, and what did it find?
checks.note: An assessment that finds a high hazard is still a yes. Record the hazards found, so that the operations and the insurance can be read against them. Risks from climate policy, such as a carbon price or a ban, belong to CAS_REGULATORY_001.

leads_to.reason: The hazards found should be set against the insurance cover

checks.question: Does the party measure its greenhouse gas emissions every year, at least those from its own operations and from the energy it buys?
checks.why: A lender that reports the emissions it finances needs the figure, and a party that measures them can show what the loan changes. To have to report emissions is not a fault.
checks.ask: Do you measure your greenhouse gas emissions? If so, please share the latest figures and say who calculated them.
checks.note: Record also the yearly emissions expected of what the loan pays for, where they have been estimated.

checks.question: Has the party agreed with the lender a written action plan that deals with every environmental gap found, with a responsible person, a budget and a date for each action?
checks.assumption: An action plan agreed with the lender closes every gap found, with a person, a budget and a date for each action
checks.note: The plan counts once the party has signed it or it is part of the facility agreement. A draft is not an agreement. An action that needs money counts only if the money is in the party's budget or in the loan.

checks.question: Has a specialist who is independent of the party estimated the cost of the clean-up or restoration, and is that cost provided for in the audited accounts or covered by a funded reserve, an indemnity from a previous owner or insurance?
checks.assumption: The cost of the clean-up or restoration is estimated by someone independent and is covered by a provision, a funded reserve, an indemnity or insurance
checks.note: An indemnity is worth what the one who gave it can pay. A provision is not cash. Say when the money will be needed and where it will come from.

indicators.title: E&S screening
indicators.claim: No activity of the business is on an exclusion list that applies to the deal, and the environmental and social risk of the deal is of a kind the lender can assess and take on.

matters_more_when.reason: A new site brings land, construction and permits that an operating business has behind it
Land conflict, forest clearing and child labour are most common in farming and in its supply
The risk sits in the loans the borrower itself makes, which the lender does not see one by one

look_again_when.reason: An impact assessment can show effects that change the category
Press reports can show an activity or a setting that was not mentioned
An expansion can bring new land, new effects and a higher category

checks.question: What does the lender's own mandate require on environmental, social and impact matters: nothing beyond the law, that these risks are weighed in the credit decision, or that the deal meets a safeguard standard and shows a development impact?
checks.why: Sets how deep the rest of this pillar has to go, and whether impact has to be shown at all.
checks.note: 'none' means the law of the country is the only standard. 'integration' means the risks are weighed in the credit decision, without a fixed standard to meet. 'dfi_impact' means the deal must meet a safeguard standard, such as the IFC Performance Standards, and the lender must be able to show what the loan achieves.

leads_to.reason: A lender with an impact mandate has to show that it is needed and what the loan achieves

checks.question: Which exclusion lists apply to the deal: the lender's own, and any list of those who fund the lender, of other financiers in the deal, or of a guarantor or insurer of the loan?
checks.why: OBS_ES_001 is answered against these lists. A list that is not named here is not checked.
checks.note: Name each list and its version or date. Where no list applies, say so. Where another financier applies a stricter environmental or social standard, name it: the strictest is the one the borrower has to meet.

checks.question: Does the business that the loan finances, including the companies the borrower controls, carry on any activity that is on an exclusion list that applies to the deal?
checks.assumption: No part of the business carries on an activity that an applicable exclusion list forbids
checks.ask: Here is the list of activities we cannot finance. Does your company, or any company it controls, do any of these, even as a small part of its business? If so, what share of revenue does it bring?
checks.if_unknown: An excluded activity that comes to light after signing can force the lender out of the deal.
checks.note: Go through each list named in OBS_ESG_MANDATE_003, activity by activity, against the revenue breakdown, the licences and the product list, and not only against the description of the main business. Where a list sets its own limit (often a share of revenue), apply that limit and record the share. For a financial institution, ask also whether it lends to such activities and how it screens for them. If the review finds nothing, record what was checked, against which lists and when.

checks.question: Which environmental and social topics arise from what the business does and from where it does it?
checks.why: Says where the rest of this pillar has to look. The topics are those of IFC Performance Standards 2 to 8.
checks.note: Name a topic when the operations, a planned expansion or the main suppliers touch it, whether or not any harm has been found. Labour arises for every business that employs people or uses contractors.

leads_to.reason: Permits, incidents and contamination are tested there for each party
Complaints from neighbours and the conduct of guards are tested there
How the land was acquired, and from whom, is tested there

checks.question: Is any site of the business, or the source of any of its main raw materials, in an area of armed conflict, in a country and sector that a public list names for child or forced labour, or in a region where natural forest is still being cleared?
checks.assumption: Neither the sites nor the main supplies of the business lie in a setting known for armed conflict, for child or forced labour, or for forest clearing
checks.ask: Where are your sites, and where do your main raw materials come from? Please name the regions, not only the countries.
checks.note: This is about the setting, not about what the business has done. A yes means that the tests on land, labour and supply need evidence from the ground and not from the office. Say which lists, maps or reports were used, and their dates. If the search finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when.

leads_to.reason: Forest clearing and child or forced labour are tested there, site by site and supplier by supplier
Armed conflict is also a risk to the operations and to repayment

checks.question: Which environmental and social risk category does the lender give the deal: A, B, C or FI?
checks.assumption: The harm the deal could do is limited in extent, can largely be reversed and can be dealt with by known measures
checks.why: Category A is given where the possible harm is diverse, irreversible or without precedent. Lenders that follow the IFC Performance Standards or the Equator Principles then ask for a full impact assessment, its disclosure and an independent review before approval, and some lenders cannot take such a deal at all.
checks.note: A is harm that is diverse, irreversible or without precedent. B is limited harm, mostly at the site, that known measures can deal with. C is little or no harm. FI is money passed on through a financial intermediary, where the risk sits in the loans the intermediary makes. A category given at screening is provisional. Say who set it and when.

checks.question: Does the financial intermediary screen the loans it makes against an exclusion list and for environmental and social risk, under a written procedure with a named person in charge, and can it show loans that it refused or made subject to conditions on those grounds?
checks.assumption: The financial intermediary screens its own lending for excluded activities and for environmental and social risk, and acts on the result
checks.ask: How do you check the loans you make for activities on an exclusion list and for environmental and social risk? Who is in charge of it, and can you show us loans that you turned down or attached conditions to for these reasons?
checks.note: A procedure on paper is not enough. Ask for the list of loans screened in the last twelve months, with the result for each. OBS_ENV_007 asks about the management system for the party's own operations, not for its lending.

checks.question: Has a specialist who is independent of the borrower assessed the deal against the environmental and social standard that the lender applies, covering every topic that arises?
checks.assumption: An independent assessment against the lender's standard covers every topic that arises
checks.note: The topics are those named in OBS_ES_002. An impact assessment written for a permit answers the law of the country, not the lender's standard, and is not enough by itself. The report should say, topic by topic, where the business falls short of the standard.

indicators.title: Impact and additionality
indicators.claim: The loan makes possible something that would not happen without the lender, the impact claimed for it can be measured, and nothing it finances runs against the lender's climate commitment.

matters_more_when.reason: Where other financing is in place, the question is what this lender adds to it
An established business is the most likely to have offers from commercial lenders
Money lent to a financial institution mixes with its other funds, so the impact has to be traced to the loans it then makes

look_again_when.reason: An offer from another financier bears directly on whether the lender is needed
Other financing that comes to light changes what the lender adds

checks.question: Who is better off because of what the loan finances, in what way, and about how many are they?
checks.why: This is the impact claim. Each group and each benefit named here needs an indicator in OBS_IMPACT_009.
checks.ask: Who will benefit from this investment besides your company (workers, suppliers, customers, the people nearby), and how? Roughly how many are they?
checks.note: Name the people and the change, not the activity. "Builds a plant" is an activity. "Buys from about two thousand more small farmers" is an impact.

checks.question: What does the lender add besides money: for example higher environmental, social or governance standards, advice, or the confidence that brings in other financiers?
checks.why: A lender that brings only money is needed only where money is short. That is tested in OBS_IMPACT_008.
checks.note: Name what the lender will do and where it is written down. A general statement of the lender's role is not an answer.

checks.question: Has a commercial bank or investor offered the borrower financing for the same purpose with a tenor, a currency and an amount close to what the lender is asked for, or do commercial lenders make such loans to comparable borrowers in the same market?
checks.assumption: Commercial lenders would not finance this on terms the borrower could work with
checks.ask: Which banks or investors have you approached for this financing, and what did each of them offer or say? What tenor and which currency can you get from your current banks?
checks.note: A lower price is not the test. A borrower that can borrow from commercial lenders and prefers the lender's price does not need the lender. "Close to" is a guide. What counts is whether the investment could go ahead on the commercial terms. A written offer or refusal from a bank is best evidence. The borrower's word that no bank would lend is its own word.

checks.question: Does every impact claimed have an indicator with a baseline figure, a target, a date and a named source of data from which the borrower will report it?
checks.assumption: Every impact claimed has an indicator, a baseline, a target and a source of data
checks.ask: For each benefit you expect, what is the figure today, what figure do you aim for and by when? From which of your records would you report it each year?
checks.note: The baseline is a figure measured before the loan, not an estimate made afterwards. The indicators count as agreed once the reporting is written into the facility agreement.

checks.question: Does the loan finance any activity that the lender treats as not aligned with the Paris Agreement?
checks.assumption: Nothing the loan finances is, by the lender's own method, out of line with the Paris Agreement
checks.note: Go by the lender's own method and list. Many development banks treat the mining of thermal coal and power from coal or peat as never aligned, and judge other activities case by case against the country's climate plans. For a loan for general purposes, look at the whole business and not only at the stated use.

checks.question: What share of the loan amount counts as climate finance, for mitigation or adaptation, under the method the lender uses?
checks.why: A lender with a climate target reports this share. It rests on what the money pays for, item by item.
checks.note: Say which method was used. Where none of the loan counts, record 0.

checks.question: Are figures available for the share of women among the owners, the board and senior management, the employees and the customers of the business?
checks.why: A lender with a gender target needs these figures before it can say whether the deal counts towards it. The 2X Challenge criteria are a common reference.
checks.ask: What share of your owners, of your board and senior managers, of your employees and of your customers are women? Approximate figures will do to start with.

indicators.title: Land and supply chain
indicators.claim: The land the party uses is held securely and was acquired fairly, and neither that land nor the party's supply chain involves the clearing of natural forest or forced or child labour.

matters_more_when.reason: Farm land and farm supply are where land conflict, forest clearing and child labour are most common
New land is being taken now, and those who lose it are still there to object
Where the land is the security, a flaw in the right to it is a flaw in the second way out

look_again_when.reason: A new or renewed lease changes how long, and on what terms, the land is held
A review of title can find a competing right or a defect in how the land was acquired
Press and civil society reports are often the first sign of a land conflict or of abuse among suppliers

checks.question: Does the party hold every site that its operations need under a title or a lease that is registered in its own name and runs beyond the final maturity of the loan?
checks.assumption: The party holds the land it needs under a registered right that outlasts the loan
checks.ask: For each of your sites, do you own the land or lease it? In whose name is it registered, and when does the lease or concession end? Please share the title deed, the lease or the extract from the land register.
checks.note: A concession or a right of use granted by the state counts as a lease here. A site held by a shareholder, a sister company or a director is not held by the party. Record for each site the kind of right, the register and the end date. Where the country keeps no register for this kind of right, answer from the signed document and a legal opinion, and say so.

leads_to.reason: Land that the party does not hold securely cannot be given as good security

checks.question: In the last ten years, was any land that the party now uses, or that the loan would pay for, acquired from people who lived on it, farmed it or earned their living from it, so that they had to move or lost that living?
checks.assumption: No one had to give up a home or a living for the land the party uses
checks.ask: How and when did you get the land for each site, and from whom? Was anyone living on it, farming it or using it at the time? What happened to them?
checks.note: Ten years is a guide. Look further back where a grievance is still alive. Count land that the state or a previous owner cleared of people for the party. A sale between willing parties, with no one else on the land, is a no.

checks.question: Does anyone contest the party's right to any of its sites, in a court, before a land authority, or through a claim made to the party or reported in the press (for example a competing title, an unpaid seller, heirs, an overlapping concession or a claim for restitution)?
checks.assumption: No one contests the party's right to its land
checks.ask: Has anyone challenged your right to any of your land, in court or outside it? Think of former owners, heirs, neighbours, communities, or another holder of a licence over the same area.
checks.note: Search the land register, the courts and the press. If the search finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when.

leads_to.reason: A claim to the land is a dispute whose cost and outcome are examined there

checks.question: Do indigenous peoples, or people who farm, graze, fish or gather by custom without a registered right, live on or use the party's sites or the land and water that its operations affect?
checks.assumption: No indigenous people and no customary users depend on the land or water that the operations use or affect
checks.ask: Who used this land before you, and who crosses it, grazes on it or takes water or wood from it today? Do any of them belong to an indigenous people?
checks.note: A clean title does not answer this. Customary use is often unregistered. If the search finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when.

checks.question: Were the people concerned consulted and compensated under a written plan or agreement (at replacement cost for what they lost, and with the consent of indigenous peoples where the lender's standard asks for it), and has someone independent of the party confirmed that the plan was carried out?
checks.assumption: Those who lost land or its use were consulted and compensated under a written plan, and someone independent has confirmed that it was carried out
checks.note: IFC Performance Standards 5 and 7 are the usual reference. Money paid to a chief or an official is not compensation paid to those who lost the land. Where the plan is not yet carried out, the answer is no, and what remains belongs in an action agreed with the lender.

checks.question: What share of the party's main raw materials, by volume, can be traced to the farm, the forest or the mine where they were produced?
checks.why: A party can only answer for the supply it can trace. The answers to OBS_SUPPLYCHAIN_002 and OBS_SUPPLYCHAIN_003 are worth no more than this share.
checks.ask: For your main raw materials, what share of the volume can you trace back to the farm, the forest or the mine it came from? And what share only as far as the first buyer, such as a co-operative, a collection point or a mill?
checks.note: Tracing to the first buyer is weaker than tracing to the place of production. Record that share separately. A party that produces all of its own raw materials records 100.

checks.question: Has natural forest, or another habitat that is protected or of high conservation value, been cleared after the cut-off date that the lender applies, on land the party uses or on land of the suppliers of its main raw materials?
checks.assumption: No natural forest or protected habitat was cleared after the lender's cut-off date for the party's land or for its main raw materials
checks.ask: Has any forest or other natural land been cleared on your own land, and since when is each plot in use? What do you know about clearing on the land of your suppliers?
checks.note: Record the cut-off date used and where it comes from (the lender's policy, a certification scheme, or a rule of the market where the goods are sold). A no for supply that cannot be traced is not a no. It is not known. If a search of satellite records or the press finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when.

checks.question: In the last three years, has an audit, an authority, a customer, a civil society group or the press found child labour or forced labour among the suppliers of the party's main raw materials or goods?
checks.assumption: No child labour or forced labour has been found among the party's main suppliers
checks.ask: Has child labour or forced labour ever been found at one of your suppliers, by you, by an auditor, by a customer or by anyone else? How do you check for it, and how far down the chain?
checks.if_unknown: In a sector known for child or forced labour, the absence of findings shows only that nobody has looked.
checks.note: Where the supply comes from a setting flagged in OBS_ES_003 and nobody has looked, the answer is not no. It is not known. Count the suppliers of the equipment the loan pays for. If the search finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when.

checks.question: Are the raw materials concerned covered by a certification scheme that sets rules on forest clearing and on child and forced labour, with a certificate that is in force and an audit by an accredited third party in the last twelve months?
checks.assumption: A certification that is in force, and audited by a third party within the last year, covers the raw materials concerned
checks.note: Check the certificate in the scheme's own public register, and record the share of the volume that it covers. A certificate for part of the volume protects only that part. Read the audit report for open findings.

checks.question: Does the party run a system that maps the suppliers concerned down to the place of production, checks them at least once a year against records of forest loss and findings on labour, and stops buying from those that fail?
checks.assumption: The party traces the supply concerned, checks it at least once a year and stops buying from suppliers that fail
checks.ask: How do you know where each delivery comes from? How often do you check your suppliers, against what, and when did you last stop buying from one?
checks.note: Ask for the list of suppliers that were suspended or dropped. A system that has never excluded anyone has not been tested.

indicators.title: Labour and community
indicators.claim: The party employs its workers lawfully and safely and has no unresolved conflict with the people around its sites, so that no strike, protest or sanction over either could stop its operations or discredit its lenders.

matters_more_when.reason: Field and packing work relies on seasonal and migrant workers, whose terms are the weakest
Construction brings contractors' workers, the highest accident rates and new neighbours

look_again_when.reason: A press report of a strike, an accident or a protest bears directly on the claim
A labour inspection report or an order from an authority can show a breach
A complaints log shows what workers and neighbours have raised and what was done about it

checks.question: Does the party meet the labour law of each country where it employs people, on written contracts, minimum wage, working hours and overtime pay, minimum age, social security contributions and the freedom to join a union?
checks.assumption: The party meets the labour law on contracts, pay, hours, minimum age, social security and the freedom to organise
checks.ask: Does every worker have a written contract? Do you pay at least the minimum wage, overtime, and social security contributions in full? When did the labour inspector last visit, and what did the report say?
checks.note: Count the workers of labour contractors who do the party's regular work, and the workers who build what the loan pays for, the builder's included. A labour inspection report or an independent labour audit is best evidence. The party's own personnel policy shows what it intends, not what it does.

checks.question: In the last three years, has a worker of the party, or of a contractor on its sites, died or been permanently disabled in an accident at work?
checks.assumption: No worker has died or been permanently disabled at the party's sites in the last three years
checks.ask: In the last three years, has anyone died or been permanently injured at work on your sites, including contractors' workers? What happened, and what did you change afterwards?
checks.note: Count contractors' workers and drivers on the party's business, and the workers who build what the loan pays for. A party that says yes is believed. A party that says no is believed once its accident register, the authority or the insurer bears it out. A site that is not yet built has no record. Say so instead of answering no.

checks.question: Are seasonal, agency, contract or migrant workers who do the party's regular work paid less, housed worse or less protected against accidents than permanent staff who do the same work, or do they pay a fee for the job or leave their identity papers with the employer or a recruiter?
checks.assumption: Workers who are not permanent staff get the same pay and protection for the same work, pay no fee for the job and keep their own papers
checks.ask: How many seasonal, agency, contract or migrant workers do you use at the busiest time of the year? Who recruits them, who pays them, and where do they live? Do they pay anything to get the job?
checks.note: Where the party uses no such workers, answer no and say so. Count the workers who build what the loan pays for, the builder's included. Fees paid for a job and papers held by someone else are signs of forced labour under IFC Performance Standard 2. Look at the contract with the labour contractor and, where workers are housed, at the housing.

checks.question: In the last three years, has the party had a strike, a lock-out, a collective dismissal, a claim brought by a group of workers before a court or a labour authority, or a fine or an order from the labour authority?
checks.assumption: The party has had three years without a collective labour dispute and without a sanction from the labour authority
checks.ask: In the last three years, have you had a strike, a mass dismissal, a court case brought by a group of workers, or a fine or an order from the labour authority? What was it about, and how did it end?
checks.note: Accidents at work are asked in OBS_SOC_005. If the search finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when.

leads_to.reason: A claim by workers or a sanction can turn into proceedings and a cost

checks.question: Have people who live or work near the party's sites raised a complaint, a protest or a claim about its operations (for example about noise, dust, water, traffic, safety or a lost livelihood) that is not yet resolved?
checks.assumption: No complaint, protest or claim from the people around the party's sites is unresolved
checks.ask: Have neighbours, local leaders or local groups complained about your operations, or protested against them? What about, and where does the matter stand today?
checks.if_unknown: Nobody has asked the neighbours, so their silence shows nothing.
checks.note: Resolved means that those who complained accept the outcome, or that a court or an authority has closed the matter. If the search finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when.

leads_to.reason: Where the complaint is about land or lost livelihoods, how the land was acquired is tested there

checks.question: Is any site of the party protected by armed guards, police or soldiers who work without written rules on the use of force or without a check of their past conduct, or who have injured or detained a worker or a local person in the last three years?
checks.assumption: Where armed guards, police or soldiers protect the party's sites, they are checked, bound by written rules on the use of force, and have harmed no one
checks.ask: Who guards your sites, and are they armed? Do police or soldiers ever protect them? What written rules do the guards follow on the use of force, and has anyone been hurt or held by them in the last three years?
checks.note: Where no site has armed guards, police or soldiers, answer no and say so. IFC Performance Standard 4 is the usual reference. If the search finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when.

checks.question: Can workers and people near the party's sites raise a complaint through a channel that is written down, made known to them and open to anonymous use, and is each complaint logged with what was done about it?
checks.assumption: Workers and neighbours have a channel for complaints that they know of, and complaints are logged and answered
checks.ask: How can a worker or a neighbour complain to you? Please share the procedure and the log of complaints received in the last twelve months, with what was done about each.
checks.note: Look at the log, not only at the procedure. An empty log at a large site more often means that the channel is not known or not trusted than that nobody has a complaint.

checks.question: Has the party agreed with the lender a written action plan that deals with every labour and community finding, with a responsible person, a budget and a date for each action?
checks.assumption: An action plan agreed with the lender deals with every finding, with a person, a budget and a date for each action
checks.note: The plan counts once the party has signed it or it is part of the facility agreement. After a death or a permanent injury, the plan should rest on a written finding of the cause. For a dispute or a sanction, the plan should show the settlement or the authority's confirmation that the breach is put right.

indicators.title: Builder and operator
indicators.claim: The builder or operator has done this kind of work well before, is bound by contract to do it here, and can be made to pay or be replaced if it fails.

matters_more_when.reason: Until the project is built there is no cash flow, so repayment rests on the builder
A single-purpose company has no staff and no means of its own, so it can do only what its contractors do

look_again_when.reason: A signed or amended construction contract changes the price, the date and what the builder answers for
A signed or amended operating contract changes the term and what the operator answers for

checks.question: In the last five years, has the builder or operator delivered work of the same technology and of about the same size as this job, on time and performing as specified?
checks.assumption: The builder or operator has delivered comparable work on time and to specification
checks.ask: Which comparable jobs has this firm done in the last five years? For each, was it finished on time, did the plant pass its tests, and who at the client can confirm it?
checks.note: For a builder, delivered means built and handed over. For an operator, it means run for at least a full year. Removal from a contract, a job left unfinished, a bond that was called or damages paid on comparable work is a no. Five years and "about the same size" are guides. The firm's own list of references is its own word until a client, a lender or an independent engineer confirms it. If a search for such events finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when.

checks.question: Is the net worth of the builder or operator, in its latest audited accounts, at least three times the most it can owe under the contract (the cap on its liability)?
checks.assumption: The builder or operator could pay the most it can owe under the contract and stay in business
checks.if_unknown: Damages and warranties are worth nothing if the firm that owes them cannot pay.
checks.note: Take the accounts of the company that signs the contract, not those of its group. Where liability has no cap, set the net worth against the contract price. Three times is a guide. What counts is that paying the cap would not break the firm. A thinly capitalised local subsidiary is a no, and its parent's guarantee is then asked for in OBS_BUILDOP_007.

checks.question: Does the builder take on the whole of the works for a fixed price and a fixed completion date, as the one party responsible for design, supply and construction?
checks.assumption: One builder answers for the whole of the works, at a fixed price and by a fixed date
checks.ask: Is the construction contract a fixed-price, fixed-date contract for the whole of the works? If the works are split, who answers for the gaps between the contracts?
checks.note: Where the works are split between several contracts, the answer is no unless one party has signed to answer for the whole. Say which parts of the price can still move, such as provisional sums, indexation or ground conditions. For equipment added to a running plant, a supply and installation contract with the maker, with a fixed price and a date, counts as yes.

checks.question: Does the operator's contract run at least until the final maturity of the loan, with no right for the operator to end it earlier at its own choice?
checks.assumption: The operator is bound for the life of the loan
checks.note: Where the contract is shorter, record when it ends, whether it renews by itself, and on what price.

checks.question: If the builder or operator fails to perform, do the contract and a direct agreement with the lender allow it to be removed and another firm to take over the work?
checks.assumption: A builder or operator that fails can be removed and replaced, by the project or by the lender
checks.note: A direct agreement is signed by the builder or operator with the lender. It lets the lender step into the contract or appoint a substitute before the contract can be ended. A right to replace is worth little where only this firm can do the work (its own technology, a licence, the only local presence). Say whether other firms could take over.

checks.question: Is the builder or operator owned or controlled by the sponsor, the borrower or their owners?
checks.assumption: The builder or operator is independent of the sponsor and the borrower, so the contract will be enforced against it
checks.ask: Is the builder or the operator part of the sponsor's group, or owned by any of the same people?
checks.note: A sponsor that controls both sides of the contract decides whether damages are claimed, a bond is called or the contract is ended.

leads_to.reason: A contract with a related party needs the price and the terms an outsider would get

checks.question: Is the performance of the builder or operator backed by security that can be called without its consent (a bank bond or letter of credit, money retained from its payments, or a guarantee from its parent)?
checks.assumption: Security that can be called stands behind the performance of the builder or operator
checks.note: Say which kind, who issued it, its amount as a share of the contract price, and when it expires. Set the amount against the damages the firm can owe. A bond that lapses at handover does not cover defects.

leads_to.reason: Where the security is a parent's guarantee, it is worth what the parent can pay

checks.question: Are the rights under the contract, and under its bonds and guarantees, assigned to the lender, so that the lender can claim damages and call the security without the sponsor or the borrower acting?
checks.assumption: The lender can enforce the contract and call its security itself
checks.note: An assignment that takes effect only after the borrower defaults under the loan comes late. Say from when the lender can act.

indicators.title: Completion support
indicators.claim: The giver of the support is bound to pay or to act until the project is proved complete, for an amount that covers a plausible overrun.

matters_more_when.reason: Until the project is complete there is no cash flow, so the support is what stands behind the loan
A single-purpose borrower cannot pay for an overrun or a delay out of its own means

look_again_when.reason: A new draft or the signed undertaking can change its triggers, its cap and its release
A sponsor support agreement can change what the giver owes and when

checks.question: Which events oblige the giver of the support to pay or to act?
checks.assumption: The undertaking states the events that oblige its giver to pay or to act
checks.why: Support that can be argued about when it is called does not arrive in time. Where the trigger is unclear, the giver decides whether it must pay.
checks.note: Choose unclear where the trigger depends on the giver's own judgement, on an event that is not defined, or on a document not yet written. Unclear may be chosen together with other options. Where the undertaking covers only the debt, it is a guarantee and belongs on a guarantees link (CAS_GUARANTEE_001).

checks.question: Is the support unlimited in amount, or capped at no less than the cost overrun in the independent engineer's downside case?
checks.assumption: The amount of the support covers a plausible cost overrun
checks.note: Record the cap. Where no independent downside case exists, set the cap against the contingency in the budget. A cap smaller than that contingency adds little.

checks.question: Which events end the support?
checks.assumption: The undertaking states when the support ends
checks.why: Where the end of the support is unclear, the giver can claim it has been released when the project runs into trouble, which is when the support is needed.
checks.note: financial_completion means the project has met stated financial tests after it started to operate. dsra_funded means the debt service reserve account is filled. A release at the start of commercial operation ends the support before the plant has shown that it performs. Record any fixed end date.

checks.question: What proof does the undertaking require before the support is released?
checks.assumption: The support is released only on a certificate from an independent engineer or with the lender's approval
checks.why: A release that the project, its builder or its sponsor can certify for itself ends the support on the word of the party that is supported. Only an independent engineer's certificate or the lender's own approval keeps the decision out of its hands.
checks.note: Choose every proof that is required. completion_certificate means a certificate signed by the project, its builder or its sponsor.

checks.question: Could the lender itself enforce the undertaking against its giver (it is signed, the lender is a party to it or holds it by assignment, and counsel confirms that it binds the giver)?
checks.assumption: The lender can enforce the undertaking against its giver
checks.if_unknown: Support that the lender cannot call depends on the sponsor choosing to honour it.
checks.note: A draft, a term sheet or a letter of comfort is a no. So is an undertaking given only to the borrower, which the lender cannot call unless it is assigned.

leads_to.reason: The support is worth what its giver can pay on the day it is called

indicators.title: Material contract
indicators.claim: The contract gives the party that the lender counts on what the projections assume, and it stays in force until the loan is repaid.

matters_more_when.reason: The first way out rests on what the contract says
A project lives on a few contracts and has no other business to fall back on

look_again_when.reason: An amendment or a new draft can change the price, the volume, the term or the right to end the contract
An amendment or a new draft can change the price, the volume, the term or the right to end the contract
A new model may count on more than the contract gives

checks.question: Would the party be unable to service the loan if this contract ended or was not performed?
checks.why: Opens the review. A contract is in the structure because someone judged that repayment depends on it. This answer says so plainly, and most of the checks that follow are asked only if it does.
checks.ask: If this contract ended tomorrow, could you still pay your lenders?
checks.note: "The party" is the party to the contract that the lender counts on. "The other side" is whoever it has contracted with. Examples are a sales contract that brings most of the revenue, and a supply, lease, concession or licence contract that the business cannot run without.

leads_to.reason: Whether the customer under a sales contract can pay, and can be replaced, is asked on the link to it
Whether the supplier under a supply contract can deliver, and can be replaced, is asked on the link to it

checks.question: What does the contract give the party and what does it ask of it: who the parties are, the term, the volume, the price or price formula, and the main duties of each side?
checks.why: The terms are set against what the projections assume (OBS_CONT_008).
checks.ask: Please share the signed contract, or a summary of its parties, term, volume, price and termination rights.

checks.question: Does the contract end, or come up for renewal, before the final repayment date of the loan?
checks.assumption: The contract runs until the loan is repaid
checks.ask: When does this contract end? Is there a right to extend it, and whose right is it?
checks.if_unknown: The projections may count on the contract in years in which it no longer exists.
checks.note: This check does not hang on OBS_CONT_001, so that the review cannot close on one answer. An option to extend that only the other side can use does not lengthen the term. Record how much time lies between the final maturity and the end of the contract (the tail).

leads_to.reason: The years after the contract ends should be projected at market terms, not at contract terms

checks.question: Do the volume, the price and the term that the financial model takes from this contract match the signed contract, or the latest draft where it is not yet signed?
checks.assumption: The projections take from the contract no more than the contract gives
checks.note: Check the price formula, the indexation, the minimum and maximum volumes, the start date and any ramp-up. Where only a draft exists, say so. The answer is then looked at again when the contract is signed.

checks.question: Can the other side end the contract without a breach by the party, or change the price or the volume without the party's consent?
checks.assumption: The other side is held to the contract, its price and its volume for the whole term
checks.note: Look for a right to end for convenience or on notice, price review and benchmarking clauses, most-favoured-customer clauses, volume flexibility, and wide rights on force majeure or change in law.

checks.question: Can the other side end or change the contract if the ownership of the party changes, or if the lender enforces its security over the party's shares or assets?
checks.assumption: The contract survives a change of ownership of the party and the enforcement of the lender's security
checks.ask: Does this contract let the other side end or renegotiate it if the ownership or control of your company changes, or if a lender takes over the company or its assets?
checks.note: Read the clauses on change of control, on assignment and on insolvency. A ban on assignment without consent has the same effect when the lender sells the business.

checks.question: Does the contract name a governing law, and a court or arbitral tribunal, whose decision could be enforced against the other side where the other side has its assets?
checks.assumption: A claim under the contract can be decided and enforced against the other side
checks.note: The contract shows the law and the forum. Whether a decision can be enforced is for a lawyer to say. Where the other side is a state or a state-owned body, ask whether it has waived immunity.
