checks.question: Can the lender keep the contract alive when it enforces: are the party's rights under the contract assigned to the lender as security, or has the other side signed a direct agreement that gives the lender notice, time to cure and the right to step in or to put a new party in?
checks.assumption: The lender can take over the contract, or keep it alive, when it enforces
checks.note: An assignment needs the other side's consent where the contract forbids assignment. Say whether the consent has been given.

indicators.title: Owner and group
indicators.claim: The tie works as the lender counts on: the owner puts money in when the company is short, cash that the owner's debt depends on can come up, and none is taken up at the lender's cost.

matters_more_when.reason: A holding company repays from what the companies it owns send up
A special-purpose borrower has only what its sponsor puts in
In distress an owner decides whether to put money in or to take it out

look_again_when.reason: A new or changed shareholder agreement can change who must put money in and who can block a dividend
New accounts show dividends, loans to the owner and the owner's own means at a new date

checks.question: Which way does the lender rely on the tie between this owner and the company it owns or sponsors: on money coming down from the owner, on cash coming up from the company, on both, or on neither?
checks.why: Most ties in a chain of owners carry nothing that the lender counts on. Then the answer is neither, and only OBS_GROUP_010 is still asked about the tie. Any other answer also asks what the owner owes on its own account.
checks.note: Answer from the financial model and the credit paper, not from memory. An equity injection, a shareholder loan or a promise to cover cost overruns in the projections means support_from_owner. Debt of the owner that is serviced from dividends, fees or loans from the company means cash_from_owned. "The company" stands for whatever is owned or sponsored.

checks.question: How much debt does the owner owe on its own account (loans, bonds and leases in its own name), at the latest balance sheet date?
checks.why: This is the debt that the cash coming up from the company has to help service, and that the owner pays before it can support the company. The consolidated accounts do not show it, because they add the company's debt to the owner's.
checks.ask: How much does the owner itself owe, leaving out the debt of the companies it owns? Please share the owner's own accounts.
checks.note: Use the owner's own accounts, not the consolidated ones. Say the date and the currency. Leave out the debt of the companies it owns, also where the owner has guaranteed it, and name such guarantees in the reason.

checks.question: How much cash did the owner receive from the company in the last financial year (dividends, fees, interest, and loans that the company repaid or gave to it)?
checks.why: Set against what the owner owes, this shows how much of the owner's debt service the company carries, and whether what comes up is enough.
checks.ask: How much cash did the owner receive from the company last year, as dividends, fees, interest or loans?
checks.note: Count cash received in the year, not dividends declared or income booked. Take it from the owner's own cash flow statement, or from the company's payments to the owner. Say the year and the currency, and how much of it was loans from the company.

checks.question: Has the owner bound itself in writing to support the company: by a guarantee of the loan, or by a signed undertaking to put money in?
checks.assumption: The owner is bound in writing to support the company
checks.why: Support that rests on the owner's goodwill is given when it suits the owner. Only a signed promise can be claimed.
checks.ask: Will the owner sign a guarantee, or an undertaking addressed to us, to put money into the company if it runs short?

checks.question: Would the company's failure hurt the owner itself: would the owner lose about a fifth or more of its own assets or revenue, see its own loans fall due through a cross-default, or have its own name or licence damaged?
checks.assumption: The company's failure would cost the owner more than supporting it
checks.note: A fifth is a guide. What counts is that walking away would cost the owner something it values. A company that is small, new, in a side business or up for sale gives its owner little reason to pay.

checks.question: When the company was last short of money (a loss, a cost overrun, a covenant breach, a payment it could not make), did the owner put money in?
checks.assumption: The owner has put money in when the company was short
checks.why: What an owner did the last time is the best guide to what it will do the next time. A company that was never short has shown nothing either way, so that answer is recorded and does not count against the owner.
checks.note: Money in means new equity, or a loan that ranks behind the lenders, paid in cash. A promise is not money in. Where the company is new, look at what the owner did for its other companies and say so.

checks.question: Could the owner, from its own cash and unused committed credit lines and after paying its own debt due in the next twelve months, cover one year of the company's debt service?
checks.assumption: The owner has the means to support the company when the company is short
checks.note: Use the owner's own accounts, not the consolidated ones. Cash held in other subsidiaries may not be the owner's to move. One year of debt service is a guide to the size of the support. Where the owner has guaranteed the loan, its capacity is tested in full as a guarantor.

checks.question: Can anything stop or limit the company from paying dividends or lending to the owner: a rule on reserves that may be distributed, a regulator's approval, exchange control, a minority shareholder's veto, a tax on the payment, or a covenant or lock-up in the company's own loans?
checks.assumption: Nothing stands between the company's spare cash and the owner
checks.note: Read the company's own loan agreements for dividend tests and lock-ups. A block that applies only after a default still counts. It bites exactly when the owner needs the cash.

checks.question: Does the company owe debt of its own (loans, bonds, leases, guarantees it has given) that is paid from its cash and assets before anything reaches the owner?
checks.assumption: No lender of the company stands between the company's cash and the owner
checks.why: A lender to the owner is paid from what is left after the company's own lenders. If the company fails, they take its assets first.
checks.note: Any such debt ranks first. Give its amount in the reason and set it against the company's yearly cash flow, so that a small working-capital line can be told from debt that takes most of the cash.

leads_to.reason: The company's lenders are paid before the owner, and so before a lender to the owner

checks.question: In the last five years, did the owner take cash out of the company (dividends, loans to itself, fees, or purchases at prices above the market) in a year in which the company made a loss, breached a covenant or paid its creditors late?
checks.assumption: The owner leaves cash in the company when the company is weak
checks.why: An owner that drew cash from a weak company has shown whose interest comes first. For a lender to the company it is cash gone. For a lender to the owner it is the source of repayment being run down.

leads_to.reason: Cash taken out by the owner is a dealing with a related party, and there may be more

checks.question: Is the company's cash swept into, or mixed with, the cash of the owner or the group (a cash pool, a common treasury, shared bank accounts), so that its balance is a claim on the group and not money in its own account?
checks.assumption: The company's cash is in its own accounts and under its own control
checks.ask: Does the company keep its cash in its own bank accounts, or is it swept into a group account or lent to the group's treasury?
checks.note: The cash pooling agreement shows who owes whom. In the audited accounts a pooled balance appears as an amount due from a group company, not as cash.

checks.question: Does the owner, or a holding company between the owner and the company, owe debt that it can service only with dividends, fees or loans from the company?
checks.assumption: The owner does not need the company's cash to service its own debt
checks.why: An owner that needs the company's cash to pay its own lenders takes it out whatever state the company is in. That is how a sound company is weakened from above.
checks.ask: Does the owner, or any holding company above the company, have debt of its own? What does it pay the interest and the repayments from?
checks.if_unknown: Where the owner's own accounts have not been seen, its debt is not known.
checks.note: This check does not hang on OBS_GROUP_001. It is asked whichever way the lender relies on the tie, and where it relies on neither. Use the owner's own accounts, not the consolidated ones, and set its debt service against its income from everything other than the company. Debt taken on to buy the company's shares often sits in a holding company above it.

checks.question: Do the lender's loan terms bind the company itself to limits on dividends, on loans and guarantees to the owner and the group, and on taking part in a cash pool?
checks.assumption: The loan terms limit what the owner can take out of the company
checks.note: The limits help only if the company has signed them. A covenant given by the owner alone does not stop the company from paying.

leads_to.reason: Limits on dividends and on loans to the group belong in the covenants

checks.question: Does the lender hold a direct claim on the company: a guarantee from it, security over its assets, or the company as a co-borrower?
checks.assumption: The lender can claim against the company itself, beside the company's own lenders
checks.note: A pledge of the company's shares is not a direct claim. It gives the lender the owner's place, behind the company's creditors. Whether a company may guarantee its owner's debt is asked about the guarantee itself.

indicators.title: The guarantee
indicators.claim: If the borrower does not pay, the lender can claim the guaranteed amount from the guarantor, at once and in full.

matters_more_when.reason: Without security the guarantee is the only second way out

look_again_when.reason: A new draft or the signed guarantee can change what it covers

checks.question: What does the guarantor promise to do?
checks.assumption: The guarantor promises to pay on first demand
checks.why: Only a promise to pay on first demand gives the lender money when it needs it. The other kinds pay late, in part or not at all.
checks.ask: What exactly would the guarantor sign up to? To pay when we ask, to pay only after we have enforced against the borrower, to share a loss, or to make sure something is done?

checks.question: What is the most the guarantor can be made to pay?
checks.why: The cap is set against what is owed under the facility and against the guarantor's own means.

checks.question: Does the guarantee cover everything owed under the facility (principal, interest, default interest, fees and enforcement costs) for the whole life of the loan?
checks.assumption: The guarantee covers all that is owed, for as long as it is owed

checks.question: Could the guarantor refuse or delay payment by raising the borrower's defences, a set-off or a dispute about the loan?
checks.assumption: The guarantor has given up the defences that would let it delay payment
checks.note: Read the waiver clause itself. A summary that says "unconditional" is not enough.

checks.question: Can the guarantee end or shrink before the loan is repaid (an expiry date, a release on a ratio or an event, a change to the loan made without the guarantor's consent)?
checks.assumption: The guarantee stays in force until the loan is repaid

checks.question: Does the guarantor receive a benefit of its own from the loan it guarantees, or has counsel confirmed that the guarantee cannot be set aside for lack of benefit to the guarantor or as financial assistance?
checks.assumption: The guarantee cannot be set aside for lack of benefit to the guarantor
checks.if_unknown: A guarantee that brings its giver no benefit may be challenged when it is called.
checks.note: Power and approvals are asked under Legal standing and Authorisation.

checks.question: Could the lender enforce a claim under the guarantee where the guarantor's assets are, and collect within about two years?
checks.assumption: A judgment or award against the guarantor can be enforced against its assets
checks.note: Two years is a guide. What counts is that the money arrives while it still matters.

checks.question: Is the guarantee signed by the guarantor and in force?
checks.assumption: The guarantee exists as a signed document

checks.question: Is the guarantee backed by something the lender can reach without going to court (cash collateral, a standby letter of credit, a pledge over the guarantor's assets)?
checks.assumption: Something the lender can reach directly stands behind the guarantee

indicators.title: The guarantor's capacity
indicators.claim: The guarantor can pay the guaranteed amount when it is called, and would not fail for the same reason as the borrower.

matters_more_when.reason: Without security the guarantor's means are the only second way out
A special-purpose borrower has nothing of its own to fall back on, so the guarantor carries the credit
Before the business earns anything, a call on the guarantee is more likely

look_again_when.reason: New accounts of the guarantor show its net worth, its debt and its guarantees at a new date
A new draft can change the amount the guarantor must be able to pay

checks.question: What kind of guarantor is this: a company, a natural person, a bank or insurer, or a government or public body?
checks.why: The kind of guarantor decides where its means are looked for: accounts for a company, a statement of net worth and title documents for a person, a rating for a bank or an insurer, a budget for a public body.

checks.question: What is the guarantor's net worth (all it owns less all it owes), leaving out its shares in the borrower and what the borrower owes it?
checks.why: The figure is read against the most the guarantor can be made to pay (OBS_GUARANTEE_CAP_001). The stake in the borrower is left out because it is worth least on the day the guarantee is called.
checks.ask: What do you own and what do you owe, in total, as of the latest date you have figures for? Please leave out your shares in the borrower and anything the borrower owes you.
checks.note: Give the date of the figure. For a person, use a signed statement of net worth and check the larger assets against title documents, registers or valuations.

checks.question: Could the guarantor pay the full guaranteed amount within 90 days of a demand, from cash, committed credit lines it has not drawn, and assets that are pledged to no one and could be sold in that time?
checks.assumption: The guarantor can find the guaranteed amount in cash within the time a demand gives it
checks.if_unknown: A guarantor whose wealth is in land, unlisted shares or the borrower itself can be worth the amount and still be unable to pay it.
checks.note: 90 days is a guide. Use the period the guarantee gives the guarantor to pay where that is shorter. Shares in the borrower and claims on the borrower do not count. Count the cash after the guarantor's own debt repayments, interest and taxes of the next twelve months, and after what could be called under its other guarantees at the same moment.

checks.question: Do the guarantees, sureties and other contingent liabilities that the guarantor has already given, added to this guarantee, come to more than its net worth?
checks.assumption: The guarantor's net worth covers all the guarantees it has given, this one included
checks.ask: Please list every guarantee you have given for someone else's debt, with the amount, the lender and the borrower.
checks.note: Count guarantees for group companies, for other borrowers and for the guarantor's owners, and capital it has promised but not yet paid in. Use the net worth given under OBS_GTOR_002. A person's guarantees appear in no accounts. Ask for a signed list and check it against a credit bureau report where there is one.

checks.question: Leaving out everything that comes from the borrower and the companies the borrower controls (dividends, fees, sales to them, loans to them and the value of the guarantor's shares in them), do the guarantor's income and net worth still cover the guaranteed amount?
checks.assumption: The guarantor's means to pay do not come from the borrower or from the companies the borrower controls
checks.why: A guarantee from someone who lives off the borrower adds a signature, not a second way out. The two would fail together.
checks.note: A guarantor in the same business and the same market as the borrower can fail with it even where the two have no dealings with each other. Where that is so, say it in the reason. Where the guarantor is the borrower's parent, the parent's other businesses count as its own.

leads_to.reason: A guarantor that would fail together with the borrower is not a second way out

checks.question: Do the guarantor's latest accounts (for a person: a list of assets with the register or account that shows each) show assets free of any pledge or charge to others that are worth at least the guaranteed amount?
checks.assumption: A creditor with a judgment against the guarantor would find assets to seize that are worth the guaranteed amount
checks.note: Whether a judgment can be enforced in the country where the assets are is asked about the guarantee (OBS_GUARANTEE_ENFORCE_001). This check asks whether there is anything there to enforce against. Where the guarantor is a holding company, its assets are shares in subsidiaries, and the subsidiaries' own lenders are paid first.

checks.question: When a guarantee given by the guarantor was called in the past, or a company it stood behind ran short of money, what did the guarantor do?
checks.assumption: The guarantor has never walked away from a guarantee or from a company it stood behind
checks.why: A guarantor that has fought or avoided a call before is likely to do so again. A guarantor that was never called has shown nothing either way, so that answer is recorded and does not count against it.
checks.ask: Have you ever been asked to pay under a guarantee, or to put money into a company you owned or backed when it was short? What happened?
checks.note: Ask the borrower's other lenders, and search court records and the press. If the search finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when.

checks.question: Are the assets that the guarantor has named as its means to pay held in the guarantor's own name alone, and not by a spouse, a relative, a trust, a foundation or a company?
checks.assumption: The assets the lender counts on belong to the guarantor in law
checks.note: Assets held jointly, or within a marriage in which property is shared, may be only partly within reach. Say which assets these are and take legal advice. Assets held through a company are reached only after that company's own creditors.

checks.question: What is the guarantor's credit rating from a rating agency?
checks.why: For a bank or an insurer, a rating says more about its ability to pay than its balance sheet does. Many lenders accept a guarantee only from a bank above a minimum rating. Each lender sets that minimum for itself.
checks.note: Record the agency, the rating, whether it is on the international or a national scale, and its date.

indicators.title: Key customer
indicators.claim: The customer will keep buying and paying until the loan is repaid, or the seller can sell the same volume to others.

matters_more_when.reason: The first way out rests on what this customer has signed
A project usually sells to one customer or to a few

look_again_when.reason: A new draft or an amendment can change the price, the volume, the term or the right to end the contract
A change in the customer's rating changes what its promise to pay is worth

checks.question: Does this customer bring in about a tenth or more of the seller's revenue, now or in the projections, or do the projections for repayment rest on its contract?
checks.why: Opens the topic. Below that size the loss of one customer is absorbed in the seller's revenue as a whole, which is tested under revenue and customers.
checks.ask: Does this customer buy about a tenth or more of what you sell, or will it once the project runs?
checks.note: A tenth is a guide. OBS_OFFTAKER_002 asks for the figure and does not hang on this answer.

checks.question: What share of the seller's revenue comes from this customer?
checks.why: The share says how much of the debt service is lost with the customer. It also checks the answer to OBS_OFFTAKER_001.
checks.ask: About what percentage of your revenue comes from this customer?
checks.note: Take the last full financial year. For a business that is not yet selling, take the share of projected revenue in the first full year of operation and say so.

checks.question: Does the customer buy under a signed contract that fixes a volume or a price for more than a year ahead?
checks.why: Decides whether the checks on the contract are asked. A customer that buys order by order is held only by its own interest, and then what counts is whether it can be replaced.

leads_to.reason: The contract is reviewed as a subject of its own

checks.question: What is the customer's credit standing?
checks.assumption: The customer's ability to pay is known, and it is not weak
checks.flag_when: is rated_B_or_below or unrated_weak or unknown
checks.why: A rating in the single-B range or below says that the agency itself sees a real chance of default within the life of a loan. Contracted revenue from such a customer is no more certain than revenue without a contract.
checks.ask: Does this customer have a credit rating, or can you share its latest audited accounts or a credit report on it?
checks.note: investment_grade means a rating of BBB- (or Baa3) or higher. rated_BB means the double-B range just below it. rated_B_or_below means single-B or lower. Choose unrated_strong where there is no rating but the customer's audited accounts show profits, cash and debt it can carry. Choose unrated_weak where they show losses, heavy debt or late payment. Choose unknown where neither a rating nor accounts have been seen. A government body without its own rating takes the rating of its state. A rating does not say that the customer pays on time. OBS_OFFTAKER_004 asks that. Give the agency, the rating and its date in the reason.

checks.question: Over the last twelve months, has the customer paid the seller within the agreed payment term or, where it has not yet bought from the seller, paid its other suppliers under comparable contracts on time?
checks.assumption: The customer pays on time
checks.ask: Does this customer pay your invoices when they fall due? Please share the ageing list of what it owes you.
checks.note: This check does not hang on OBS_OFFTAKER_001. Read the seller's ageing list of receivables and its bank statements. An invoice paid more than 30 days after it fell due counts as late. That is a guide. A strong rating does not replace a record of payment.

checks.question: If this customer stopped buying, could the seller sell the same volume to other buyers within about six months, at a price no more than about a tenth lower?
checks.assumption: The seller could place this volume with other buyers within a season, without a large cut in price
checks.ask: If this customer stopped buying tomorrow, who else would take the volume, how soon, and at what price?
checks.note: Six months and a tenth are guides. What counts is whether the seller could go on servicing its debt while it finds other buyers. Where there is one possible buyer by law or by geography (a single power buyer, the only processor within reach), the answer is no.

checks.question: In the last three years, has the customer cut the price it pays, lengthened its payment term, charged the seller rebates or fees that were not agreed, or dropped a product of the seller, without the seller's consent?
checks.assumption: The customer has kept to the prices and terms it agreed with the seller
checks.why: A large customer that buys without a long contract can use its weight through price cuts, rebates, longer payment terms and delisting. The checks on the contract do not show that.
checks.ask: In the last three years, has this customer cut its price, taken longer to pay, charged you rebates or fees you had not agreed, or dropped one of your products, without your consent?
checks.note: Set the agreed prices and terms beside what the customer in fact paid, and when, over the three years. The seller's price lists, credit notes and ageing list of receivables show it. A change that both sides negotiated and signed is not a yes. A seller that says yes is believed.

checks.question: If the customer ends the contract early, takes less than the agreed volume or pays late, does the contract oblige it to pay a stated amount (a termination payment, a take-or-pay or minimum payment, interest on late payment)?
checks.assumption: The contract makes the customer pay if it ends the contract early, takes less or pays late
checks.note: Set the termination payment against the debt that would then be outstanding, and say in the reason whether it covers it. Whether the lender can take over the seller's rights is asked about the contract itself (OBS_CONT_MIT_001).

checks.question: Are the customer's payments backed by something other than its own promise: a letter of credit or a bank guarantee, credit insurance, an escrow or collection account that the lender controls, or an assignment of the receivables to the lender?
checks.assumption: The customer's payments are backed by more than its own promise to pay
checks.note: Say which of these is in place. An assignment or a collection account sends the money to the lender. It does not make a customer pay that cannot.

indicators.title: Other lenders
indicators.claim: The other lender cannot take the party's cash or assets ahead of the lender, or call its loan and bring the party down, without the lender having a say.

matters_more_when.reason: The lender has agreed to rank behind, so what the senior lender may do decides what is left
Without security the lender stands behind every lender that holds some
Lenders to the operating companies are paid from their assets before a lender to their owner

look_again_when.reason: A new debt schedule can show a new loan, a new maturity or new security
A new draft can change the vote, the standstill or the order of payment
A new search can show a charge that was not there before

checks.question: Security aside, would the lender's claim be paid ahead of, beside or behind the other loan if the party became insolvent?
checks.assumption: The lender's claim is paid no later than the other loan
checks.why: A lender that ranks behind is paid only from what is left once the other loan is repaid in full. Ranking beside shares a loss in proportion, which is the usual place of a senior lender, so only 'behind' is flagged.
checks.ask: If the company could not pay everyone, who would be paid first: us, this other lender, or both side by side? Where is that written down?
checks.note: Count ranking by agreement (a subordination), by law, and by place in the group: a loan to the company that holds the assets is paid from them before a loan to its owner. Take the worst of the three. Security is asked about in OBS_LENDER_002. This indicator is for a loan that a party the lender counts on owes to someone else. A loan that such a party has made to someone else belongs to CAS_RELATED_PARTY_001.

checks.question: Does the other lender hold security over, or control of, anything the lender counts on: the assets offered to the lender as security, the assets that produce the cash, or the accounts the revenue is paid into?
checks.assumption: What the lender counts on is free of the other lender's security and control
checks.ask: What have you pledged or charged to this lender? Does it include the assets or the bank accounts that we would rely on?
checks.note: A right of set-off over accounts kept with the other lender counts as control. If the search finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when.

checks.question: Is the party free under the other loan agreement to take the lender's loan and to give the lender's security, either without asking or with a consent the other lender has given in writing?
checks.assumption: Taking the lender's loan and giving its security breaks no promise made to the other lender
checks.ask: Does your agreement with this lender limit new borrowing, or forbid you to give security to another lender? If it does, has the lender agreed in writing to our loan?
checks.if_unknown: The new loan may itself be a default under the other loan, which the other lender could then call.
checks.note: Read the other agreement itself for a limit on new debt and for a negative pledge (a promise not to give security to anyone else). The consent must come from the other lender. The party's own account of it is not a consent.

checks.question: Does the other loan fall due in a single payment, or come up for renewal, before the lender's loan is repaid, for an amount the party could not repay from one year's cash flow after its other debt service?
checks.assumption: The other loan can be repaid from cash flow as it falls due, without a refinancing, while the lender's loan is outstanding
checks.note: A line that runs for a year and is then renewed falls due at its next renewal date. A loan that is repaid in instalments from cash flow is a no.

leads_to.reason: The other loan is repaid or refinanced during the life of the lender's loan, so that payment has to be in the cash flow

checks.question: Can the other lender cancel its loan or demand repayment at any time without a default (an uncommitted line, an overdraft, a loan repayable on demand)?
checks.assumption: The other loan stays in place until its agreed maturity unless the party defaults
checks.ask: Is this line committed for a fixed period, or can the lender reduce it or ask for its money back whenever it chooses?

leads_to.reason: A line that can be withdrawn at will is not liquidity the party can count on

checks.question: Are the other loan's covenants tighter than the lender's own, so that they would be breached first (tighter levels, more frequent testing, or events of default that the lender's agreement lacks)?
checks.assumption: The other lender gets no default before the lender does
checks.note: Compare the same ratio on the same definitions. A looser level on a stricter definition can still be breached first.

leads_to.reason: The lender's covenants can be set so that they are breached no later than the other lender's

checks.question: Have the lenders agreed in writing that the other lender will not call its loan or enforce its security for a fixed period without the lender's consent (a standstill), and that the lender has a vote on enforcement?
checks.assumption: An agreement between the lenders gives the lender a vote and holds the other lender back for a fixed period
checks.note: A vote that the other lender can always outvote is not a say. Record the lender's share of the vote and what needs its consent. Until the agreement is signed, a term sheet agreed by both lenders is supporting evidence only.

checks.question: Has the other lender agreed in writing that no principal is repaid on its loan before the lender's loan is repaid in full, and that nothing at all is paid on it while the lender's loan is in default?
checks.assumption: The other lender has agreed in writing to be paid after the lender
checks.note: This is the usual answer for loans from shareholders and related parties. A bank will seldom agree to it. A subordination that is only promised in a term sheet, or only mentioned in the notes to the accounts, is not yet an agreement signed by the other lender.

indicators.title: Support between projects
indicators.claim: When the supported project falls short, cash from the supporting project must reach it, ahead of any payment to the owners.

matters_more_when.reason: A project whose cash flow is only projected is the more likely to need the support
Other financing is in place, and the supporting project's own lenders have the first claim on its cash

look_again_when.reason: A signed or amended facility agreement can change the order of payments and the triggers
An agreement between lenders decides whether cash may leave the supporting project

checks.question: Is the support set out in a signed agreement that binds the supporting project?
checks.assumption: The support is set out in a signed agreement that binds the supporting project
checks.ask: Where is the support between the projects written down? Please share the agreement, or the section of the facility agreement that sets out the order of payments.
checks.if_unknown: Support that is not written down is the sponsor's intention, not an obligation.
checks.note: A term sheet, a group policy or a practice of moving cash between projects is a no.

checks.question: What form does the support take?
checks.why: The form decides what moves between the projects. A sweep or a shared reserve moves cash. Cross-collateral gives a claim on assets. A cross-default moves no cash at all, and lets trouble in one project bring down the other.
checks.note: Choose every form that applies.

checks.question: Which events oblige the supporting project to pay?
checks.assumption: The agreement states the events that oblige the supporting project to pay
checks.why: Where the trigger is unclear, the supporting project or its owners decide whether the support is owed, and they decide at the moment it is needed.
checks.note: dscr_breach means the supported project's debt service cover ratio has fallen below a stated level. distribution_lockup means the supported project is barred from paying its owners. Choose unclear where the trigger is not defined or depends on someone's judgement. Unclear may be chosen together with other options.

checks.question: Once a trigger event has occurred, must the supporting project pay without a further decision by its board or its owners?
checks.assumption: The support is owed as soon as it is triggered, with no further decision
checks.note: Wording such as "may", "intends to" or "subject to approval" is a no.

checks.question: Where does the support come in the supporting project's order of payments (its cash waterfall)?
checks.assumption: The support is paid before the supporting project pays anything to its owners
checks.why: Support that comes after distributions is paid only from what the owners chose to leave behind. Before distributions it has a prior claim on the cash.
checks.note: The debt service meant in the options is the supporting project's own.

leads_to.reason: There is cash to pass on only if the supporting project has some left after its own debt service

checks.question: Can the supporting project pay the support without the consent of its own lenders (no bar on payments to affiliates, and no lock-up that would stop it)?
checks.assumption: The supporting project's own lenders cannot stop the support from being paid
checks.note: Read the supporting project's own loan documents, not only the agreement that grants the support. Where the supporting project has no debt of its own, the answer is yes. Record that.

leads_to.reason: The supporting project's lenders decide whether cash may leave it

checks.question: Which events end the support?
checks.assumption: The agreement states when the support ends
checks.why: Where the end of the support is unclear, the supporting project can claim it has been released once the supported project runs into trouble.
checks.note: dsra_funded means the supported project's debt service reserve account is filled. Any release before the supported loan is repaid leaves the rest of its life without the support. Record the event and any fixed end date.

checks.question: Do the supporting project and the supported project depend on the same customer, the same resource or the same tariff, so that one event would weaken both at once?
checks.assumption: The two projects would not be weakened by the same event
checks.note: Two plants that sell to the same buyer, draw on the same river or wind region, or are paid under the same tariff scheme fall short together. The support is then weakest when it is needed.

indicators.title: Related parties
indicators.claim: Dealings with related parties take no cash or value out of the party that the lender counts on.

matters_more_when.reason: A group gives more ways to move cash and value between companies
In distress, owners can move value out before the creditors reach it

look_again_when.reason: New accounts carry a new note on related parties and new balances
A restructuring moves businesses or assets between related parties

checks.question: Does the party buy from, sell to, lend to, borrow from, guarantee for or share costs with related parties (its shareholders, directors and managers, their families, and companies that any of them own or control)?
checks.why: Opens the topic. A "no" is not the end of it. OBS_RP_005 checks it against the audited accounts.
checks.ask: Does your company buy from, sell to, lend to or borrow from its shareholders, its directors, their families, or other companies that they own? A yes or no is enough to start with.

checks.question: What kinds of dealings does the party have with related parties?
checks.why: Each kind takes value out in its own way: sales below the market price, purchases above it, loans that are not repaid, guarantees that are called, fees for nothing, pay and advances beyond what the work is worth. Guarantees and security received take nothing out, but they show how far the party's borrowing rests on its owners' own means. Loans given open the checks on what is owed to the party.
checks.note: Choose every kind that applies. Choose guarantees_and_security_received where a shareholder, a director or a related company guarantees the party's debt or pledges its own assets for it, and record who gave what as a fact about the link that holds that debt. Choose pay_and_advances_to_insiders for salaries, bonuses and advances to shareholders, directors, managers and their families. A loan to a related company is loans_given. A guarantee that the party has given for a related party's debt needs no link: record for whom and how much in a fact. Its size is asked under OBS_DEBT_009.

leads_to.reason: A guarantee for a related party is a debt that the balance sheet may not show

checks.question: What is the total yearly value of the party's dealings with related parties (sales, purchases, fees, rents and interest), as a percentage of its revenue?
checks.why: Says how much of the business runs through related parties, and so how much hangs on the prices between them. A price set between related parties can be moved at will. Set too high, it takes cash out of the party. Set too low, it flatters the margin the lender counts on. Loans and balances are asked separately.
checks.ask: What is the total value of all your dealings with related parties in the last financial year, as a percentage of your revenue? The notes to your audited accounts should give the breakdown.
checks.note: Take the last full financial year and name it. Give purchases and payments also as a share of costs.

checks.question: Are the prices and terms of the party's dealings with related parties the same as it gets, or would get, from unrelated parties?
checks.assumption: Related parties get no better prices or terms from the party than strangers would
checks.ask: How are prices set for what you buy from and sell to related companies? Is there a transfer-pricing study, or can you show us what unrelated customers and suppliers pay for the same thing?
checks.if_unknown: Margins and cash flow may be flattered, or drained, by prices that the owners set.
checks.note: Compare with the party's own dealings with unrelated parties, with market prices, or with a transfer-pricing study. The party's statement that its terms are at arm's length is its own word.

checks.question: Must each dealing with a related party be approved by directors or shareholders who have no interest in it, under a written policy, the articles or a shareholder agreement?
checks.assumption: Those who gain from a dealing with a related party do not decide on it alone
checks.ask: Who approves a transaction with a related party? Is there a written rule that the director or shareholder concerned does not vote on it?

checks.question: What do related parties owe the party (loans, advances and trade receivables), as a percentage of its tangible equity?
checks.assumption: What related parties owe the party is a small part of the party's own capital
checks.why: Related parties are seldom pressed to pay, so analysts take what they owe off the party's equity. Above about a tenth of tangible equity, taking it off changes leverage and covenant headroom enough to be seen. A tenth is a reference point from credit practice, not a rule. A lender can set its own.
checks.ask: Please add up all loans, advances and receivables owed to you by related parties (group companies, associates, shareholders, directors). What is the total, and what is your equity?
checks.note: Tangible equity is equity less goodwill and other intangible assets. Give the date of the balance.

checks.question: What was the highest balance of loans and advances that related parties owed the party during the last financial year, as a multiple of the balance at the year-end?
checks.assumption: The year-end balance shows what related parties owe the party during the year
checks.why: The balance at year-end hides the peak. Loans to related parties are often repaid just before the balance-sheet date and drawn again after it. A peak half as high again as the year-end figure is taken as the sign of this. It is a guide, and a lender can set its own.
checks.ask: What was the highest amount that related parties owed you at any time in the last financial year, and what did they owe you at the year-end? Monthly balances would answer this.
checks.note: Some accounts disclose the highest balance in the year. Where they do not, ask for the monthly balances. Where nothing was owed at the year-end but money was owed during the year, the multiple cannot be worked out. Record 99 and give the peak amount in the reason.

checks.question: Can the party call back what it has lent to related parties, and could they pay?
checks.assumption: The party can get back what it has lent to related parties
checks.why: A right to demand repayment from a related party that has no cash, or a loan with nothing in writing, is money the party will not see when it needs it. Lenders treat such loans as capital given away.
checks.ask: Can you demand repayment of your loans to group companies, for example at 30 days' notice? If you did, would the company that borrowed have the cash to pay?
checks.if_unknown: The loans to related parties cannot be counted as assets that turn into cash.
checks.note: The options: demandable_and_liquid, repayable on demand and the related party has the cash or the credit lines to pay. demandable_illiquid_borrower, repayable on demand but the related party that borrowed could not pay. term_loan, a written loan with a repayment date. no_terms, nothing in writing. Where the loans differ, answer for the largest.

checks.question: Does the note on related parties in the audited accounts name every related party, dealing and balance that the party has told the lender about, or that the lender knows of from other sources?
checks.assumption: The audited accounts disclose all the party's dealings and balances with related parties
checks.note: This check does not hang on OBS_RP_001, so that the topic cannot close on one answer. Compare the note with the shareholder register, the organisation chart, the list of directors and the bank statements. Where the party said it has no dealings with related parties and the accounts show some, correct the answer to OBS_RP_001.

checks.question: In the last 24 months, has a business, a subsidiary or a plant been moved into or out of the party (through a sale to or a purchase from a related party, a merger, a demerger, a carve-out or a scheme of arrangement)?
checks.assumption: The party is still the business that its past accounts describe, with nothing moved into it or out of it
checks.why: A transfer between related parties can take a business or an asset out of the lender's reach, at a price that the owners set. It also breaks the trend, because the figures before and after the transfer describe different businesses.
checks.ask: In the last two years, has any plant, division or subsidiary been moved into or out of the company, for example through a scheme of arrangement, a carve-out, a demerger or a merger? If so, which periods are affected?
checks.if_unknown: The past figures may describe a business that is no longer the one the lender counts on.

leads_to.reason: Changes in the figures across the transfer need restated accounts before they are read as a trend

indicators.title: Key supplier
indicators.claim: The supplier will keep delivering until the loan is repaid, or the buyer can replace it before its own production stops.

matters_more_when.reason: A project usually has one supplier of its fuel, its feedstock or a key service
A crop that is not delivered cannot be made up before the next harvest

look_again_when.reason: A new draft or an amendment can change the volume, the price formula or the term

checks.question: What share of the buyer's need for this input does the supplier deliver?
checks.why: The share says how much of the buyer's production stops with the supplier.
checks.ask: How much of this input do you buy from this supplier, as a share of all you need?
checks.note: Take the last full financial year, by volume, or by value where volume is not recorded. Name the input in the reason.

checks.question: If this supplier stopped delivering, could the buyer get the same input in the volume it needs from other suppliers within three months, at a cost no more than about a tenth higher?
checks.assumption: The buyer could replace the supplier within a quarter, without a large rise in cost
checks.ask: If this supplier stopped delivering tomorrow, who else could supply you, how soon, and at what price?
checks.note: Three months and a tenth are guides. Count the time needed to approve a new supplier (tests, certification, a customer's sign-off) and to move the goods. A supplier that owns the only pipeline, grid connection, licence or technology cannot be replaced.

checks.question: In the last 24 months, has the supplier shown a sign that it may not keep delivering: a missed or short delivery to the buyer, a loss or a default in its own accounts, an insolvency or restructuring filing, or the loss of a licence it needs?
checks.assumption: The supplier is able to keep delivering
checks.note: Check the buyer's delivery records, the supplier's accounts or a credit report on it, the insolvency register and the press. If the search finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when.

checks.question: Does a signed contract oblige the supplier to deliver the volume the buyer needs, at a fixed price or under a price formula, until the final repayment date of the loan?
checks.assumption: The supplier is bound to deliver the volume the buyer needs, at an agreed price, until the loan is repaid
checks.why: Asked where the supplier cannot be replaced. Then the contract is all that holds it.

leads_to.reason: The contract is reviewed as a subject of its own

checks.question: Has the buyer paid the supplier in advance for more than about one month of deliveries (advances, deposits or loans), without a bank guarantee or other security for the money?
checks.assumption: The buyer's advances to the supplier are small or secured
checks.ask: Do you pay this supplier before it delivers? How much is outstanding with it at the highest point in the year, and is any of it covered by a bank guarantee?
checks.note: One month of deliveries is a guide. Advances to growers, deposits for equipment and goods of the buyer held at the supplier's site all count. Give the amount at its highest point in the year.

checks.question: What would keep the buyer supplied if this supplier stopped: stock of the input that lasts until a new supplier delivers, a second supplier that already delivers part of the need and is bound by contract to raise its deliveries, both, or neither?
checks.assumption: Stock or a second supplier would carry the buyer until the supplier is replaced
checks.why: Stock, and a second source that already delivers, buy the time it takes to replace a supplier. A second source that has only been named, and has never delivered, buys none.
checks.note: Give the stock in days of use, and the share of the need that the second supplier delivers today and is bound to deliver.

indicators.title: Support undertaking
indicators.claim: The undertaking binds its giver to do something definite that the lender itself can demand and enforce until the loan is repaid.

matters_more_when.reason: Without security the undertaking may be all that stands behind the borrower
A special-purpose borrower has only what its supporter is bound to put in

look_again_when.reason: A new draft or the signed undertaking can change what is promised and to whom
The opinion says whether the undertaking binds

checks.question: What does the giver of the undertaking promise to do?
checks.why: The promise decides what the lender could claim. A promise to keep its shares or to keep the company solvent gives, at best, a claim for damages. A promise to fund a named shortfall gives a claim for money. A letter that only says the giver knows of the loan, or states its policy, promises nothing.
checks.note: Answer from the wording of the document, not from its title. "Comfort letter", "letter of support" and "keepwell" are used for very different promises. Choose no_firm_promise where the letter states an intention or a policy only.

checks.question: Is the undertaking given to the lender, so that the lender can demand performance and sue the giver in its own name without going through the borrower?
checks.assumption: The lender itself can hold the giver to the undertaking
checks.note: An undertaking given only to the borrower, to its board or to its auditors leaves the claim with the borrower.

leads_to.reason: An undertaking that the lender cannot enforce is not a second way out

checks.question: Can the giver withdraw the undertaking, or does it lapse, before the loan is repaid (an end date, a right to give notice, an end when the giver sells its shares in the borrower)?
checks.assumption: The undertaking stays in force until the loan is repaid

checks.question: When the giver was asked in the past to do what an undertaking of this kind promised, for the borrower or for another company, what did it do?
checks.assumption: The giver has never walked away from an undertaking of this kind
checks.why: An undertaking is weaker than a guarantee, so the giver's record counts for more. A giver that was never asked has shown nothing either way, so that answer is recorded and does not count against it.
checks.note: Ask other lenders to the giver's group, and search court records and the press. If the search finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when.

checks.question: Does a legal opinion confirm that the undertaking binds the giver under the law that governs it, as a duty that a court would enforce and not as a statement of intent?
checks.assumption: The undertaking is a binding promise under the law that governs it
checks.if_unknown: Without an opinion the undertaking is counted as a statement of intent, and not as a second way out.

checks.question: Has the giver's board, or the body that its articles require, approved the giving of the undertaking?
checks.assumption: The giver has approved the undertaking as its own rules require
checks.if_unknown: An undertaking signed by a manager without approval can be disowned by the giver when it is relied on.

indicators.title: Authorisation
indicators.claim: Every approval the party needs for its part in this deal (from its board, its shareholders and any authority) has been given as its own rules and the law require, and those who sign have the power to bind it.

matters_more_when.reason: In a group, a guarantee or security for another member's debt often needs approvals beyond the board's
A supervised financial institution may need its supervisor's consent to borrow or to guarantee

look_again_when.reason: A new resolution can approve the transaction, or approve something other than what is being signed
A shareholders' resolution can give an approval that was missing
Amended articles can change who has to approve and who may sign
Counsel's opinion can confirm the approvals, or qualify them

checks.question: Has the party's board passed a resolution that approves its part in this transaction, the documents it will sign and the persons who sign them?
checks.assumption: The board has approved the transaction and named who signs
checks.ask: Has the board passed a resolution for this financing? Please share a certified copy, or say when the board will meet to pass it.
checks.note: The resolution has to fit this transaction (the lender, the amount, the documents). A general approval "to raise finance", or one for another amount, is not this resolution. For a party without a board (a natural person, a public body), ask for whatever approval takes its place and say what it is.

checks.question: Do the party's articles, as they stand today, allow its directors to commit it to this transaction at this amount, without exceeding any cap on borrowing, guarantees or security?
checks.assumption: The articles do not put this transaction beyond what the directors may commit the party to
checks.ask: Do the articles or a shareholders' agreement cap what the directors may borrow, guarantee or pledge without going to the shareholders? If so, what is the cap and how much of it is used?
checks.note: Where a cap is a multiple of capital and reserves, work it out on the latest accounts and count all the party's other borrowings. Where the shareholders have lifted a cap by resolution, answer yes and record the resolution under OBS_AUTH_008. Whether the party itself has the power to borrow or guarantee is asked under OBS_LEGAL_003.

checks.question: Do the articles, a shareholders' agreement or company law require the shareholders to approve this transaction, and if so, have they approved it?
checks.assumption: No approval by the shareholders is missing
checks.why: A transaction that needed the shareholders' approval and went ahead without it can be challenged by a shareholder, or by a liquidator, at the moment the lender relies on it.
checks.note: An answer of not_required should rest on counsel's reading of the articles, any shareholders' agreement and the law, not on the party's say-so. Typical cases that need approval are reserved matters, a transaction large against the party's assets, and a guarantee or security given for a shareholder or a related party.

checks.question: Does this transaction need an approval from, or a registration with, an authority (for example the central bank or an exchange-control or investment authority for a loan from abroad), and if so, is it in place?
checks.assumption: No approval or registration by an authority is missing
checks.why: Where such an approval or registration is required and missing, the borrower may be unable to buy and send the currency to repay, and the lender may be unable to enforce the loan.
checks.if_unknown: Ask counsel in the party's country early. An approval of this kind can take months and may have to be in place before the first drawing.
checks.note: An answer of not_required should rest on the advice of counsel in the party's country. This check is about approvals for the financing itself. Licences to run the business are looked at under licences and regulation.

checks.question: Are the persons who sign the documents authorised to bind the party for this amount, by the board resolution or a power of attorney, and within any signing limit?
checks.assumption: Those who sign have the power to bind the party for this amount
checks.note: Match the names and the signatures on the documents to the resolution or the power of attorney, and to the specimen signatures. Check that a power of attorney is still in force and covers this transaction. Ask for the party's signing rules (limits, joint signatures, list of signatories) and check against them.

checks.question: Has counsel given a legal opinion, on which the lender may rely, that the party has taken every corporate action needed to authorise the documents and that they are validly signed?
checks.assumption: Independent counsel has confirmed that the documents are duly authorised and validly signed
checks.note: Read the assumptions and the qualifications. An opinion that assumes the resolutions are valid has not confirmed them.

indicators.title: Conditions and follow-up
indicators.claim: Everything left open at approval is written down as a condition, a covenant or an agreed action, and each is met when it falls due, before the money moves or by its date after.

matters_more_when.reason: The money is drawn in stages while the project is built, and each drawing has conditions of its own
A business in distress changes fast between approval and disbursement

look_again_when.reason: A new checklist shows which conditions are met, waived or still open
The signed agreement fixes the conditions and the undertakings, and may differ from what was approved
A waived or deferred condition has to be followed until it is met

checks.question: Does every claim that is challenged or not tested at approval have against it a condition precedent, a covenant, or an agreed action with an owner and a date?
checks.assumption: Nothing is left open at approval without a condition, a covenant or an agreed action
checks.note: Start from the tool's own list of claims that are challenged or not tested. An open point that the approval paper mentions but ties to nothing counts as a no.

checks.question: Are the conditions precedent listed in the term sheet or the facility agreement, each worded so that a named document or a fact that can be looked up shows whether it is met?
checks.assumption: Each condition precedent can be checked against a document or a fact
checks.note: A condition such as "insurance in place" passes only if it names what has to be delivered (the policy, the broker's letter). One that says only "to the lender's satisfaction" does not pass.

checks.question: Since approval, has anything that the decision rested on changed: the latest figures of the parties that repayment relies on, their owners or managers, the structure of the deal, a licence or a contract, or the terms as documented against the terms approved?
checks.assumption: Nothing that the approval rested on has changed since it was given
checks.note: Ask at signing and again before each disbursement. If the review finds nothing, record what was looked at and when (the latest accounts, the registry, the press, the signed terms against the approved terms).

checks.question: Before each disbursement so far, was every condition for it met, or waived or deferred in writing, with the document that shows it on file?
checks.assumption: No money moved while a condition was neither met nor formally let go

checks.question: Has any condition precedent been waived, or deferred to a date after disbursement?
checks.assumption: No condition precedent was waived or deferred
checks.note: Record which condition, why it was let go, and what it was there to protect.

checks.question: Do payment records show that the money drawn so far was spent on the purposes named in the facility agreement?
checks.assumption: The money was used for the agreed purpose
checks.ask: Please show how the money drawn so far was spent, with the invoices and the proof of payment for the larger items.
checks.note: The borrower's own certificate of use is its word. Trace the larger payments to invoices and bank statements, or rely on an engineer's or auditor's report that did.

checks.question: Have all accounts, compliance certificates and other reports that fell due under the facility agreement in the last twelve months arrived complete and by their due dates?
checks.assumption: The borrower reports in full and on time
checks.note: Compare the date each report was received with the date it was due. Late figures are often the first sign that the figures are bad.

checks.question: Is every agreed action whose date has passed (a condition deferred to after disbursement, an action plan item, an undertaking with a date) complete?
checks.assumption: Agreed actions are completed by their dates
checks.ask: Which of the agreed actions are complete, which are late, and what shows it for each?
checks.note: Complete means that the thing itself is there (the registered charge, the permit, the policy), not that work on it has started.

checks.question: Was the waiver, the deferral or the change approved at the level that the lender's rules require for it, and does whatever it leaves open have an owner and a date?
checks.assumption: The waiver, deferral or change was approved at the level the lender's rules require, and what it leaves open has an owner and a date
checks.note: For a change to what was approved, that is usually the level that approved the loan. An officer's own decision to let a condition go is not an approval.

indicators.title: Covenants
indicators.claim: The covenants warn the lender while there is still time to act, give it the right to act, and keep cash and assets from leaving the borrower before it does.

matters_more_when.reason: Without security the covenants are the lender's only hold on the borrower
In a group, cash and assets can move to members that the covenants do not reach
Other lenders have covenants of their own, and theirs may be breached first

look_again_when.reason: A new draft can change the covenants or their levels
The signed agreement can differ from the term sheet, most often in definitions, exceptions and cure rights
New cases move the room between the covenant levels and the figures

checks.question: Which financial covenants does the facility carry?
checks.why: Opens the topic. A covenant on cash flow against debt service warns earlier than one on the balance sheet. An answer of none is picked up by OBS_COV_004.

checks.question: As results fall from the lender's base case towards the point where cash flow no longer covers debt service, when is a financial covenant first breached?
checks.assumption: A financial covenant is breached while the debt is still being serviced, and none is breached in the base case
checks.why: A covenant that the base case already breaches will be waived until it means nothing. One that is breached only once cash no longer covers debt service, or not at all, tells the lender what it already knows. The level belongs between the two.
checks.if_unknown: If no downside case has been run against the covenant levels, nobody knows when they would warn.
checks.note: Run the lender's downside case with the covenant's own definitions. It shows how far results have to fall before the first breach, and how many test periods lie between the breach and the first period in which cash flow no longer covers debt service. Record the room between each level and the base case.

checks.question: Are the financial covenants tested on the accounts of every party that repayment relies on (consolidated where it relies on a group), and not only on the borrower's own accounts?
checks.assumption: The covenants are measured where the cash flow that repays the loan is earned
checks.note: Read the definitions. A covenant tested on a holding company's own accounts says nothing about the subsidiary that earns the cash, and the other way round. Where there is no financial covenant, leave this open. OBS_COV_004 records it.

checks.question: Do the terms of the facility oblige the borrower to deliver audited annual accounts, interim accounts and a compliance certificate that shows the covenant calculations, each by a stated date?
checks.assumption: The lender is entitled to the figures it needs to test the covenants, by fixed dates
checks.ask: Which accounts and reports would you have to send the lender, how often, and how long after the period ends? Can the finance team meet those dates today?

checks.question: Do the terms of the facility forbid the borrower to give security to anyone else (a negative pledge) and limit the new debt it may take on, with every exception capped at a stated amount?
checks.assumption: No other creditor can take security or add debt ahead of the lender without the lender's consent
checks.note: Read the exceptions (permitted security, permitted debt). An exception without a cap undoes the rule. Where repayment relies on a group, the limits should bind the group's members too.

leads_to.reason: Nothing stops another lender from ranking ahead

checks.question: Do the terms of the facility make dividends and other payments to the owners, sales of assets, and loans or guarantees to related parties subject to the lender's consent or to a stated test?
checks.assumption: Cash and assets cannot leave the borrower for its owners or related parties unless the lender agrees or a stated test is met
checks.note: All three have to be covered for a yes. Repayments of shareholder loans and fees paid to the owners count as payments to the owners.

leads_to.reason: Money can reach related parties without the lender knowing

checks.question: Does a breach of a financial covenant give the lender the right to stop further drawings and to demand repayment, once any stated cure period has run out?
checks.assumption: A covenant breach gives the lender the right to act
checks.note: A breach that only blocks dividends, or only obliges the borrower to present a plan, does not give this right. Record the length of the cure period.

checks.question: Can the owners cure a breach of a financial covenant with new money without a limit on how often, or in test periods that follow one another?
checks.assumption: The owners cannot cover up repeated breaches with new money
checks.note: Where the facility gives no right to cure with new money, the answer is no. Also read how the new money is counted. Money counted as cash flow hides the breach. Money used to repay debt reduces it.

checks.question: Do the terms of the facility give the lender the right to demand repayment if control of the borrower passes to someone else without its consent, or if a guarantor or sponsor that the lender relies on ceases to own the borrower?
checks.assumption: The lender can leave if the owners it lent to are replaced
checks.note: Read how control is defined. A sale of shares higher up the chain of ownership should count as a change of control too. A clause that only obliges the borrower to tell the lender of the change does not give this right.

checks.question: Does a default under another loan of the borrower, or of a party that repayment relies on, give the lender the right to call its own loan at once (a cross-default clause)?
checks.assumption: When another lender can call its loan, the lender can call its own
checks.note: A clause that gives the right only once the other lender has in fact called its loan (cross-acceleration) leaves the lender one step behind. Answer no and say which clause it is. This check takes the place of OBS_LENDER_007, which asked the same of each other loan in turn.

checks.question: Does the compliance certificate for the latest test date show every financial covenant within its limit?
checks.assumption: The borrower is within its financial covenants at the latest test date
checks.if_unknown: A certificate that has not arrived is itself a breach of the information covenant. OBS_COND_007 records it.
checks.note: Work the ratios out again from the accounts that came with the certificate, using the definitions in the facility agreement.

indicators.title: Legal standing
indicators.claim: The party exists in law, is in good standing, is not in insolvency proceedings, and has the power to take on what it signs in this deal.

matters_more_when.reason: A business in distress is the one most likely to face a creditor's petition or to have let its filings lapse
A company set up for the deal has no record to show that it exists and is kept in order

look_again_when.reason: A new extract shows the party's standing at a new date
Amended articles can widen or narrow what the party may do
Counsel's opinion can confirm the party's existence and powers, or qualify them

checks.question: Is the party incorporated and registered as a legal person?
checks.assumption: The party exists in law and can be held to what it signs
checks.ask: Under which name, number and country is the company registered? Please share the certificate of incorporation or a recent extract from the registry.
checks.note: Check that the name and the registration number are those of the party that will sign, not of a sister company with a similar name. For a natural person an official identity document takes the place of the registration. For a public body it is the law or decree that set it up.

checks.question: Is the party in insolvency proceedings, administration, receivership or a court-supervised restructuring, or is a petition to wind it up pending?
checks.assumption: The party is not in insolvency proceedings and no petition to wind it up is pending
checks.ask: Has the company, or any creditor, filed for its insolvency, administration or winding-up, or for a restructuring under the court's protection?
checks.note: Search the company registry, the insolvency or court register and the press. If the search finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when. This check does not hang on OBS_LEGAL_001.

leads_to.reason: A petition is a claim in court, and it is seldom the only one
Proceedings follow from debts that were not paid

checks.question: Does the company registry show the party in good standing: annual returns filed, fees paid, and no notice of striking off or dissolution?
checks.assumption: The party is in good standing with the registry and is not about to be struck off
checks.ask: Are all annual returns filed and all registry fees paid? A recent certificate of good standing or registry extract would show it.
checks.note: Record the date of the extract. Standing can lapse between diligence and signing, so a fresh extract is usual before the documents are signed.

leads_to.reason: A lapse that is not cured by approval has to become a condition precedent

checks.question: Do the party's constitutional documents give it the power to do its part in this deal (to borrow, to guarantee another party's debt, or to give security)?
checks.assumption: The party has the power to take on the obligations it signs
checks.ask: Do the company's articles allow it to borrow, to give guarantees and to give security? Please share the current articles with all amendments.
checks.if_unknown: An obligation that the party had no power to take on can be challenged when the lender comes to rely on it.
checks.note: Read the objects and the powers in the current articles, with all amendments. For a guarantor, look for the power to answer for someone else's debt, not only to borrow. Limits on what the directors may approve are asked under OBS_AUTH_004.

indicators.title: Asset given as security
indicators.claim: The asset belongs to the one who gives it as security, would fetch the value counted on in a forced sale, and can be taken and sold by the lender.

matters_more_when.reason: The whole second way out rests on this one asset
The asset may have to be taken and sold soon

look_again_when.reason: A new valuation changes the value counted on
A new search can show a charge that was not there before
Cover is renewed each year and can lapse or change

checks.question: What kind of asset is it?
checks.why: The kind of asset decides what proves ownership, where a charge is registered, how the asset is valued and whether it can be insured.
checks.note: The kinds are those of OBS_SECPKG_001. 'contract_rights' covers an assignment of a contract, of a concession or of insurance proceeds.

checks.question: Does a title document or a public register show the one who gives the security as the owner of the asset?
checks.assumption: The asset belongs to the one who gives it as security
checks.ask: In whose name is this asset held? Could you send the title deed, the register extract or the other document that shows it?
checks.note: For shares, the share register. For cash, an account in the giver's own name. For receivables, invoices issued by the giver. Land held under a lease, a concession or a right of use is not owned: answer no and say what the giver holds. Whatever the answer, the owner belongs in the structure.

checks.question: Has someone independent of the borrower and of the one who gives the security valued the asset within the last twelve months?
checks.assumption: The value counted on rests on a recent valuation by someone independent
checks.ask: When was this asset last valued, by whom, and who asked for the valuation?
checks.note: Twelve months is a guide. Stock, receivables and listed shares change faster and need a fresher figure. For cash, the bank's own confirmation of the balance counts. For stock and receivables, a count or an ageing list checked by someone independent counts. A book value is not a valuation.

checks.question: What would the asset fetch in a forced sale, after the costs of the sale and after any claim that ranks ahead of the lender?
checks.why: This is the figure the security package is measured with (OBS_SECPKG_006). The market value and the book value are both higher and neither is what a lender receives.
checks.note: If the valuer gives no forced-sale value, say what discount was taken from the market value and why. Say how long a sale is assumed to take.

checks.question: Have assets of this kind been sold in this country in the last three years to buyers outside the business that used them, at prices that bear out the forced-sale value counted on?
checks.assumption: There are buyers for the asset outside the business, and past sales bear out the value counted on
checks.note: Three years is a guide. Record the sales relied on: what was sold, when, and at what price. Typical cases for a no: a plant built for one purpose or in a remote place, stock that only this business can use, receivables that customers stop paying once supply ends, shares in the borrower itself. Cash on deposit is not sold: leave the check unanswered and record that decision with its reason.

checks.question: Does the title document or a search of the registers show any charge, lien, lease, attachment or other claim on the asset besides the lender's own?
checks.assumption: The asset is free of any claim but the lender's
checks.ask: Has anyone else a charge, a lien or a lease on this asset, or a claim to it in court? Is any part of its purchase price still owed to the seller?
checks.note: Search the register that belongs to the kind of asset (land, vehicles, movable assets, company charges) and the courts. If the search finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when.

leads_to.reason: Where the holder of the claim is another lender, its rights are examined there

checks.question: Does a rule or a contract stop the lender or its security agent from holding security over the asset, or from selling it to a buyer of its choice (a limit on foreign ownership of land, a licence or concession that does not pass to a buyer, a consent not yet given)?
checks.assumption: The lender or its agent may hold security over the asset and sell it to whoever pays most
checks.note: The question is about this asset and this lender. Obstacles that hold for every kind of security in the country are asked about in CAS_SECURITY_LEGAL_001.

checks.question: Can the lender take and sell the asset without first obtaining a court judgment (a private sale, taking the asset in payment, or a power of sale given in the security agreement)?
checks.assumption: The lender can sell the asset without waiting for a court
checks.note: Record also how long a sale would take from the day of default, with or without a court. The forced-sale value in OBS_SECASSET_004 assumes that time.

checks.question: Is the lender's security over the asset registered, or otherwise made effective against other creditors, at first rank?
checks.assumption: The lender holds first-ranking security over the asset that is effective against other creditors
checks.note: A filing receipt shows that registration was asked for. The extract shows that it was made, and at what rank. Where there is no register (a notice to the debtor, control of an account), counsel's confirmation takes the place of the extract.

checks.question: Is the asset insured against loss and damage for at least its replacement value, and is the lender named on the policy as the one to whom a claim is paid (loss payee)?
checks.assumption: If the asset is lost or destroyed, the insurance money is enough to replace it and is paid to the lender
checks.note: If only one of the two holds, answer no and say which. An endorsement on the policy, or a notice that the insurer has acknowledged, shows that the lender is loss payee: a clause in the loan agreement that asks for it does not. Bare land has nothing to insure: leave the check unanswered and record that decision with its reason.

leads_to.reason: The party's insurance as a whole is examined there

indicators.title: Security in law
indicators.claim: The security can be created, registered and enforced under the law that governs it, and lenders have done so in practice.

matters_more_when.reason: The lender's place as a secured lender holds only if the security holds in law
Security over a whole business is made of several kinds of charge, and each must hold

look_again_when.reason: A new or final opinion can add a qualification
A new draft can change what is created and under which law

checks.question: Under the law that governs it, can each kind of security in the package be validly created in favour of the lender or its security agent?
checks.assumption: Each kind of security in the package can be validly created in favour of the lender
checks.note: Go through the package kind by kind: a charge over future assets, over a changing pool of stock or receivables, over a bank account, security held by an agent for several lenders, security given by someone other than the borrower. One kind that fails makes the answer no: say which.

checks.question: Can the lender or its counsel name cases in the country where the assets are in which a lender enforced security of this kind through to a sale and received the proceeds?
