checks.assumption: Lenders have in practice enforced this kind of security in the country where the assets are, and been paid
checks.note: A law that allows enforcement is not proof that it happens. Record the cases, how long each took and what share of the debt was recovered. If the search finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when.

checks.question: Do searches against each one who gives security show a charge over all its assets, a lien that arises by law (unpaid taxes or wages) or a court attachment that would rank ahead of the package?
checks.assumption: No earlier charge, lien or attachment over the giver's assets as a whole ranks ahead of the package
checks.ask: Is there any charge over all the company's assets, any unpaid tax or wage claim, or any court order against its assets? A search of the company's charges register would confirm it.
checks.note: This check is about the package as a whole and is searched against the giver. Claims on one asset are searched for under CAS_SECURITY_ASSET_001. If the search finds nothing, record what was searched, where and when.

checks.question: Can each kind of security in the package be registered, or otherwise made to hold against other creditors and against a liquidator?
checks.assumption: The security can be registered, and then holds against other creditors and in an insolvency
checks.note: Record the register, the time limit for filing and the cost. Stamp duty and registry fees can be a real share of the loan, and a filing made late can lose its rank. Say which kind fails if the answer is no.

checks.question: If the borrower defaults or becomes insolvent, does the law put other claims ahead of the lender's security (unpaid wages, taxes, the costs of the insolvency), suspend enforcement with no fixed end, or stop a foreign lender from enforcing or from taking the proceeds out of the country?
checks.assumption: On default the lender can enforce the security and take the proceeds, with no claim put ahead of it by law
checks.if_unknown: The forced-sale values assume an enforcement that nobody has checked can happen.
checks.note: Say which obstacle it is and which assets it touches. What stands in the way of one asset only is asked about under CAS_SECURITY_ASSET_001.

leads_to.reason: Where the obstacle is a limit on taking money out of the country, it is a transfer risk and is examined there

checks.question: Has counsel signed a legal opinion which confirms that the security is validly created, holds against other creditors and can be enforced, and which leaves out none of the assets the lender counts on?
checks.assumption: A signed legal opinion confirms the whole security package
checks.note: Read the assumptions and the qualifications, not only the opinion paragraph. An opinion still in draft has not been given: answer no until it is signed.

checks.question: Does the lender hold security that can be enforced outside the country and under another law (a pledge over shares in a holding company abroad, or over accounts abroad into which the revenue is paid)?
checks.assumption: Part of the security can be enforced outside the country, under another law
checks.note: A pledge over shares abroad gives control of the company, not of its assets. Say what the lender could in fact do with it.

indicators.title: Security package
indicators.claim: If the first way out fails, a forced sale of the security would repay what the lender is then owed under the facility.

matters_more_when.reason: The lender's place as a secured lender is worth only what the security would fetch
The first way out is a forecast, so more weight falls on the second
The security may have to be used, and soon

look_again_when.reason: A new valuation changes what a forced sale would repay
A new draft can add or take out an asset, or change the rank
A change in the amount or the security changes the cover

checks.question: What is offered as security for the facility?
checks.why: Opens the topic. Each kind that is offered must appear in the structure as an asset that secures the facility, and each such asset is then examined on its own.
checks.ask: What could you offer as security for this loan? For example land and buildings, equipment, receivables, stock, shares, cash on deposit, or your rights under contracts. A list with rough values is enough to start with.
checks.note: Choose every kind that is offered. 'contract_rights' covers an assignment of contracts, of a concession or of insurance proceeds. Choose 'none' only on its own, and only where the loan is to be unsecured. While the security is not settled, leave this question open, and the checks on the security wait for it.

checks.question: What is the most the lender can be owed under the facility: the full amount committed, plus interest that is capitalised or can run unpaid, at its highest point?
checks.why: The security and any guarantee are measured against this figure, not against the amount drawn today.
checks.note: Say in which currency, and whether a grace period or capitalised interest lifts the figure above the amount committed.

checks.question: Can the payments due under the main contracts, or from the main customers, be assigned to the lender and paid into an account the lender controls?
checks.assumption: The revenue that repays the loan can be assigned to the lender and collected in an account it controls
checks.ask: Could the payments from your main customers be made into an account that we control? Does any of your contracts forbid assigning its payments, or need the customer's consent?
checks.note: Look for a clause that forbids assignment or needs the customer's consent, and ask whether the customers would follow a payment instruction.

checks.question: Is any of the security shared with other creditors, or does the lender rank behind another creditor on any of it?
checks.assumption: The lender holds the security at first rank and for itself alone
checks.note: Security held by an agent for several lenders is shared. Say with whom, and in what proportion.

leads_to.reason: Whoever shares the security or ranks ahead on it decides, with the lender or before it, when and how it is sold

checks.question: Does the security cover the assets the business cannot run without (the plant, the site, the main contracts, the accounts the revenue is paid into)?
checks.assumption: The security covers the assets that produce the cash, not only assets the business can do without
checks.why: A lender that holds only spare assets has no hold on the business. Whoever holds the assets it runs on decides what happens to it.

checks.question: What would the security fetch in a forced sale, as a percentage of the most the lender can be owed under the facility?
checks.assumption: A forced sale of the security would repay what the lender is owed
checks.why: Below 100 percent a forced sale leaves part of the loan unpaid, and that part rests on a guarantee or on nothing. Many lenders ask for more than 100 percent, to allow for the cost and the time of a sale and for falling prices. An institution can set its own level.
checks.note: Add up the forced-sale value of each asset (OBS_SECASSET_004), after the costs of sale and after claims that rank ahead. Where security is shared, count only the lender's share. Do not count guarantees. Divide by the figure in OBS_FACILITY_EXPOSURE_001. Where no security is offered, the answer is zero.

checks.question: Does a guarantee, or another promise to pay by someone other than the borrower (a standby letter of credit, credit insurance), cover within its own limit the part of the loan that a forced sale of the security would not repay?
checks.assumption: A guarantee or another promise to pay covers what the security would not repay
checks.note: Compare the cap of the guarantee with the shortfall in money, not in words.

leads_to.reason: That part of the loan then rests on the guarantee, which is tested on its own link

indicators.title: Terms
indicators.claim: The loan's tenor and repayment schedule fit the cash flow that repays it.

matters_more_when.reason: No cash comes in until the project is built and running, so the grace period and the first instalments carry the whole schedule
Terms fitted to a forecast fit only as well as the forecast holds

look_again_when.reason: A new draft can change the amount, the tenor or the schedule
The signed agreement can differ from the term sheet that was approved
A new model moves the cash flow the terms were fitted to

checks.question: How far have the terms of the facility got on paper: proposed by one side, agreed in a term sheet or heads of terms, or signed?
checks.why: Opens the topic. The tests below are tests of terms that are written down. While none are, leave this question open, and the tests wait for it.
checks.ask: Is there a term sheet or heads of terms that you and the lender have both accepted? Please share the latest version and say whether it is signed.
checks.note: There is no answer for "none yet". An open question says that, and it is listed as the thing to do. Where the terms are only proposed, the answers to the tests below should say so.

checks.question: Does the term sheet state the amount, the currency, the tenor, the grace period, the repayment schedule, the interest rate and the fees, with none of them left open?
checks.assumption: The main terms are written down and none is still to be agreed
checks.note: A term marked "to be agreed", or a range in place of a figure, counts as left open.

checks.question: Set against a month-by-month cash flow, does any repayment fall due before the cash to pay it has come in (during a ramp-up, or ahead of the season's sales)?
checks.assumption: Each repayment falls due after the cash that pays it has come in
checks.ask: In which months does your cash come in, and when would the first repayment fall? If the loan pays for an investment, when will that investment start to earn?
checks.note: A yearly cash flow hides this. Use a monthly or quarterly one for the grace period, the ramp-up and one full season. For a project under construction, the first repayment is set against completion under OBS_ECON_007.

checks.question: Does repayment in full depend on a refinancing or a sale at maturity: a bullet, or a final instalment larger than the cash flow of its year can pay?
checks.assumption: The loan is repaid in full from cash flow by its final maturity, without a refinancing or a sale
checks.note: A working-capital line that is repaid in full from each trading cycle does not depend on a refinancing. One that is only ever rolled over does.

leads_to.reason: The cash flow and the value at maturity have to be strong enough for another lender to take the loan over

checks.question: Are the proposed tenor, grace period and repayment profile within what lenders have agreed for comparable loans in this sector and country?
checks.why: Terms more generous than any precedent need a reason that belongs to this deal. Comparable means the same sector, the same country or region and the same kind of borrower.
checks.if_unknown: Where no comparable loan is known, the terms have no outside reference. The credit paper should say so.

checks.question: Does the price of the loan (margin and fees together) meet the return the lender requires for a credit of this risk, tenor and rank?
checks.why: A price below the lender's own requirement means the risk is carried for less than it costs. This is the lender's judgement of its own loan, not a test of the borrower.

checks.question: Do the loan terms require the borrower to use surplus cash to prepay this loan (a cash sweep), so that the final payment shrinks in the years the business does well?
checks.assumption: Surplus cash reduces the debt that would have to be refinanced
checks.note: Check what counts as surplus cash, and whether dividends are paid before the sweep or after it.
